 Sonam Kapoor has been the quintessential poster girl for the Indian brides, long before she was even married. She can thank her association with the Indian Gems and Jewellery industry, she has always set trends, in terms of bridal lehengas, jewellery, makeup etc. I saw her once during my Mumbai to Delhi flight a few years back. Even then, she was flaunting a beautiful Indian ensemble. She is charming and well mannered. It was one of the few occasions that I got to see a celeb at the airport, in spite of staying for more than a decade in the city. I was hoping to meet more celebs during my flight to Mumbai but that never happened. So coming back to Sonam Kapoor, she was recently seen in Delhi as a showstopper for an established jewellery brand. And I am absolutely floored by her poise in that heavy purple lehenga by the designer Jayanti Reddy. She has been styled by celebrity stylist Tanya Ghavri. She looked elegant while walking the ramp while husband Anand Ahuja cheered her during the fashion show. She looks like a queen in this traditonal jewellery inspired by the history of Delhi; the collection aptly named as Delhi Durbar, by Bhirdichand Ghanshyamdas. Use of pastel coloured gemstones is the USP of this collection.    In fact, during her marriage to business man Anand Ahuja, she looked fabulous in her bridal avatar.  Her makeup never overpowers her delicate features. But her ensemble and jewellery is always on top of everything. Here are a few more pics for inspiration from her wedding. So all the brides-to-be, take a cue from Sonam Kapoor and plan your D day with much style and grandeur.  Sonam Kapoor was recently seen in Veere Di Wedding and will be soon seen in The Zoya Factor and Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga.  What do you think about her style sense? Do leave a comment below. Sonam Kapoor always arrives in style in Cannes. Everyone is talking about her beautiful pale pink Elie Saab gown. Not only her ensemble but her jewellery has turned heads in the fashion world as well. She wore Victorian era inspired dark romance jewellery designed by sister Rhea Kapoor and Kalyan Jewellers at the ‘The Meyerowtiz Stories’ screening during the 70th annual Cannes Film Festival.  Look at these beauties! This stone-studded, rose-gold collection can only be termed as wearable art. 12 artisans worked for 35 days to create these. Her glittering, customized accessories included dramatic haat phools and lightweight shoulder duster earrings.  To match the shade of pink used in the gown, Rhea Kapoor worked closely with Kalyan Jewellers and chose Tourmaline – an exquisite gemstone. This was paired with brilliantly sparkling polished diamonds, strings of fresh water pearls and muted Polki diamonds all set in a rose gold base with just the right hint of white gold. At 5.23 inches, the 18 carat shoulder duster earrings surprisingly weigh just 60.43 grams. The haat phools have a more elaborate design with multiple pearl strands connecting daintily from the finger to the bracelet, and the pair weighs 171.09 grams. Commenting on the design Rhea Kapoor said, “For Sonam’s Cannes appearance this year, I wanted jewellery that would go with the intricate embroidery and the high-shine embellishment of Elie Saab’s design, but at the same time, I wanted something that was inspired by Dark Romance. It was a memorable experience working with Kalyan Jewellers to create this look. We combined the traditional Indian technique of studded jewellery making with a design linage that is essentially very European. Our aim was to create pieces of wearable art that blends the best of 18th century dark romance designs with Indian idioms.”  Recently, the Kapoor sisters also launched their fashion line Rheson which is available at Shoppers Stop. These girls are definitely the game changers in the Indian fashion scene. Rajesh Kalyanaraman, Executive Director, Kalyan Jewellers added, “It was a challenging proposition for us, when Rhea suggested blending Victorian dark romance inspired design ideas with Indian kaarigari. But today, we are extremely proud that we could render the designs with precision. The jewellery complemented Sonam Kapoor perfectly, and the most important aspect of this design is that they are lightweight and can be easily paired with an Indian or a more global ensemble.” I just loved what she wore at Cannes. What do you guys think? Denims never go out of season. From winters to summers, there are a variety of ways you can sport chic looks with denim. You might be the tomboy or the ultra femme fatale, denim will always make way into your wardrobe. But are you aware of the latest denim trends in the market? If not, Mumbaigloss will help you to figure it out with the help of fashion brand ONLY and let you shop for your sartorial needs. FRAYED DENIMS: This season the focus of denims has moved all the way down with raw, unfinished edges, frayed hems, decorative laces that enhance your summer look giving it a casual yet edgy feel. Unleash the denimized babe in you by pairing your open-hemmed skinny boyfriend jeans or scalloped hemmed short shorts with an off-shoulder top!  PATCHES AND FLOWERS: Market is flooded with garments with patches of appliques. Denims have bitten this trend bug too. You might find patch work starting from jackets, to pants, dungarees, shorts and spice them up with floral motifs, goofy doodles, detailed embroideries that add the much needed quirkiness to your ensemble!  BETTER FROM THE BACK: Tops, shirt dresses, distressed jackets with statement graphics, messaging and embroidered designs at the back make sure that you always make a statement.  DENIM SPORT – ATHLEISURE: There is always a denim for every hour of the day. Denims can give us stylish outfits for a lazy Sunday brunch, a date night, casual Fridays at work and now the athleisure laid-back weekend vibe. Looks ranging from sporty bomber jackets, jogger pants with washed out tones and distress effects have made lazing in denim easier than ever!  DENIMIZED RUFFLES: Frills, ruffled sleeves, bleached cold shoulder dresses, denim jackets with an Ombre effect and distressed jeans have been spotted on every global fashionista’s wardrobe. Sport a ruffled top with slightly sliced high waisted skinny denims and get ready to effortlessly take the world by storm!  LACED UP: Lace and denims are two things that every girl swears by. What if we told you that, this season you can surprise your loved one with both at one go? Up your denim game with lace detailed denim crop tops, stringy laced denim dresses or high waisted pants with lace running up to your ankles. Will you be at the top of this lace race? As summers are approaching, white and off white dresses will take centre stage again. Fashionistas take a cue and bring them out of your closet.       Do you know how did the name Maldives came into existence? Well, it is derived from Sanskrit words Maala and Dwipu that means ‘Garland of Islands’. There are 26 islands in the shape of a necklace. Maldives islands are slowly drowning due to climate change. May be after a decade those islands will be submerged under water. Unless we take care of our environment, these gems of the ocean might disappear permanently from the face of earth. Well, this photoshoot is also to bring awareness towards this issue. I was a Sari is a brand which debuted at Lakme Fashion Week during Summer Resort 2017. I was a Sari is a lifestyle brand offering a unique and premium line of up-cycled fashion products made from beautiful Indian saris. This isn’t the first in its segment as handbags from Holii started their business by incorporating Indian saris and motifs into their designs years ago. So what makes this brand different? Well, it is its simplicity. The designs are basic but versatile. They not only make dresses, tops, shoes, jewellery but also reusable bags, stoles, scarfs and a variety of other fashion accessories. Sustainable fashion is the way forward and I was very happy to see their collection.  This made me think how can we make our saris useful which have not seen the light of the day for very long. I scouted a few celebrity images and found that we can convert our unused saris into dresses and accessories with a bit of imagination and the art of tailoring. ( Only catch is to find a good tailor) Inspiration one: Look at how effortlessly Juhi Chawla has gone glam with Indian fabric and motifs in this dress. The golden zari work looks amazing against the green fabric. She wore it at the Anita Dongre show, Lakme Fashion Week Grand Finale. I think any of our Benarasi saris lying unused can be modified into a dress similar to this floor length kurta dress.  Inspiration two: Convert any of your silk sarees into a chic summer dress like this one from I was a Sari. If you have extra fabric left, then create matching accessories like bags, fabric bead jewellery, scarf, etc. Gorgeous, isn’t it? Inspiration three: If you have georgette embellished sarees that you wore last at your wedding and have’t touched them in a while then convert them into evening dresses like this dress worn by Sangeeta Bijlani. Sangeeta wore this dress at the Lakme Fashion Week Grand Finale by Anita Dongre show. Perfect for an evening soiree.  Inspiration four: Not too keen on the entire dress? Then go for jazzy evening wear top made from an elaborate Sari pallu. Look how Gul Panag teamed up a cream top with black cigarette pants and high heels. Impressive!  Inspiration five: A silk blouse with a benarasi skirt can spell modern chic in the most pronounced way. Look at Padma Lakshmi wearing a Tarun Tahiliani ensemble. Use any embellished or zari work sari to make a long skirt which you can team up with a plain shirt for fresh a look at a sangeet or mehendi ceremony. I was a Sari is a brand which debuted at Lakme Fashion Week during Summer Resort 2017. I was a Sari is a lifestyle brand offering a unique and premium line of up-cycled fashion products made from beautiful Indian saris. This isn’t the first in its segment as handbags from Holii started their business by incorporating Indian saris and motifs into their designs years ago. So what makes this brand different? Well, it is its simplicity. The designs are basic but versatile. They not only make dresses, tops, shoes, jewellery but also reusable bags, stoles, scarfs and a variety of other fashion accessories. Sustainable fashion is the way forward and I was very happy to see their collection.  This made me think how can we make our saris useful which have not seen the light of the day for very long. I scouted a few celebrity images and found that we can convert our unused saris into dresses and accessories with a bit of imagination and the art of tailoring. ( Only catch is to find a good tailor) Inspiration one: Look at how effortlessly Juhi Chawla has gone glam with Indian fabric and motifs in this dress. The golden zari work looks amazing against the green fabric. She wore it at the Anita Dongre show, Lakme Fashion Week Grand Finale. I think any of our Benarasi saris lying unused can be modified into a dress similar to this floor length kurta dress.  Inspiration two: Convert any of your silk sarees into a chic summer dress like this one from I was a Sari. If you have extra fabric left, then create matching accessories like bags, fabric bead jewellery, scarf, etc. Gorgeous, isn’t it? Lakme Fashion Week Summer Resort 2017 saw a couple of firsts this season. 1.The event was low key compared to previous seasons as it moved its venue from five star hotels to Jio Garden in BKC (a first in its history) and kept it simple with only the fashion fraternity and limited media. This may be a big relief for the organisers as mostly buyers and journalists thronged the bays and guests were kept to minimum. 2.For the first time ever stunning Padma Lakshmi, model and cookbook author walked the ramp in Lakme Fashion Week for designer Tarun Tahiliani.  3. Lakme Fashion Week became gender neutral by including transgender model Anjali Lama from Nepal in the model pool. Gender-neutral model Petr Nitka from Czech Republic who has walked numerous international runways was also part of the Lakme Fashion Week for the first time. With more and more designers going for androgynous silhouettes, it makes sense to hire people from various orientations and built. Mr. Jaspreet Chandok, Head- Fashion, IMG Reliance Ltd said, “With the aim of evolving mindsets and creating a more inclusive conversation around fashion, we have opened our runway to diverse and unconventional models and are curating some path-breaking shows that will further highlight our commitment to continue the conversation on inclusivity which we started last season. As a leading voice in Fashion, IMG Reliance hopes to continuously drive the industry into conversations around inclusivity which we feel will only enhance the business of fashion in the years to come.” 4. Lakme Fashion Week opening show was on a cruise ship called Costa neoClassica which sails between Mumbai and Maldives, for designer Monisha Jaisingh.  It was a luxurious affair with customised robes for the models, shirtless sailors strutting the ramp and on the house champagne for the guests. Lakme Fashion Week is evolving with each season, trying to get something new with every show. Let’s see what new strategies will they include next time for the fashion savvy audience. Sushmita Sen recently walked the ramp for Hyderabad based fashion designer Sashi Vangapalli on the final day at the  Lakme Fashion Week Summer Resort 2017. And her spontaneous twirl and fun at the ramp proved that she is the queen of the ramp.  Last, she was seen walking the ramp in Manila at the Miss Universe 2016 pageant and she set it ablaze with her sheer presence. She won the Miss Universe title 23 years back. Since then she has come a long way as a Bollywood actor but never left the fashion world. She never ceases to surprize me with her grit and stamina as she is one of the fittest mothers in Bollywood who have crossed 40. Sushmita Sen is one of the coveted showstoppers for the fashion weeks.  This time she held all her fans spellbound with her easy going diva vibe.  Her lavender gown had structured, embellished peplum bodice with crafted sleeves and a cascading asymmetrical trail which looked edgy and elegant at the same time. The silver and gold tone embellishments on the gown had motifs derived from the Bidri Art form. The Bidri Art Form, which originated in the town of Bidar is a mix of the Persian, Arabic and Turkish art forms, to make the Bidri ware. The intricacy and beauty of the Bidri art form was an influential aspect for the vibrant collection presented by Sashi Vangapalli for her label ‘Mugdha Art Studio’ during Lakmé Fashion Week, Summer/Resort 2017.  Sushmita wore minimum accessory in the form of metal hand cuffs with the gown. She used subdued makeup. Even though the pastel colour of the gown was feminine but the over all look was fierce and modern. The gown looked flirty and even better on the former beauty queen.  I am looking forward to Sushmita’s next appearance on the ramp. Let’s see what’s up her sleeve this time. I am looking forward to Sushmita’s next appearance on the ramp. Let’s see what’s up her sleeve this time. Winters are knocking at our door and it is time to pull out our winter wear. Yes, the bulky jackets, pullovers, turtlenecks, woollen caps, shrugs, etc. I know many of you are cringing at the very thought of wearing these items. But dear fashionistas, a girl needs to fight the chill as well, right? With stylish winter wear currently available in the market, it’s not that bad as it seems, trust me! A decade ago Indian fashion embraced parkas, overcoats, warm shrugs, beanies and a lot other fashionable accessories to keep us warm so there is no dearth of warm winter wear items that can make us look like leading ladies from Kjo movies. Well, he has come a long way since he made Kajol wear a skimpy red dress in powdery swiss snow for DDLJ (Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge). The latest flick from Karan Johar had Aishwarya and Anushka rock the most stylish winter wear while roaming the streets of Vienna. So let’s take a cue from them and list a few select pieces which can bring out the diva in us this winter. 1. Biker/Bomber leather jacket: The bohemian style of Anushka was well complimented with long kurta, leather bomber jacket, kohled eyes, ethnic silver jhumkas, boots with black quilted bomber jacket. Her care free spirit came out on-screen effortlessly. She defied rules so her look can be pulled off by all rebels at heart women. In the past Kareena Kapoor had also sported boots with kurta and ethnic jewellery for the movie Gabbar is Back. If you are one of those people who like to create their own style without blindly following fashion then this look is for you. 2. Overcoats/Parkas: Aishwarya’s impeccable, sophisticated and ultra-stylish look is ageless in the movie Ae Dil Hai Mushkil. Those long floor length parkas and furry overcoats are a staple to every stylish woman in the world. Teamed with high heeled boots her parkas projected a confident, beautiful woman who knows what she wants. Smokey eyes added to the intrigue. This look is for women who are professionals and mature in their outlook. I loved her look in the movie. https://www.instagram.com/p/BMBkLI6DUwQ/ 3. Shrugs/Sweater: Cover up in style with shrugs and sweaters for women available at various stores in your vicinity. Be it Sarojini Nagar market, online stores like Myntra or highstreet fashion brands like Only, Vero Moda, Desigual, etc. you will find your stylish sweaters for women here. Don’t frown as these could help you fight light to moderate chill in the air as well as help you layer efficiently so that you can control the exposure to low temperatures with ease. First put on soft comfy top, try to put a cardigan over it and on top you can go for shrugs and warm stoles or scarves. The idea is to layer clothes so that you can control your body temperature as per the outside temperature. https://www.instagram.com/p/BMeWNBijWWP/ 4. Scarves/stoles: Infinity scarves are trending as well as warm stoles are getting popular in the areas that do not see extreme shift in temperatures. Mumbai is one of those cities which doesn’t see much change in temperature. The climate remains moderate throughout the year. December and January seem pleasantly cooler than other months. That is when stoles and scarves come handy to beat the early morning chill. Pop colour scarves are in this season. Look how effortlessly chic Anushka is looking in this scarf. 5. Boots: Boots!!! Do I need to say more? Wear them with anything and everything. Period! They look cool, they are warm and comfortable. What else does a girl need? See how Anushka has paired them with leather look tights and winter coat.  6. Caps/ Beanies: There are ample of options in this segment. From flowery, crocheted, girly headgears to tomboyish leather look caps. I wore one last year while on my Eurotrip. Check it out here. It is very important to keep your head warm in protective caps during extreme winters.    7. Gloves: I love the sleek leather ones which has a faux fur lining inside it. Those are soft, warm, water proof and stay forever. Recently, I bought a pair for Rs. 600 at Dharavi Leather market and those look amazing. Did I miss out on something? Do let me know. Till then stay stylish and happy this winter. Winters are knocking at our door and it is time to pull out our winter wear. But dear fashionistas, a girl needs to fight the chill as well, right? With stylish winter wear currently available in the market, it’s not that bad as it seems, trust me! A decade ago Indian fashion embraced parkas, overcoats, warm shrugs, beanies and a lot other fashionable accessories to keep us warm so there is no dearth of warm winter wear items that can make us look like leading ladies from Kjo movies. Well, he has come a long way since he made Kajol wear a skimpy red dress in powdery swiss snow for DDLJ (Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge). The latest flick from Karan Johar had Aishwarya and Anushka rock the most stylish winter wear while roaming the streets of Vienna. So let’s take a cue from them and list a few select pieces which can bring out the diva in us this winter. 1. Biker/Bomber leather jacket: The bohemian style of Anushka was well complimented with long kurta, leather bomber jacket, kohled eyes, ethnic silver jhumkas, boots with black quilted bomber jacket. Her care free spirit came out on-screen effortlessly. She defied rules so her look can be pulled off by all rebels at heart women. In the past Kareena Kapoor had also sported boots with kurta and ethnic jewellery for the movie Gabbar is Back. If you are one of those people who like to create their own style without blindly following fashion then this look is for you. 2. Overcoats/Parkas: Aishwarya’s impeccable, sophisticated and ultra-stylish look is ageless in the movie Ae Dil Hai Mushkil. Those long floor length parkas and furry overcoats are a staple to every stylish woman in the world. Teamed with high heeled boots her parkas projected a confident, beautiful woman who knows what she wants. Smokey eyes added to the intrigue. This look is for women who are professionals and mature in their outlook. I loved her look in the movie. https://www.instagram.com/p/BMBkLI6DUwQ/ 3. Shrugs/Sweater: Cover up in style with shrugs and sweaters for women available at various stores in your vicinity. Be it Sarojini Nagar market, online stores like Myntra or highstreet fashion brands like Only, Vero Moda, Desigual, etc. you will find your stylish sweaters for women here. Don’t frown as these could help you fight light to moderate chill in the air as well as help you layer efficiently so that you can control the exposure to low temperatures with ease. First put on soft comfy top, try to put a cardigan over it and on top you can go for shrugs and warm stoles or scarves. The idea is to layer clothes so that you can control your body temperature as per the outside temperature. https://www.instagram.com/p/BMeWNBijWWP/ 4. Scarves/stoles: Infinity scarves are trending as well as warm stoles are getting popular in the areas that do not see extreme shift in temperatures. Mumbai is one of those cities which doesn’t see much change in temperature. The climate remains moderate throughout the year. December and January seem pleasantly cooler than other months. That is when stoles and scarves come handy to beat the early morning chill. Pop colour scarves are in this season. Look how effortlessly chic Anushka is looking in this scarf. 5. Boots: Boots!!! Do I need to say more? Wear them with anything and everything. Period! They look cool, they are warm and comfortable. What else does a girl need? See how Anushka has paired them with leather look tights and winter coat.  6. Caps/ Beanies: There are ample of options in this segment. From flowery, crocheted, girly headgears to tomboyish leather look caps. I wore one last year while on my Eurotrip. Check it out here. It is very important to keep your head warm in protective caps during extreme winters.    7. Gloves: I love the sleek leather ones which has a faux fur lining inside it. Those are soft, warm, water proof and stay forever. Recently, I bought a pair for Rs. 600 at Dharavi Leather market and those look amazing. Did I miss out on something? Do let me know. Till then stay stylish and happy this winter. Lakme Fashion Week Autumn/Winter 2016 showcased India’s first ever plus size fashion show in association with the brand ‘aLL’. Keeping up with the international pulse of celebrating all types of bodies, Indian fashion industry took a big leap when they decided to go ahead with a plus size clothing fashion show and handpicked 10 plus size models through rigorous auditions. Let’s be honest, most of us have gained enough mass around the midriff to rejoice such an effort. But when the show went live, many overweight people felt disappointed, rather threatened with the idea of fashion for plus size, the way it was presented during the show. The models were presented like hip-hop artists wearing chains, hoodies, leather jackets, hoops, studded B-boy caps, beanies, chunky belts and ankle-high sports shoes. The show was curated by Little Shilpa and she wanted to show the fun and carefree side of the generally underrated size category by styling them like the back street hip-hop stars performing with their high voltage confidence.  Underrated size category, definitely agreed, but low in confidence is rather far fetched assumption for plus size people. I have seen many overweight men and women carry themselves with elan and with much style and confidence than others. The very assumption that they never show their carefree and  confident style is a dent in the idea of promoting plus size clothing in the Indian fashion industry. College going plus size men and women are already dressing in the so called hip-hop fashion. So this fashion show was nothing exclusive. Nothing Lakme Fashion Week worthy! Though, it did help launch careers of the 10 chosen plus size models or may be add to their CV value. But as an audience, or a plus size fashion consumer, there was very little for us to take back home. There was no inspiration, no enthusiasm.  In the brand aLL’s defense, I would say that they cater to casual wear for the plus size consumer and cannot procure couture pieces for the show. They would showcase whatever they have to offer off their shelf. But as an audience, may be we were expecting more. We were expecting sexy silhouettes, curvy embellished gowns, flowing ensembles, just like the other brands who strutted on the fashion week runway this season for the so called normal sized people. This show left the plus size consumer high and dry. Can we have plus size fashion in India which is Ashley Graham worthy?  Hoping to see other plus size brands showcase the best they have in bridal wear, ethnic wear, handlooms and couture in the plus size category. But why create a separate show all together? I think other brands should showcase one or two plus size pieces in each collection they present during the fashion show. Include size 16 (UK) and above in your collection if you want to reach larger market in India. What do you guys think? How is the plus size fashion market in India? Kareena Kapoor Khan looked resplendent in a Sabyasachi ensemble during the Lakme Fashion Week Autumn/Winter 2016 closing show. She was cheered on by her family during the show, especially by sister Karishma Kapoor. Her pregnancy glow definitely illuminated the collection, which is also called ‘Illuminate’ by Sabyasachi. She is the second pregnant showstopper in the history of Lakme Fashion Week. Last season model Carol Gracias started this trend.  The Grand finale show was at the mega Mehboob studios. The added bonus was the performance by the Symphony Orchestra of India. The show was grand and the designs spelt grandeur. Sabyasachi Mukherjee’s designs have been loved and admired for the way they celebrate India’s rich heritage through exceptional handloom and craftsmanship. The collection included sportswear, a first from Sabya, along with lush fabrics weaved into salwar suits, kurtas and sarees all infusing a striking shimmer twist. I also saw bejeweled micro mini dresses that are perfect for the upcoming festive and cocktail season. The muted autumn colours ruled the collection. “Being at Lakmé Fashion Week always feels like a beautiful walk down memory lane, given this is where I made my debut in fashion! It’s an honour to be the Grand Finale designer once again and working with an inspiring brand like Lakmé. I have thoroughly enjoyed creating this collection inspired by the ‘Illuminate’ statement”, said Sabyasachi. Kareena was thrilled to be a part of this show. She added, “I love his designs and wear them often, and his creations for the illuminate collection are simply fabulous. Lakmé and Sabyasachi are the ultimate combination to have on a runway and I am glad to be a part of this!” The entire collection was breathtakingly beautiful. Brides to be can take a cue from the designs showcased in this collection as it included both traditional drapes as well as modern take on our heritage. Loved it! Ideal for a modern day princess look. What do you guys think about this collection? Do leave a comment below. Rohit Khandelwal is representing India in Mr. World 2016 pageant to be held at Southport, UK on July 19. In the 9th edition of Mr. World, contestants from 42 countries will participate and compete to win the crown. At the pageant, Rohit will be seen competing for various sub-contests at the pageant to get him closer to the title like Mr. World Multimedia Award, Mr. World Talent, Mr. World Sports Event, Mr. World Fashion & Model Award, Mr. World Extreme Sports and Mobstar People’s Choice Awards.  “I am very excited and thrilled to represent India at the Mr. World pageant. I am going to give it my best shot at winning the title and encouraging the youth of today to believe in themselves.” Said Rohit. Coming from a conservative family in Hyderabad, Rohit has worked hard to reach this far. The endless running, multiple reps, healthy eating, the pain, the sweat – he gave it his all. After all, it is not easy being chosen as Mr. India World 2015 amongst the fittest and smartest men in the country. Rohit has got the opportunity to be trained and mentored by some of the leading experts from the industry like Nivedita Saboo, Surabhi Sharma, Sabeera Merchant, Supreet Bedi, Jamuna Pai, Dr.Sandesh Mayekar, Swaroop Medara, Rukshana Eisa and many more. He will be seen in a Tuxedo, exclusively designed by Nivedita Saboo for his final round. Hope you make India proud Rohit. Textile day at LFW Spring Summer 2016 saw Gaurang present his latest collection Calico to the fashion enthusiasts and it certainly was eye catching. Indian fabric like Jamdani was presented in western wear and international silhouettes. Vintage styles have been repeated which looks fresh from the regular fashion. The colours, the golden borders that you see in a saari were beautifully designed into evening wear gowns. Saaris were also presented in unusual drapes.  Calico is homage to the traditional textile from the 11th century. The collection is a juxtapose of traditional Jamdani weaving tailored to silhouettes from the royal India in 1920s. Each ensemble is woven in the signature Jamdani weaving technique that takes 8-10 months to weave.  Gaurang has used various textures in Khadi like Muga, Tussar , Dupion , Silk to create these dresses. The theme being the Tree of Life. Calico is a manifestation of the Jamdani weave in an international flavour.  Moreover, I was impressed to see a pregnant Carol Gracias on the ramp. The designer has broken the taboo that expecting mothers cannot work in the modeling industry. She looked elegant and did justice to her job. More power to such initiatives.  Talking about his latest collection, Gaurang says, “Calico is iconic weaves and techniques in all their unfettered glory. Calico emphasizes the rich and vibrant history of Indian craftsmanship while championing the Indian woman of today.”  “Each ensemble from this collection is crafted from exquisite handwoven textiles in Khadi, Uppada and Kota using the Jamdani technique,” said the designer. Declared an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO, the Jamdani is a singularly striking weave that has created an impact across the centuries. The patterns are woven with a non-structural weft resulting in vibrant patterns that dance across the fabric. I am glad that the Hyderbad based designer is using Indian weaving techniques like Jamdani and Chikankari to promote our artisans and create value for our designs. What do you feel about this collection? Holi is just a day away. Mumbaigloss spoke to senior stylist Najeeb Ur Rahman, from Schwarzkopf India to give us hair care tips Pre and post Holi celebrations. After all, who would want to mess up their beautiful mane. Here is what he had to say: PRE-HOLI PREPARATION PREPARATION WHILE PLAYING HOLI Avoid toxic colors – Once you are in the Holi battlefield there is not much that you can do to guard your lovely locks. However, what you can do is, go for organic colors and avoid playing with chemical dyes or metallic colors. They can be toxic for your hair. POST-HOLI TREATMENT Rinse comes first – Once you are back from your Holi extravaganza, do not reach out for your bottle of shampoo, immediately. First rinse your hair with plain water, profusely. This will wash away the visible dry colors. Follow through a mild shampoo and a subsequent Treatment. It is advisable to complete the process with a conditioner. In case of any colour residue, do not wash it again on the same day as it may make your tresses dry. Don’t stress over your tresses. Play a safe holi. Happy Holi! Holi is just a day away. I have been asked many a times how my complexion glows all the time? To this, I have always answered that a good BB Cream and eyebrow definer does the trick. Of course, a beautiful lip gloss and mascara add to the over-all clean look. More about this later. I have been using Ponds White Beauty BB Cream for a while now and it has been my favorite for the past year or may be more. In fact, once I pitted it against Garnier BB Cream where Garnier miserably failed.  But recently, I discovered another gem in the market and I have been using it for a month now. It is called LOreal Paris True Match BB Cream in the shade Gold. Both the creams are mid-range. LOreal Paris True Match BB Cream 50 gm costs Rs. 500 at Amazon.in and Ponds White Beauty BB Cream 50 gm costs Rs. 297 at Amazon.in. The best part about both the creams is that they easily blend with your skin. I have a medium to fair complexion and combination skin. These two creams perfectly blend with my skin, giving me medium to natural looking coverage.  Moreover, LOreal Paris True Match BB Cream has Hyaluronic Acid that helps in reducing the appearance of fine lines and creases. Ideal for mature skin. This is what I needed post 35. Hyaluronic acid is a major component of skin, where it is involved in tissue repair. Both the creams feel hydrating and not cakey like Lakme CC Cream. Ponds White Beauty BB Cream though settles in the fine lines under the eyes over a period of time but LOreal Paris True Match BB Cream makes the skin look supple and smooth throughout the day.  LOreal Paris True Match BB Cream comes in three shades – Ivory, Honey and Gold. Ivory is for cool skin tone, Honey is for neutral skin tone and Gold is for warm skin tone. Whereas Ponds White Beauty BB Cream comes in just one shade and adapts to the skin complexion instantly. For darker skin tones, Ponds BB Cream is not an ideal choice. Coverage is better in Ponds BB Cream, but LOreal BB Cream gives a more luminescent satin finish. On a hot summer day, LOreal feels lighter on the skin than Ponds. My skin perspires under Ponds BB Cream in the summer. But nevertheless it doesn’t fade out.  Of course, there are better BB Creams in the market like MAC’s Prep + Prime BB Beauty Balm SPF 50 and Bobbi Brown BB Cream SPF 35. But then you pay a premium for these products. I feel it is not necessary to spend a bomb when you can get a good deal in the mid-range products for everyday use. But this is my personal opinion. I like to be frugal when it comes to cosmetics and use only those products where I am completely convinced irrespective of the brand.  What do you all think of this review? Do leave a comment below. Platinum and diamond jewellery was a favourite among the A Listers at the Oscars 2016. Do you know why? Platinum is the ideal choice for red carpet jewelry because it holds diamonds and precious gemstones more securely than any other metal. It is not only the highest quality metal, but its density makes it one of the most durable and enduring precious metals. Platinum is also naturally white, unlike white gold, which means it will not cast any tint onto a diamond or gemstone, allowing the stone’s genuine color to sparkle brightly. From Charlize Theron’s plunging diamond pendant to Lady Gaga’s statement diamond drop earrings, the world watched as celebrities sparkled in naturally white platinum jewellery at the 88th Annual Academy Awards. In fact our own desi girl Priyanka Chopra wore a beautiful diamond and platinum earring for the occasion. Priyanka wore a Lorraine Schwartz Platinum and diamond front back earrings and finger rings to go with her angelic Zuhair Murad gown. Her simple makeup added to her overall elegant look.  Lady Gaga wore Lorraine Schwartz Platinum And diamond earrings to go with her white jumpsuit by Brandon Maxwell. Her $8 million worth of jewellery shined bright with her blonde hair colour styled in vintage waves. Charlize Theron’s deep plunging neckline in her red Dior gown was complimented by Platinum Secret Cluster necklace with diamonds by Harry Winston. It was accompanied by cluster earrings, cushion cut diamond ring with micropave, and queen ring with diamonds. No doubts, the lady sparkled her way through the event. Cate Blanchett wore Platinum earrings with marquise and round diamonds by Tiffany & Co. It looked elegant with her baby blue Armani Prive gown. Her understated hairstyle and minimal makeup let her jewellery and ensemble shine through the occasion. Jennifer Garner wore Platinum and diamond bracelets by Neil Lane along with swirl drop earrings with diamonds and emerald, emerald cut baguette diamond ring and other finger rings to go with her black sequined by Atelier Versace gown. She looked so glamorous! There were several other celebs like Kerry Washington, Reese Weatherspoon and others who rocked the platinum and diamond jewellery to go make a statement at the Oscars!  Eyebrow filler and definer You can use the extreme right lower line dark eye-shadow shade to fill and define your eyebrows. Do we have a Laith Ashley in India? – A transgender model who will enchant you with his hot body and looks to die for. Check his Instagram account here. He was born a girl. The most hyped Caitlyn Jenner aka Bruce Jenner transformation has already taken the year 2015 by storm. Carmen Carrera was voted to walk with the Victoria’s Secret Angels last year as the first transgender angel in the fashion show. Not many know that she was born as Christopher Roman. But are we ready for transgender models and professionals in India yet? Every morning I cross a junction where a transgender woman (Hijra) asks for money from the commuters waiting at the traffic signal. She used to ask me money in the beginning and I used to give her a very rude look. I somehow feel that by giving alms to the beggars we are encouraging an unhealthy environment. Crimes related to children and women are rooted into begging. I would rather buy a packet of agarbatti or a balloon from the not so fortunate but never encourage begging by giving money. Many a times, I offer food to the beggars. Two vada pavs may cost Rs. 20 but it fills up a hungry stomach. I am more than ready to do that. But I have seen beggars refusing to take food and instead ask for money. I feel pretty unhappy with this behavior. So I avoid to entertain beggars at all cost. Coming back to this transgender woman, who I am very sure, knows me by face now and every time I see her coming towards my car, either I look away or make a nasty face so that she doesn’t ask money from me. Worst is when she starts banging hard on the car’s glass window as if threatening ‘either you give money or I will break the window’. Over a period of time, she has stopped coming to my car. I feel relieved. But then the question arises, why a healthy human being like her is forced to beg. Yes, we are humans first and a gender later. She wears some great sarees, applies bindi and lipstick then why doesn’t she earn money by doing some business or a job? This is a valid question and might absolutely support my stance. But when I did some reality check, I realized that may be that transgender woman has no other option but to beg. India recognized the third gender in 2014. In many official forms you will find the mention of a third segment below Male and Female. But has the transgender community come at par with the others after this ‘on paper’ recognition? May be not. I was reading about an incident where a transgender woman wanted to start a tea stall and run her own business. No one knows if she was able to fulfill her dreams. First of all in India, we still look down upon transgender people. Not many will be ready to consume food or tea prepared by a transgender woman due to several reasons including religion. And in case, she is able to run a business, she will be subjected to a lot of humiliation, harassment and bullying. May be she will be violated and abused physically and mentally, for trying to lead a normal life, like every one of us. In India, the minute a family realizes that a child is born with intersexual characteristics or over a period of time they realize that the child has transsexual bent, they quietly hand over the child to the hijra community. This is specifically true for the rural and small town low income families as they believe that they will not be able to support or protect the little one with special tendencies. How unfortunate is the child who is given away to an unknown group where he/she is raised without proper education, nutrition and safe environment. Transsexual people are never allowed to be a part of the main stream. They are never offered an opportunity to get formal education or to get regular jobs. Often they are subjected to violence, discrimination, sexual assault and forced to either beg or to take up prostitution. Most of them contract AIDS or other deadly diseases which leads to their untimely and painful death. So in this light of ambiguous identity of the transgender people in our society, are we ready to feature a transgender model for our popular brands alongside Khans and Kareenas? I remember two incidences from my growing up years that show how insensitive we are in terms of transgender community, their needs and their rights. And this insensitivity is engraved in our childhood. An effeminate boy in my class was always harassed by a group of the so called manly boys. He was beaten up so badly once in high school where they tore his shirt, blew dust on his face and hair, and he had cuts and bruises all over his face. He cried a lot. He was traumatized, physically and emotionally. He didn’t know why he was subjected to this harsh treatment. He couldn’t understand why other boys pounced on him just because he was a little different than them. Apparently, the boyish boys were trying to fix him up as they deemed his condition to be abnormal. These were school boys who were conditioned by our society to look down upon people who did not fall into the normal category. They were conditioned to behave in a certain manner and made to believe that anybody who belonged to their gender and behaved abnormally should be outcasted, beaten and bullied. Boys like these, carry this idea of discrimination throughout their adulthood and are never able to accept or respect the third gender. Another incidence is when I was in my early twenties and a boy used to come to office with full make-up on. Yes, he loved his mascara, lipsticks, nail polish, kajal and everything feminine. He used to dress up like men but could never let go off the makeup. People used to think he is weird, including me. He was a pretty boy who didn’t have many friends. I had seen him cry a few times alone in the cafeteria. People used to laugh at him and the managers used to talk to him harshly. He was made to feel unwanted on many instances. One day, he decided to wear a skirt and use the women’s toilet. That was the breaking point. He was relieved from his service immediately. He was educated, belonged to a decent family but his fault was that he felt like a woman trapped in a male body. I know, we Indians are not sensitized to deal with such incidents in our home and work environment. But that day I felt that it was unnecessary, it was unfair and unjustified to sack him from work. May be the office could have been more sensitive towards his condition and helped him understand the consequences before firing him. I don’t know where he is today. May be he would have made a great transgender model! Rudrani Chettri, a transgender activist from Delhi and the head of the MITR Trust, is launching India’s first Transgender Model Agency – run by transgender people, for transgender people – and they need our help to make this a reality. MITR attempts to give an opportunity to beautiful, talented and young TGs to get respectable, mainstream work and showcase their talent. To realize this dream, Chettri has taken an unconventional route of crowd funding through BitGiving to fund her project. Chettri has been working for more than 10 years in spreading awareness and fighting to improve TG’s lives in India. Her trust helps over 1500 TG in Delhi alone. They have also teamed up with eminent fashion stylist and photographer, Rishi Raj who will work towards getting a spread in a leading fashion magazine. In addition, the trust has been working with an Indian-British team of filmmakers for the last one year. They have been closely documenting their lives and struggles, with the hope that it will connect the long isolated hijra community with the national and international audience. Their aim is to identify 5 top models, who we will work towards getting a spread in a leading fashion magazine – in an attempt to launch them to mainstream society. They will also have photos done by a top fashion photographer. These will be turned into printed postcards which will contain information about the TG community in India and the crises that they face on every day basis. They hope to sell these postcards far and wide. We can also contribute and make way for these game-changers. Their crowd funding campaign aims to reach out to everyone, with the hope that they can bring the change and successfully set up India’s first TG modelling agency.
Log onto https://www.bitgiving.com/tgmodels (Get details here and donate generously) Now you must be wondering why modeling? Fashion industry in India is more open to transgender people working with them than any other industry till now. Be it stylists, fashion assistants, or makeup artists, you will find many TG professionals working in this industry without any bias. Now, the TG community is looking for a face which can represent them in the fashion industry nationally and internationally. Of course, they mean serious business. They aren’t looking for cross dressed characters from the comedy shows but beautiful transgender people who can give international transgender super model Peche Di run for her money. I am sure Indian LGBT community has a lot to offer in terms of manpower in various industry segments. When we can have Manabi Banerjee as the first transgender college principal then why not explore other areas of work life. This initiative is a small step to get the transgender people back to the mainstream work environment. Let us support this cause! They hope to sell these postcards far and wide. We can also contribute and make way for these game-changers. Their crowd funding campaign aims to reach out to everyone, with the hope that they can bring the change and successfully set up India’s first TG modelling agency.
Log onto https://www.bitgiving.com/tgmodels (Get details here and donate generously) Now you must be wondering why modeling? Fashion industry in India is more open to transgender people working with them than any other industry till now. Be it stylists, fashion assistants, or makeup artists, you will find many TG professionals working in this industry without any bias. Now, the TG community is looking for a face which can represent them in the fashion industry nationally and internationally. Of course, they mean serious business. They aren’t looking for cross dressed characters from the comedy shows but beautiful transgender people who can give international transgender super model Peche Di run for her money. I am sure Indian LGBT community has a lot to offer in terms of manpower in various industry segments. When we can have Manabi Banerjee as the first transgender college principal then why not explore other areas of work life. This initiative is a small step to get the transgender people back to the mainstream work environment. Let us support this cause! Do we have a Laith Ashley in India? – A transgender model who will enchant you with his hot body and looks to die for. Check his Instagram account here. He was born a girl. The most hyped Caitlyn Jenner aka Bruce Jenner transformation has already taken the year 2015 by storm. Carmen Carrera was voted to walk with the Victoria’s Secret Angels last year as the first transgender angel in the fashion show. Not many know that she was born as Christopher Roman. But are we ready for transgender models and professionals in India yet? Every morning I cross a junction where a transgender woman (Hijra) asks for money from the commuters waiting at the traffic signal. She used to ask me money in the beginning and I used to give her a very rude look. I somehow feel that by giving alms to the beggars we are encouraging an unhealthy environment. Crimes related to children and women are rooted into begging. I would rather buy a packet of agarbatti or a balloon from the not so fortunate but never encourage begging by giving money. Many a times, I offer food to the beggars. Two vada pavs may cost Rs. 20 but it fills up a hungry stomach. I am more than ready to do that. But I have seen beggars refusing to take food and instead ask for money. I feel pretty unhappy with this behavior. So I avoid to entertain beggars at all cost. Coming back to this transgender woman, who I am very sure, knows me by face now and every time I see her coming towards my car, either I look away or make a nasty face so that she doesn’t ask money from me. Worst is when she starts banging hard on the car’s glass window as if threatening ‘either you give money or I will break the window’. Over a period of time, she has stopped coming to my car. I feel relieved. But then the question arises, why a healthy human being like her is forced to beg. Yes, we are humans first and a gender later. She wears some great sarees, applies bindi and lipstick then why doesn’t she earn money by doing some business or a job? This is a valid question and might absolutely support my stance. But when I did some reality check, I realized that may be that transgender woman has no other option but to beg. India recognized the third gender in 2014. In many official forms you will find the mention of a third segment below Male and Female. But has the transgender community come at par with the others after this ‘on paper’ recognition? May be not. I was reading about an incident where a transgender woman wanted to start a tea stall and run her own business. No one knows if she was able to fulfill her dreams. First of all in India, we still look down upon transgender people. Not many will be ready to consume food or tea prepared by a transgender woman due to several reasons including religion. And in case, she is able to run a business, she will be subjected to a lot of humiliation, harassment and bullying. May be she will be violated and abused physically and mentally, for trying to lead a normal life, like every one of us. In India, the minute a family realizes that a child is born with intersexual characteristics or over a period of time they realize that the child has transsexual bent, they quietly hand over the child to the hijra community. This is specifically true for the rural and small town low income families as they believe that they will not be able to support or protect the little one with special tendencies. How unfortunate is the child who is given away to an unknown group where he/she is raised without proper education, nutrition and safe environment. Transsexual people are never allowed to be a part of the main stream. They are never offered an opportunity to get formal education or to get regular jobs. Often they are subjected to violence, discrimination, sexual assault and forced to either beg or to take up prostitution. Most of them contract AIDS or other deadly diseases which leads to their untimely and painful death. So in this light of ambiguous identity of the transgender people in our society, are we ready to feature a transgender model for our popular brands alongside Khans and Kareenas? I remember two incidences from my growing up years that show how insensitive we are in terms of transgender community, their needs and their rights. And this insensitivity is engraved in our childhood. An effeminate boy in my class was always harassed by a group of the so called manly boys. He was beaten up so badly once in high school where they tore his shirt, blew dust on his face and hair, and he had cuts and bruises all over his face. He cried a lot. He was traumatized, physically and emotionally. He didn’t know why he was subjected to this harsh treatment. He couldn’t understand why other boys pounced on him just because he was a little different than them. Apparently, the boyish boys were trying to fix him up as they deemed his condition to be abnormal. These were school boys who were conditioned by our society to look down upon people who did not fall into the normal category. They were conditioned to behave in a certain manner and made to believe that anybody who belonged to their gender and behaved abnormally should be outcasted, beaten and bullied. Boys like these, carry this idea of discrimination throughout their adulthood and are never able to accept or respect the third gender. Another incidence is when I was in my early twenties and a boy used to come to office with full make-up on. Yes, he loved his mascara, lipsticks, nail polish, kajal and everything feminine. He used to dress up like men but could never let go off the makeup. People used to think he is weird, including me. He was a pretty boy who didn’t have many friends. I had seen him cry a few times alone in the cafeteria. People used to laugh at him and the managers used to talk to him harshly. He was made to feel unwanted on many instances. One day, he decided to wear a skirt and use the women’s toilet. That was the breaking point. He was relieved from his service immediately. He was educated, belonged to a decent family but his fault was that he felt like a woman trapped in a male body. I know, we Indians are not sensitized to deal with such incidents in our home and work environment. But that day I felt that it was unnecessary, it was unfair and unjustified to sack him from work. May be the office could have been more sensitive towards his condition and helped him understand the consequences before firing him. I don’t know where he is today. May be he would have made a great transgender model! Rudrani Chettri, a transgender activist from Delhi and the head of the MITR Trust, is launching India’s first Transgender Model Agency – run by transgender people, for transgender people – and they need our help to make this a reality. MITR attempts to give an opportunity to beautiful, talented and young TGs to get respectable, mainstream work and showcase their talent. To realize this dream, Chettri has taken an unconventional route of crowd funding through BitGiving to fund her project. Chettri has been working for more than 10 years in spreading awareness and fighting to improve TG’s lives in India. Her trust helps over 1500 TG in Delhi alone. They have also teamed up with eminent fashion stylist and photographer, Rishi Raj who will work towards getting a spread in a leading fashion magazine. In addition, the trust has been working with an Indian-British team of filmmakers for the last one year. They have been closely documenting their lives and struggles, with the hope that it will connect the long isolated hijra community with the national and international audience. Their aim is to identify 5 top models, who we will work towards getting a spread in a leading fashion magazine – in an attempt to launch them to mainstream society. They will also have photos done by a top fashion photographer. These will be turned into printed postcards which will contain information about the TG community in India and the crises that they face on every day basis. They hope to sell these postcards far and wide. We can also contribute and make way for these game-changers. Their crowd funding campaign aims to reach out to everyone, with the hope that they can bring the change and successfully set up India’s first TG modelling agency.

A fun post which includes my day-today looks with non-maternity clothes. This time I evaded maternity clothes completely and the results were better than my previous pregnancy. In all these images, I look pregnant. Before you guys ask, let me break it to you. Yes, I am pregnant. And that needs every day adjustments in many areas including how I dress. I am in my comfortable late 30’s and trust me fashion is the last thing on my mind when it comes to pregnancy. All, I want to look is happy and stylish. So, with my current stock of clothes, I did manage to create looks which were practical as well as looked good on my frame. And these looks are from my recent Euro trip and the so called winters in Mumbai. Thankfully, Mumbai winters allow dusters and cover ups on certain days.  Apart from anarkali and tights, there are several other clothes from your regular-wear that you can easily continue wearing right up to your 9th month, without opting for the maternity wear like maxi dresses, skirts below the belly with oversized tees and denim shirts as a cover up. You can get as creative as you want with your current wardrobe. Moreover, the kind of maternity wear available in India makes me cringe at the every sight. I think the only piece of clothing that is required from the maternity wear (that I would recommend) during pregnancy is maternity denim pants with a big belly band. Anyway, this is just my opinion and in no way am I endorsing non-maternity clothes over maternity clothes. What is important is that one should be comfortable wearing what they want to wear.  I wore my winter coat from the regular wear, without any hiccups. I buttoned only the top buttons and left the jacket unbuttoned below my bust area. I used layers of clothes on my belly area to create a warm cover. Thermal, long t-shirts, sweat shirt, bella band and thin layers of clothing were used to create a warm cover which protected my belly area from cold.  I usually wore platform shoes or flat knee length boots to give my growing body some balance. But when it came to a lot of walking, I opted for my walking shoes. Bright walking shoes look great with a sporty look. Tights, sweat shirts or long t-shirts with a duster/jacket can easily become your comfort wear.  When it came to partying in style, I didn’t compromise on the chic appeal. I wore my regular party body hugging dress in green colour. Solid colours make you look elegant. I tried to keep the accessories to the minimum. My belly was showing a lot but then I balanced it with a stole. Moreover, why get conscious about the belly. After all, I am pregnant and not suffering from any disease.   Back in Mumbai, I used my oversized denim shirt over a white spaghetti t-shirt, along with a denim skirt and black platform boots to create a cool yet comfortable look. I only buttoned the lower buttons on my shirt to fold it inside the spaghetti strap t-shirt. It gave my belly enough room and also created an illusion that I had tucked my shirt inside the skirt. I completed the look by carrying a bright clutch bag. I also tried to create another party look in all black. I used an all-black tights which had a tiny panel of bright pink on the sides, a black tank top which was comfortably long, and a black duster. To balance that I used a clutch and block heel shoes in zebra print. It was a contrast to the plain black look. This was the easiest and the most comfortable party look till date. I accessorised less as I already had a lot of shimmer on my top.  Last but not the least, I wore a turtle neck, midi dress in black and white stripes along with a black duster and carried a big yellow bag to add a colour element to my look. The shoes were comfortable pumps with kitten heels. This was comfortably showing my bump and looked super stylish.  What do you guys think about my maternity looks? Do you have any other suggestions? (Starred images clicked by Protibha Chakravorty) In my recent trip to Europe, I realised that European women hardly use any harsh makeup. Either they opt for nude lips with a light non-gooey gloss, and a bit of mascara or they go for a classic red lip and black winged eye liner look. There is nothing too extreme for them with heaps of eye shadows or layers of foundation on their face. Even the brides keep it simple. And believe me, it looks much more appealing as they try to keep it as natural as possible. Their vintage/classic look of red lips is fascinating. They love to use cool shades of red on their lips. (Cool shades mean pinkish reds or bluish reds.) These are not stark vermilion reds but something subtle and beautiful. Mumbaigloss decided to list 5 beautiful shades of reds in India which I regularly use. These are not exactly red but look beautiful on my skin tone. And mind it, none of this is sponsored. It is my choice of makeup that I use on everyday basis. I am sure it will help a lot of others who are trying to figure out a decent shade of lipstick for themselves. Lakme 9 to 5 Red Chaos 
My first pick is Lakme 9 to 5 Red Chaos enriched with vitamin E. This lip shade has a good staying power and a matte finish. Ideal for every day wear, the colour is muted pink hinting towards red but looks beautiful on medium to fair complexion. I use it almost every day and it looks and feels great. If I want to make it look more dramatic then I apply a Colourbar gloss in the shade of Natural Tan over it and it feels perfect. Maybelline Superstay 14 hour lipstick – Non-Stop Red 
If you are fed up of the pop colour pinks then take a pick on this lovely shade. This is a beautiful pinkish red and looks great with denims or blue casual wear. It is not a cutesy/girly colour but a bold matte red with a hint of pink to enhance your natural complexion. The staying power is decent and not 14 hours as claimed by the company. It doesn’t transfer easily. You can use clear gloss as a top coat to add a little drama to your lips. Always keep it handy for touch ups as when you eat, it tends to comes off. MAC Ruby Woo 
MAC’s Ruby Woo shade is a classic beauty. I prefer it over Russian Red. This is a bold matte berry red colour which goes very well with classic LBD (Little Black Dress) or any navy to blue dress. Even silver or sequinned dresses look great with this shade. The texture might feel a bit dry so it is better to apply it on moisturised lips. It comes off very easily while eating, especially from the inside lips, so I always carry it for emergency touch ups. (Please don’t do touch ups right at the dining table. Always excuse yourself to another room or bath room before re-applying makeup.) Ruby Woo looks great on medium to fair complexion. Faces Canada Ultime Pro Longwear Matte Lipstick – Bold 
At first, Faces Canada Ultime Pro Longwear Matte Lipstick – Bold shade looks more of hot pink than red. But gradually when the pigments settle, it gives a very blush red/pink sort of colour which instantly brightens up the complexion. The staying power is good and it doesn’t transfer easily. It looks great with summery floral dresses or casual wear. I wore it with black and it still looked great. Revlon Pencil Lip liner in Burgundy 
This is a beautiful deep red colour which stays on for more than 4 hours. I use this lip liner all over my lips after exfoliating and moisturising and then top it up with a clear gloss or Vaseline lip liner. The product is inexpensive but gives a beautiful shape and colour to my lips. I have worn it to many evening parties and it has looked great with both ethnic and western wear. It is my choice of makeup that I use on everyday basis. I am sure it will help a lot of others who are trying to figure out a decent shade of lipstick for themselves. Lakme 9 to 5 Red Chaos 
My first pick is Lakme 9 to 5 Red Chaos enriched with vitamin E. This lip shade has a good staying power and a matte finish. Ideal for every day wear, the colour is muted pink hinting towards red but looks beautiful on medium to fair complexion. I use it almost every day and it looks and feels great. If I want to make it look more dramatic then I apply a Colourbar gloss in the shade of Natural Tan over it and it feels perfect. Maybelline Superstay 14 hour lipstick – Non-Stop Red 
If you are fed up of the pop colour pinks then take a pick on this lovely shade. This is a beautiful pinkish red and looks great with denims or blue casual wear. It is not a cutesy/girly colour but a bold matte red with a hint of pink to enhance your natural complexion. The staying power is decent and not 14 hours as claimed by the company. It doesn’t transfer easily. You can use clear gloss as a top coat to add a little drama to your lips. Always keep it handy for touch ups as when you eat, it tends to comes off. MAC Ruby Woo 
MAC’s Ruby Woo shade is a classic beauty. I prefer it over Russian Red. This is a bold matte berry red colour which goes very well with classic LBD (Little Black Dress) or any navy to blue dress. Even silver or sequinned dresses look great with this shade. The texture might feel a bit dry so it is better to apply it on moisturised lips. It comes off very easily while eating, especially from the inside lips, so I always carry it for emergency touch ups. (Please don’t do touch ups right at the dining table. Always excuse yourself to another room or bath room before re-applying makeup.) Ruby Woo looks great on medium to fair complexion. Faces Canada Ultime Pro Longwear Matte Lipstick – Bold 
At first, Faces Canada Ultime Pro Longwear Matte Lipstick – Bold shade looks more of hot pink than red. But gradually when the pigments settle, it gives a very blush red/pink sort of colour which instantly brightens up the complexion. The staying power is good and it doesn’t transfer easily. It looks great with summery floral dresses or casual wear. I wore it with black and it still looked great. Revlon Pencil Lip liner in Burgundy 
This is a beautiful deep red colour which stays on for more than 4 hours. I use this lip liner all over my lips after exfoliating and moisturising and then top it up with a clear gloss or Vaseline lip liner. The product is inexpensive but gives a beautiful shape and colour to my lips. I have worn it to many evening parties and it has looked great with both ethnic and western wear. Which lipstick colour would you prefer  to use? Do leave a comment below. In my recent trip to Europe, I realised that European women hardly use any harsh makeup. Either they opt for nude lips with a light non-gooey gloss, and a bit of mascara or they go for a classic red lip and black winged eye liner look. There is nothing too extreme for them with heaps of eye shadows or layers of foundation on their face. Even the brides keep it simple. And believe me, it looks much more appealing as they try to keep it as natural as possible. Their vintage/classic look of red lips is fascinating. They love to use cool shades of red on their lips. Which lipstick colour would you prefer  to use? Do leave a comment below. Diwali is next week and many of you must be still deciding what to wear. Of course, this once in a year festival is so special in many ways and you want to look your best. Mumbaigloss decided to round up a few experts to give tips on the kind of makeup, jewellery and dressing that will help you shine in the festival of lights. What to wear? According to fashion designer Ritu Seksaria, opt for traditional dresses like sari, lehenga, etc. in bright colours. Bright colors go really well with festivals. Diwali should be celebrated wearing eye catching colors like tangerine, fuschia, red and violet. Go traditional this Diwali with a twist of modern trend. Wear a beautiful red or green saree with a brocade pallu and team it up with a well-fitting halter neck blouse. You can opt for something classier like a sheer saree in monochrome, and accessorize it with diamonds and pearls. One can never go wrong with them. A mid-riff baring choli and a low cut lehenga does seem to up the style quotient this Diwali. Try a simple lehenga with an embroidered dupatta. It is very important to wear a cut that fits you well and accentuates the right parts of your body. What makeup? As the dresses will be heavy with embellishments, thread work and will be bright and colourful, it is better to go light on the makeup. Minimal makeup and a neat hairdo will complete your look and you’re all set to enjoy your Diwali, says Ritu. Prep-up your skin by going for deep hydrating facials, moisturizing daily and applying sunscreen whenever you are outdoors. It helps you to get that festive glow. Use a hydrating foundation as the weather is dry comparatively. Invest in a good bronzer. What jewellery to wear? According to jewellery designer Aakash Barmecha of Yoube Jewellery, pick one statement piece rather than go all out with accessorizing. He also insists that jewellery should be worn as per the dress. If you are wearing traditional sari then go for traditional jewellery designs, if you are wearing an indo-western outfit then go for modern designs. Keep it modern with simple accessories or wear just one statement piece. Cult favourite jewellery like diamond or jaded jhumkis, chaand balis, balas, Kadas or pendants are great options. If your outfit is inclined more towards an indo-western look, fusion jewellery works well, a mix and match of diamond, polki and jadau jewellery with bright colourful gemstones in innovative ways and eclectic styles add appeal to any outfit. Wear print! A digital print dupatta with a plain dress or digital print kurti teamed with pretty hoops, balas, kadas or a pretty pair of bangles lend a completely modern, trendy look. Palazzo pants are seen frequently and can also add a bit of style teamed with the right top, add a single earring or wrist cuff to create a unique distinct look this Diwali. Floral motifs are really in and look both gorgeous and feminine. Keep in mind your outfit, it is not necessary to match everything perfectly, so try something unique and distinctive. Rose gold looks lovely with most ensembles, though you could also pick up a dual tone. Diwali is next week and many of you must be still deciding what to wear. Fashion design students need not go all the way to New York to get education from the esteemed Parsons School of Design. Now you can get the same courses right here in Mumbai. David Van Zandt, President of The New School – Parsons School of Design, New York visited the Indian School of Design and Innovation (ISDI) – Parsons Mumbai campus here in Mumbai to inaugurate the ISDI Academic Campus and formalize the association between the two design institutions. The New School – Parsons School of Design, ranked number one for design, supports ISDI by creating a unique design education delivery system, ISDI benefits from Parsons’ faculty, on-going training, a global curriculum, global relationships, student and faculty exchanges all meeting international academic quality assurance processes. David Van Zandt, President, The New School – Parsons School of Design, said, “Design is engaging boardrooms; creating a problem solving ethos in a corporation. Design schools are not only a major source of new talent for the economy’s rapidly growing creative sector, but are critical catalysts for entrepreneurship. Universities must embrace interdisciplinary learning on both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Even for students who are not focusing in the arts, some experience and literacy with design will prove crucial in an increasingly creative economy. While design is a concept that is often assumed to be about engineering and high-tech applications, it is only a small part of its focus. Design, broadly defined, is an interdisciplinary approach to problem-solving that seeks to develop more effective products, environments, and organizations.” “At its heart, design is about understanding people and how they interact in the larger world. By leveraging design thinking and its intersections with other disciplines, universities will continue to serve as the incubators of creative innovation.” Radha Kapoor, Founder & Executive Director, ISDI, and also an alumnus of Parsons School of Design, New York said “ISDI – Parsons Mumbai is laser focused on building a New-Gen ecosystem of Design & Innovation driven by Creative Entrepreneurship in India. In today’s globalised economy, our key focus is to create an effective global design network, that significantly accelerates the success of Indian Entrepreneurship & Innovation across cultural boundaries. I am so glad that a world-class design school has finally decided to make our city its home. More power to art! I am glad that Vero Moda chose style icon Kangna Ranaut to design their new AW, 15 collection. Now high-street fashion will get the crisp style cue from our very own fashionista and Bollywood actress Kangna who is known for her quirky sense of fashion. Kangana Ranaut, who is very excited to have designed the collection with VERO MODA said, “My fashion philosophy is to follow my mood for the day and is about what makes me feel good. I’m not a follower of fashion trends, instead I make my own rules and this collection does exactly that. I’m happy that this collection is inspired by my very own personal style. Unlike most occasion wear which is very one-dimensional – we’ve tried to stay away from the traditional and explored different hues, silhouettes and textures.” The MARQUEE by Kangana Ranaut AW’15 collection has five distinct lines: European high-street fashion brand VERO MODA launched the 2nd edition of MARQUEE Autumn Winter ’15, a limited edition collection designed by Kangana Ranaut at a glitzy fashion evening attended by the crème de la crème of Mumbai at Mehboob Studio, Bandra. The collection was presented on the runway through a splendid fashion show with the lovely Kangana Ranaut herself as the show-stopper. The actress looked absolutely stunning in a halter neck printed dress from the collection. Supermodel Ujjwala Raut made a rare appearance and opened the show in a strappy number. The legendary Pop-Rock music band ‘The Other People’, known for their energetic performances, released a track especially composed for the VERO MODA MARQUEE collection. Aditi Rao Hydari, Radhika Apte, Nandita Mahtani, Bhavana Pandey, DJ Yudhishtir, Upen Patel, Tara Sharma, Sameer Malhotra, Prateik Babbar, Siddhanth Kapoor, Madhoo Shah, Ravi Krishnan, Anu Dewan, Ayesha Takia, Anjana Sukhani, Dino Morea, Falguni and Shane Peacock, Suchitra Pillai, Manasi Scott, Elli Avram, Prerna Goel, Rashmi Nigam, Marc Robinson, Richa Chadda, Vikram Raizada, Ayan Mukerji, Mahek Chahal, Keith Sequeira, Rochelle Rao, Shaina NC, Sikander Kher, Rhea Chakraborty and Ira Dubey  were some of the names that were present to get a first glimpse of this bespoke collection and celebrate Kangana’s foray into fashion designing. Renowned fashion name and stylist, Anaita Shroff Adajania created distinct looks for the gorgeous models who walked the ramp in a well-coordinated fashion show. The fashion show was followed by a grand celebration. I liked the ivory and blue collection better than the bold red and black collection. But again it’s a personal choice. Apart from the collection, I liked Richa Chadda’s monochrome skater dress that she wore to the event.  Would you wear a dress designed by Queen Kangna Ranaut? Leave your comments below. The legendary Pop-Rock music band ‘The Other People’, known for their energetic performances, released a track especially composed for the VERO MODA MARQUEE collection. Aditi Rao Hydari, Radhika Apte, Nandita Mahtani, Bhavana Pandey, DJ Yudhishtir, Upen Patel, Tara Sharma, Sameer Malhotra, Prateik Babbar, Siddhanth Kapoor, Madhoo Shah, Ravi Krishnan, Anu Dewan, Ayesha Takia, Anjana Sukhani, Dino Morea, Falguni and Shane Peacock, Suchitra Pillai, Manasi Scott, Elli Avram, Prerna Goel, Rashmi Nigam, Marc Robinson, Richa Chadda, Vikram Raizada, Ayan Mukerji, Mahek Chahal, Keith Sequeira, Rochelle Rao, Shaina NC, Sikander Kher, Rhea Chakraborty and Ira Dubey  were some of the names that were present to get a first glimpse of this bespoke collection and celebrate Kangana’s foray into fashion designing. Renowned fashion name and stylist, Anaita Shroff Adajania created distinct looks for the gorgeous models who walked the ramp in a well-coordinated fashion show. The fashion show was followed by a grand celebration. I liked the ivory and blue collection better than the bold red and black collection. But again it’s a personal choice. Apart from the collection, I liked Richa Chadda’s monochrome skater dress that she wore to the event.  Would you wear a dress designed by Queen Kangna Ranaut? Leave your comments below. I am glad that Vero Moda chose style icon Kangna Ranaut to design their new AW, 15 collection. Now high-street fashion will get the crisp style cue from our very own fashionista and Bollywood actress Kangna who is known for her quirky sense of fashion. Kangana Ranaut, who is very excited to have designed the collection with VERO MODA said, “My fashion philosophy is to follow my mood for the day and is about what makes me feel good. I’m not a follower of fashion trends, instead I make my own rules and this collection does exactly that. I’m happy that this collection is inspired by my very own personal style. Unlike most occasion wear which is very one-dimensional – we’ve tried to stay away from the traditional and explored different hues, silhouettes and textures.” The MARQUEE by Kangana Ranaut AW’15 collection has five distinct lines: European high-street fashion brand VERO MODA launched the 2nd edition of MARQUEE Autumn Winter ’15, a limited edition collection designed by Kangana Ranaut at a glitzy fashion evening attended by the crème de la crème of Mumbai at Mehboob Studio, Bandra.
