Mumbaigloss attended a recent event by Godrej India Culture Lab, an intellectual cultural hub in Mumbai city, in association with LFW about the future of Fashion Journalism in India. Parmesh Shahani, Head, Godrej India Culture Lab, moderated the hour long panel discussion with fashion and journalism pundits like Aishwarya Subramanyam, Editor, ELLE India, Ambika Anand, Fashion Editor, NDTV Good Times and MissMalini, fashion blogger. I being a blogger was rather intrigued at this debate. With a sea of fashion bloggers and vloggers all over India in the recent times, where did the editorial authority lie when it came to Indian fashion? Do people who talk about fashion, really understand fashion? Where will fashion journalism head 10 years from now? And are there any good fashion journalists left in the country? Ok, let’s face it. We don’t really read our morning newspapers anymore. Well, most of us. We hold our tablets instead, with our morning cup of coffee rather than the traditional newspapers. And going forward, as future generations become more and more absorbed into the digital world, the trend will become to get all news and info online. Be it fashion or politics, digital mode will become the preferred mode. But does digital world has editorial authority? Well, not completely. In the digital world, anyone can publish. There are no rules or an authority to regulate information. Freedom of speech is used to voice out opinions about anything and everything without any restraint. This might make or break any brand or a person. So how can we claim that the views presented on the digital platform are from a subject matter expert? But this is just one side of the story. The other side is that people can relate to a common person talking about fashion. They can relate more to a person’s style than a fashion designer’s brand and most of the time it is street style. So, in effect it has invoked interest of a common man into the world of fashion. This is where bloggers, vloggers and influencers have more power over the print platform. As Aishwarya Subramanyam put across aptly that the print media should fear the Malinis of the digital world as their reach is growing faster and stronger. But she disagreed on any existing single editorial authority. Coming back to the bloggers/vloggers – are they in any way experts of the subject? No, most of them are not. Most of them don’t know anything about fashion journalism. Leave aside pronouncing the names of the brands correctly, they don’t know about the designers, their style or their market. They don’t even know the difference between Hermes and Harman Kardon. Yet, they are valued because of their readership. The concentrated readership on the fashion can only be sought through fashion bloggers which a magazine might not provide. Magazines usually have mixed readership. But does that give bloggers an editorial upper-hand? May be not. Aishwarya said that while digital gave audience quick updates on the fashion events but print provided them factual and informative report on possible trends. Though, digital gives liberty in terms of space, print could have space restrictions. So it is a great mix to use TV, print and digital mediums than concentrating on only one medium. Aishwarya admitted good writers were rare and multitasking was needed to translate the same into digital world. Digital world is real-time (most of the times) and churning out quality features is rather difficult on that medium. So where does fashion critiques feature in the scheme of things? Aishwarya responded it was not necessary to criticize in a magazine since most of the regular readers know the difference between good and bad fashion. Ambika stated being a lifestyle channel, critiquing was not done on NDTV either. Malini highlighted that though critiquing gives rise to social media bullying but then if serious critiques are considered then much honest opinions are reflected on the digital platform than print. Aishwarya pointed out that if critiquing was the strength of a journalist and if put in context of designer world and history of fashion, then internet helps.  How does digital world help in chronicling fashion history? Malini felt the internet as digital space was a time capsule recording history. Aishwarya added that print has invaluable archives and resources available.  So what is the future of fashion journalism? Ambika stressed it will be a multiple platform world for all to survive. Aishwarya asserted print will not disappear as it is about balanced storytelling and brave and informed fashion journalists are needed. Digital will expand too and there is no denying that it will have its own demand in terms of fashion influencers and trend setters. Anaita Shroff Adajania, Fashion Director, Vogue India added, that there were many types of readers and catering to all was necessary. To conclude, MissMalini said that authority will always lie with the legacy of print and television, while social media for her was a part of an eco-system that bridged the gap and decoded fashion for the common man. Dry ends, hair looking like hay after a lot of styling abuse and you wonder what you can do to make them look healthy and shiny again. You go to your hair stylist who suggests Cysteine Keratin treatment for your hair. Of course, it doesn’t come cheap. The total amount spent on the treatment and the supporting products will easily cost your around Rs. 11, 000. So is it worth it? Let’s find out.  I went through the Cysteine treatment on 3rd April, 2015. I purposefully waited for three and a half months to give you a first-hand account as to what happens during and after the treatment. My natural hair was straight, glossy and fine during my college days. It had a lot of volume. But over a period of time, with irregular hair spas or oiling and N number of product applications like hair colour, hair spray, etc. on them, my hair started to look a lot wavy, dry and lifeless. The ombre hair colour made the ends of my hair very dry. They were on the verge of getting split ends. That’s when I decided it was time to do something about it. I went to Enrich Salon where the senior stylist suggested that I go for the Cysteine treatment (Of course, they always suggest an expensive treatment but it is up to us to decide if it is really going to be worth it). Not many know that it is a protein treatment for your hair which relaxes its texture like curls and waves. It doesn’t straighten them though. It gives a very natural smooth finish to your hair texture making them look more polished. So, I decided to give it a go. The treatment is called Cysteine Complex Intense Smoothening. My hair is below shoulders so they quoted Rs. 7500 for my treatment. The rest of Rs. 3500 was spent towards the after care products. The stylist got me a paper to sign which had its terms and conditions stating that the treatment lightens the colour of the hair by 2 shades, it won’t make my hair completely straight etc. Finally, he took me to the wash basin where he washed my hair with a special shampoo that helps to remove every iota of dirt and oil from the hair. Basically, it strips down your hair completely from any possible product residues, natural oil, and gunk. My hair was then blow dried. It looked strayed, dry and weak. I felt very bad looking at their condition.  Then he got the Amazon Cysteine Complex Smoothening Cream and started applying on my hair section by section. The procedure is same as when a hair cream is applied to your hair during a hair spa. He left one inch hair from my root and applied the cream to the rest of the hair till the end. It is done so that the cream doesn’t make the roots go soft which eventually may result in hair fall.  After applying the cream to all my hair he wound it up in a clear plastic film. He ensured that my hair didn’t have any folds or creases. After about half an hour he came back to check my hair and removed the clear film. He took my semi-wet-with-cream hair section by section and with the help of a hair straightener, started drying up my hair. Towards the end of it my hair looked poker straight which had a strange little smell and of course product deposit. I was asked not to wash my hair for two to three days.  After that, I was allowed to wash my hair with three specific products that the stylist recommended– De Fabulous Hair Repair Shampoo, De Fabulous Hair Repair Conditioner, and Amazon Series Acai Oil Treatment. My stylist told me that these products should last me for over a month and I will see the condition of my hair get better with regular use.  He said the hair will stay smooth for a period of 3 – 4 months post this treatment. I left the salon with a heavy heart and an empty pocket. But I told myself, it was worth the investment. Rs. 11, 000 divided by 4 months comes to Rs. 2750 per month which is ok if not bad for healthy looking hair.  I washed my hair with the shampoo on the third day. It is a very mild shampoo and my hair felt icky and was still smelling of the product. The conditioner weighed my hair down for the first few washes as it is full of moisturizing elements. Combined with freshly done protein treatment, my hair looked limp. But in later washes it made my hair feel very soft. The stylist asked me to leave the conditioner in my hair for at least 5 minutes before washing it off. It actually makes the hair feel smooth and soft. I think I will continue with this conditioner even after the Cysteine effect wears off. Amazon Series Acai Oil Treatment smells wonderful. I was advised to apply it to my hair roots post hair wash and before styling on towel dried hair. I was asked to take a few drops of the oil on my palm, warm it up a bit on my hand and then apply to the roots which will give it amazing shine and fragrance. It definitely makes me feel good. I started using all the products regularly. The shampoo was over in a month. The conditioner and the Acai Oil are still there. I started using mild shampoo from other brands to wash my hair. Till now my hair looks straight (not poker straight but natural straight). Slight waves have started appearing towards the ends but it looks polished and smooth for sure. Cysteine treatment is one of the safest hair treatments in the market with excellent results. If you are unsure about how it will react, go for a patch test. Though it is expensive but it surely makes the hair smooth and soft. Many might feel that they have lost hair volume after the treatment but usually it is because straight hair looks less in volume than wavy or curly hair. So, if you are looking for a dramatic change in your looks or just want to fix your unruly hair then you can try this treatment. *I paid for my treatment and products and this is not a promotion but mere beauty experience that I wanted to share. Do let me know what do you think about this treatment? It gives a very natural smooth finish to your hair texture making them look more polished. So, I decided to give it a go. The treatment is called Cysteine Complex Intense Smoothening. My hair is below shoulders so they quoted Rs. 7500 for my treatment. The rest of Rs. 3500 was spent towards the after care products. The stylist got me a paper to sign which had its terms and conditions stating that the treatment lightens the colour of the hair by 2 shades, it won’t make my hair completely straight etc. Finally, he took me to the wash basin where he washed my hair with a special shampoo that helps to remove every iota of dirt and oil from the hair. Basically, it strips down your hair completely from any possible product residues, natural oil, and gunk. My hair was then blow dried. It looked strayed, dry and weak. I felt very bad looking at their condition.  Then he got the Amazon Cysteine Complex Smoothening Cream and started applying on my hair section by section. The procedure is same as when a hair cream is applied to your hair during a hair spa. He left one inch hair from my root and applied the cream to the rest of the hair till the end. It is done so that the cream doesn’t make the roots go soft which eventually may result in hair fall.  After applying the cream to all my hair he wound it up in a clear plastic film. He ensured that my hair didn’t have any folds or creases. After about half an hour he came back to check my hair and removed the clear film. He took my semi-wet-with-cream hair section by section and with the help of a hair straightener, started drying up my hair. Towards the end of it my hair looked poker straight which had a strange little smell and of course product deposit. I was asked not to wash my hair for two to three days.  After that, I was allowed to wash my hair with three specific products that the stylist recommended– De Fabulous Hair Repair Shampoo, De Fabulous Hair Repair Conditioner, and Amazon Series Acai Oil Treatment. My stylist told me that these products should last me for over a month and I will see the condition of my hair get better with regular use.  He said the hair will stay smooth for a period of 3 – 4 months post this treatment. I left the salon with a heavy heart and an empty pocket. But I told myself, it was worth the investment. Rs. 11, 000 divided by 4 months comes to Rs. 2750 per month which is ok if not bad for healthy looking hair.  I washed my hair with the shampoo on the third day. It is a very mild shampoo and my hair felt icky and was still smelling of the product. The conditioner weighed my hair down for the first few washes as it is full of moisturizing elements. Combined with freshly done protein treatment, my hair looked limp. But in later washes it made my hair feel very soft. The stylist asked me to leave the conditioner in my hair for at least 5 minutes before washing it off. It actually makes the hair feel smooth and soft. I think I will continue with this conditioner even after the Cysteine effect wears off. Amazon Series Acai Oil Treatment smells wonderful. I was advised to apply it to my hair roots post hair wash and before styling on towel dried hair. I was asked to take a few drops of the oil on my palm, warm it up a bit on my hand and then apply to the roots which will give it amazing shine and fragrance. It definitely makes me feel good. I started using all the products regularly. The shampoo was over in a month. The conditioner and the Acai Oil are still there. I started using mild shampoo from other brands to wash my hair. Till now my hair looks straight (not poker straight but natural straight). Slight waves have started appearing towards the ends but it looks polished and smooth for sure. Cysteine treatment is one of the safest hair treatments in the market with excellent results. If you are unsure about how it will react, go for a patch test. Though it is expensive but it surely makes the hair smooth and soft. Many might feel that they have lost hair volume after the treatment but usually it is because straight hair looks less in volume than wavy or curly hair. So, if you are looking for a dramatic change in your looks or just want to fix your unruly hair then you can try this treatment. *I paid for my treatment and products and this is not a promotion but mere beauty experience that I wanted to share. Do let me know what do you think about this treatment? I went through the Cysteine treatment on 3rd April, 2015. I purposefully waited for three and a half months to give you a first-hand account as to what happens during and after the treatment. My natural hair was straight, glossy and fine during my college days. It had a lot of volume. But over a period of time, with irregular hair spas or oiling and N number of product applications like hair colour, hair spray, etc. on them, my hair started to look a lot wavy, dry and lifeless. The ombre hair colour made the ends of my hair very dry. They were on the verge of getting split ends. That’s when I decided it was time to do something about it. The heat through the year takes a toll on your skin and hair. Moreover, if your job requires you to travel far and wide then a lot of damage is done during the peak sunny mornings. You can get skin tan, skin rashes, frizzy hair, body odour due to sweat and heat, itchy scalp and skin and a gamut of other problems due to heat. But there are a few good solutions which can counter these problems. You can say that these are my beauty secrets which help me to look and feel better during summer months. Problem 1: Skin Tan Skin tan is a major problem. It makes the complexion dull irrespective of your skin colour. I feel dark skin tone is equally beautiful if the skin is clean and glowing. But sun and heat leaves the skin patchy giving it irregular blotches of colour. This can be tackled with honey and ground chana dal face pack. Apply it on the affected area. Leave it for 15 minutes and then wash. If you do this regularly for two weeks, you will see a lot of difference in your complexion. But in case you are one of those who love quick results and less mess then go for Spinz Sun Tan Remover. This is a cream based product that contains no bleach. It has been dermatologically tested and found to be safe for all skin types. If your job requires you to be outside a lot then you can keep this little tube in your bag and use this product to get a de-tanned radiant look right before an important meeting or an event. Apply about 2 finger lengths of Spinz Sun tan remover cream on you face for 5 -10 minutes and wash it with plain water. It is that simple. It is like an on-the-go mini-facial anywhere you want.  #SpinzBanTheTan Look at this movie to know more:  Problem 2: Darkened lips Sun can darken the delicate skin on your lips making them look discoloured and dry. I always use a good lip balm to make them look soft and supple but in case the damage has already being done then use a high-definition matt lipstick or lip line in natural pink to fill up the lips and use a neutral balm on top of it. Try to make a fine granulated sugar and oil scrub for your lips and use it twice a week to regain natural colour and suppleness. I use Lakme High-definition in Rose Bloom or Coral Flare to cover the darkened lips.  Problem 3: Frizzy Hair First and foremost, if you have frizzy hair then look no further than your kitchen. Mix two tablespoon of coconut oil with curd water. The residual water left after the curd has been taken is full of protein and nutrients. Apply this lavishly on your frizzy hair then cover your hair with plastic/shower cap or hot towel. Let it stay on your hair for 20-30 minutes and rinse with a mild shampoo. With weekly use, you will find that your hair looks smooth. You can also use hair serum on your wet hair to give it shine. I use Amazon hair serum.  Problem 4: Body Odour Market is flooded with deodorants. If you find them ineffective or if they irritate your skin then make your own spray. Mix water and equal amount of herbal oil of your choice into a spray bottle and then shake. You can create your own body spray. I use lemongrass oil to create my own body spray. Else, I use Chambor body mist which has a very floral-rainforest sort of fragrance. It lingers on for quite a while.  Problem 5: Oily face Face gets oily in the summer months. It looks and feels unpleasant. To keep the skin from producing more oil, mix lemon and cucumber juice in equal quantity on your face and wash it off with plain water after 15 minutes. Do this process thrice a week and see the results. Try not to use foundation or oily make up on your skin. Instead apply Lacto Calamine which soothes the skin as well as gives it a basic coverage. I use Lacto Calamine Oil Control.  Which are your summer beauty secrets? Do share with me in the comments section.  // <![CDATA[

It has been dermatologically tested and found to be safe for all skin types. If your job requires you to be outside a lot then you can keep this little tube in your bag and use this product to get a de-tanned radiant look right before an important meeting or an event. Apply about 2 finger lengths of Spinz Sun tan remover cream on you face for 5 -10 minutes and wash it with plain water. It is that simple. It is like an on-the-go mini-facial anywhere you want.  #SpinzBanTheTan Look at this movie to know more:  Problem 2: Darkened lips Sun can darken the delicate skin on your lips making them look discoloured and dry. I always use a good lip balm to make them look soft and supple but in case the damage has already being done then use a high-definition matt lipstick or lip line in natural pink to fill up the lips and use a neutral balm on top of it. Try to make a fine granulated sugar and oil scrub for your lips and use it twice a week to regain natural colour and suppleness. I use Lakme High-definition in Rose Bloom or Coral Flare to cover the darkened lips.  Problem 3: Frizzy Hair First and foremost, if you have frizzy hair then look no further than your kitchen. Mix two tablespoon of coconut oil with curd water. The residual water left after the curd has been taken is full of protein and nutrients. Apply this lavishly on your frizzy hair then cover your hair with plastic/shower cap or hot towel. Let it stay on your hair for 20-30 minutes and rinse with a mild shampoo. With weekly use, you will find that your hair looks smooth. You can also use hair serum on your wet hair to give it shine. I use Amazon hair serum.  Problem 4: Body Odour Market is flooded with deodorants. If you find them ineffective or if they irritate your skin then make your own spray. Mix water and equal amount of herbal oil of your choice into a spray bottle and then shake. You can create your own body spray. I use lemongrass oil to create my own body spray. Else, I use Chambor body mist which has a very floral-rainforest sort of fragrance. It lingers on for quite a while.  Problem 5: Oily face Face gets oily in the summer months. It looks and feels unpleasant. To keep the skin from producing more oil, mix lemon and cucumber juice in equal quantity on your face and wash it off with plain water after 15 minutes. Do this process thrice a week and see the results. Try not to use foundation or oily make up on your skin. Instead apply Lacto Calamine which soothes the skin as well as gives it a basic coverage. I use Lacto Calamine Oil Control.  Which are your summer beauty secrets? Do share with me in the comments section.  // <![CDATA[

She avoids hard drinks and juices but tends to drink a lot of water. Time to time, she keeps on stretching or moving around to avoid cramps. The Club is a member’s only recreational club which provides facilities like swimming pool, a well-equipped gym and spa. Who doesn’t like a relaxing and rejuvenating spa treatment? So when Antara Spa invited me to try out their Cool Splash Spa Therapy which included 60 mins of Swedish and Thai massage strokes with Vetiver and Orange blossom oil and 30 mins of cooling and rehydrating Aloe Vera Mint Wrap  to beat the summer heat, I readily agreed to get pampered. The Club is conveniently located in D.N. Nagar and I reached the venue on time. The property is huge, clean and well-managed. Manager and the staff had been waiting for me and without any delay, I was taken inside the treatment room. I was asked to fill up a form giving my health and allergy details. I would have loved to get a refreshing welcome drink (herbs and spices) after travelling to the venue in the scorching Mumbai heat but it wasn’t offered. So, I would like to suggest to Antara Spa to create a signature drink which can be offered to the clients before the spa session to make them feel rehydrated. The spa is located next to the swimming pool and has a lovely view. The interiors are soothing and minimalistic with artefacts strewn tastefully across the property. Use of silk, teak wood, mother of pearl has rendered the treatment rooms with class and beauty. Relaxing music soothes the nerves and the aroma of various oils and products prepares the mind to shut off from the world and relax. Antara Spa has: It was time to check what they had to offer.  The therapist was extremely courteous and asked me to get comfortable. She asked me if I had any particular concern area like back pain, neck pain etc. She also inquired about the pressure applied and if I was ok with it. I had a few scare moments when she pulled my hands at the back putting slight pressure on the lower back and I heard a little snap. For few seconds I felt I would never be able to walk again. But that was just a bad thought. As my body felt less tensed and relaxed. My back felt a little heat and the lower back pain somehow vanished. With little tugs and pulls, she went on for an hour as if trying to rebuild the structure of my body. The aroma of the oils had already made me go half sleepy and half excited. The end result after the massage session was that I felt refreshed. I felt happy and relaxed.  After this she put cooling Aloe Vera and Mint wrap and covered my body with a plastic film. This is to seal the moisture in the skin provided by these two herbs. Unfortunately, she left the AC on and didn’t ask if I wanted it to continue. I started to shiver in spite of two towels which were put on me as a cover.  I would like to suggest Antara spa to get proper body covers for the clients who might feel cold after the treatment as well as check with them if they would like the AC on at least twice in those 30 minutes of Aloe Vera and Mint wrap.  Otherwise, the experience was absolutely terrific. I came back all glowing and rejuvenated. The total cost of this treatment was Rs. 4800/- + taxes and is worth every penny spent. Later, the manager of the spa gave me a Reiki session to relax my mind completely. He held his hand near my head and I could feel a buzzing energy flowing inside my head. The result was less strained neck muscles and a light head.  Will I recommend this to you? Certainly! They might not have been impeccable with my service but they were very good and the overall package was nice. The property is grand and is a feel good factor even before you start with the spa session. I so envy The Club members.  Have you ever been to Antara Spa? What do you think about their Spa services? I am delighted with the opportunity to spread awareness about it,” Vidya said in a statement. “ World Ethnic Day is a concept that came out of the passion and vision of Craftsvilla.com, India’s largest online marketplace for ethnic products.  It is a way to celebrate unique cultures of the world on a single day in unison.”, said Monica Gupta, co-founder Craftsvilla.com. Mumbaigloss was part of the #9wBloggerHunt where I got a chance to choose Nine West India’s best of accessories and shoes from their Spring Summer 2015 collection. The contest gave me an opportunity to shoot at their Palladium store where I chose three products from their SS’15 collection. It was a fun shoot with Fashion Most Wanted team who helped me with the images required for my post. While styling myself for the shoot I had a few things on my mind. I wanted the complete look to be low maintenance yet fun. Summer means outdoors, barbeques, sun dresses, bright colours, florals and wedges. And that is what I aimed to achieve in my style. Yes, I love wedge and platform shoes. Firstly, I find them convenient, especially with a toddler in tow.  I can run behind my toddler in these without many ouch moments. Secondly, they provide height to my petite frame that automatically makes me look leaner and taller. Styling is all about experimenting and presenting oneself confidently in whatever shape or size one might be. So I set myself up for this challenge by choosing the right accessories and shoes from Nine West which were stylish yet comfortable. I love Maxi dresses for the summers and this Guess Maxi dress just gave me the right start to a summer glam look. With a knee high slit and a halter neckline it looked sassy. The floral print in white, blue and pink was perfect to go with my complexion. I chose a white wedge heel and a hot pink clutch to go with it. The white wedge was extremely comfortable to walk. I loved it from the moment I put them on. I think these will look great even with a rolled up denim. The hot pink clutch looked great and had many pockets making it a functional bag to carry quite a lot of stuff including lipstick, mobile phone as well as wet wipes (All the mums can cheer now!). Make up was done by Inglot artists and they used blue and pinks on eyes and lips to complete the look. I am glad they took me out of my comfort zone where I usually try to play safe and used such bright colours to match the dress. It looked sultry but not loud. I was happy with the outcome. Later, I was going through their collection when I spotted these beauties. These platform shoes can be another stylish addition to my wardrobe. These shoes can be easily paired with sun dresses. (Like Amal Clooney who usually wears summer dresses with wedges and platforms). It will give poise and confidence to my strut as I won’t be trying to balance my body weight on them. Ha ha ha! Yes, I am no supermodel who can run a marathon in pencil heels. For me comfort comes first and Nine West shoes provided me exactly what I was looking for – comfort with style. I also loved the summer hues in their bags which varied from light pinks to purples apart from usual monochromes and nudes.  What do you think about my look? Do you like what I am wearing? Do leave a comment below. (Images from various online portals) Like every year, Cannes Film Festival 2015 has also brought us some amazing fashion moments. European tabloids are going gaga over Kendel Jenner’s dress. But to me it was run-of-the-mill stuff. Of course, Kendel Jenner is one of the most searched celebs from the Kardashian clan and even if any member from their family sneezes, it becomes a news. So I wasn’t surprized when her black crop top and skirt (more like Indian ghagra choli) started getting rave reviews. But coming to Indian celebs currently at the French town, Sonam Kapoor tried to take fashion risks this year which just backfired. Her cobalt blue Ralph & Russo dress and the feathery green Elie Saab gown, both were not red carpet favourites. The cobalt blue nearly washed out her complexion making her look sick in few frames. The makeup artist should have paid attention. Though her hair looked fab. Her Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla Black and gold brocade dress was too vintage, yet was eye catching. Fashion is all about experimenting so I can say lady, you haven’t lost it all. Keep trying and next time beat up the fashion blues. (Literally) Katrina Kaif was a first timer so we ought to give her some leeway. Her towering look in red lace Elie Saab with a 10 inch heel didn’t get her any brownie points. It was very orthodox for her age. Or maybe she was adhering to some ‘Kapoor Bahu’ protocols. Her black and beige Oscar De La Renta gown was nothing extraordinary either. The makeup was looking drab as she tried to pull together a Kim Kardashian pale lips and dark eyes look. She looks great in pinks and should have tried something in that colour family. Though I liked her daytime Milly black and white dress. Aishwarya Rai never fails to surprize. Her last few years at Cannes have been anything but boring.  This time she chose a teal Elie Saab gown which was fun and flirty but not classy. I was a bit disappointed with that choice for her red carpet appearance. Moreover, she chose a Sabyasaachi dress for one of her day looks which made her look like a palatial rose garden. The dress made her look older than she is. But later she appeared in more polished looks that made up for that disappointment.  I loved her Ralph & Russo structured white and black gown with embellishments. It had drama, it had class and it looked perfect for a high-octane red carpet event like Cannes Film Festival. I also loved her burgundy Oscar De La Renta gown for the Jazbaa photocall. The colour looked rich and made her appear younger in the backdrop of the French Riviera. No wonder she is still the most sought after celebrity for brand associations. Apart from these Bollywood beauties, Richa Chaddha was seen promoting her movie Masaan, which received a standing ovation at the premier. Sabyasaachi saari looked fabulous on her. Apart from these Bollywood beauties there were many international artists who appeared in astonishingly beautiful and stylish dresses this year. Here is a glimpse of the stylistas who looked fabulous in Cannes 2015 according to me. 1. Li Bing Bing in Zuhair Murad from his Spring Couture collection. Just out from a fairy tale. 2. Rooney Mara and Cate Blanchett in laser cut Alexander McQueen dress and jacket. They epitomise Ying and Yang. 3. Miranda Kerr in Emanuel Ungaro bubble gum pink gown. She looks delicious. 4. Li Bing Bing in Elie Saab gown with pearl details. Class apart. 5. 77 year old Jane Fonda in white suit and statement necklace. Proves age is no bar when it comes to tasteful fashion. 6. Cate Blanchett in black low neck Armani Prive gown with a kimono like broad belt. Poise! 7. UK pop star Cheryl Fernandez Vercini wore a beautiful Ralph & Russo couture dress. Dreamy! 8. Lupita Nyongo wore Gucci jade green gown complete with embroidered crystals and silk flowers. She knows what looks good on her. 9. Doutzen Kroes in cut-out Atelier Versace gown with thigh-high split. Daring and sexy! 10. Cate Blanchett in Giles strapless gown. That Cinderella moment! What do you think about these dresses? Did I miss out on any beautiful dress from Cannes 2015? Rooney Mara and Cate Blanchett in laser cut Alexander McQueen dress and jacket. They epitomise Ying and Yang. 3. Miranda Kerr in Emanuel Ungaro bubble gum pink gown. She looks delicious. 4. Li Bing Bing in Elie Saab gown with pearl details. Class apart. 5. 77 year old Jane Fonda in white suit and statement necklace. Proves age is no bar when it comes to tasteful fashion. 6. Cate Blanchett in black low neck Armani Prive gown with a kimono like broad belt. Poise! 7. UK pop star Cheryl Fernandez Vercini wore a beautiful Ralph & Russo couture dress. Dreamy! 8. Lupita Nyongo wore Gucci jade green gown complete with embroidered crystals and silk flowers. She knows what looks good on her. 9. Doutzen Kroes in cut-out Atelier Versace gown with thigh-high split. Daring and sexy! 10. Cate Blanchett in Giles strapless gown. That Cinderella moment! What do you think about these dresses? Did I miss out on any beautiful dress from Cannes 2015? Leave a comment below. (Images from various online portals) Like every year, Cannes Film Festival 2015 has also brought us some amazing fashion moments. European tabloids are going gaga over Kendel Jenner’s dress. But to me it was run-of-the-mill stuff. Of course, Kendel Jenner is one of the most searched celebs from the Kardashian clan and even if any member from their family sneezes, it becomes a news. So I wasn’t surprized when her black crop top and skirt (more like Indian ghagra choli) started getting rave reviews. But coming to Indian celebs currently at the French town, Sonam Kapoor tried to take fashion risks this year which just backfired. Her cobalt blue Ralph & Russo dress and the feathery green Elie Saab gown, both were not red carpet favourites. The cobalt blue nearly washed out her complexion making her look sick in few frames. The makeup artist should have paid attention. Though her hair looked fab. Her Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla Black and gold brocade dress was too vintage, yet was eye catching. Fashion is all about experimenting so I can say lady, you haven’t lost it all. Keep trying and next time beat up the fashion blues. (Literally) Katrina Kaif was a first timer so we ought to give her some leeway. Her towering look in red lace Elie Saab with a 10 inch heel didn’t get her any brownie points. It was very orthodox for her age. Or maybe she was adhering to some ‘Kapoor Bahu’ protocols. Her black and beige Oscar De La Renta gown was nothing extraordinary either. The makeup was looking drab as she tried to pull together a Kim Kardashian pale lips and dark eyes look. She looks great in pinks and should have tried something in that colour family. Though I liked her daytime Milly black and white dress. Aishwarya Rai never fails to surprize. Her last few years at Cannes have been anything but boring.  This time she chose a teal Elie Saab gown which was fun and flirty but not classy. I was a bit disappointed with that choice for her red carpet appearance. Moreover, she chose a Sabyasaachi dress for one of her day looks which made her look like a palatial rose garden. The dress made her look older than she is. But later she appeared in more polished looks that made up for that disappointment.  I loved her Ralph & Russo structured white and black gown with embellishments. It had drama, it had class and it looked perfect for a high-octane red carpet event like Cannes Film Festival. I also loved her burgundy Oscar De La Renta gown for the Jazbaa photocall. The colour looked rich and made her appear younger in the backdrop of the French Riviera. No wonder she is still the most sought after celebrity for brand associations. Apart from these Bollywood beauties, Richa Chaddha was seen promoting her movie Masaan, which received a standing ovation at the premier. Sabyasaachi saari looked fabulous on her. Apart from these Bollywood beauties there were many international artists who appeared in astonishingly beautiful and stylish dresses this year. Leave a comment below. Mumbaigloss recently spoke to nutritionist Janvi Chitalia (jkchitalia@gmail.com) on the reasons why people leave their diet plans mid-way. Why they do not pursue their weight loss journey till the end? We all have tried to lose weight in different degrees. Some even succeed but only to regain what was lost with a vengeance. Disheartened and discouraged, we leave our efforts to remain fit mid-way. A lot of tips are written around how to lose weight but no one really reflects on why an individual gives up on his/her weight loss journey. The most common reasons for giving up on a program starts from • Lack of motivation • Extreme feeling of deprivation from not eating ones favourite food • The need to fit in socially (whist the rest of the people are eating) • The need to keep ones weight loss effort a secret • Emotional eating • The need to let go and not feel responsible all the time for one’s weight • A sense of overconfidence once the goal is achieved ( to feel that a little out of control eating won’t  harm anyone) So, in effect, weight loss starts with your mind. When you are able to control the negative thoughts and start on a productive journey. Remember, weight loss is a personal goal and you are doing it for yourself, for your own health and no one else. Weight loss will make your feel better, agile and healthy. Self-motivation is the best motivation. To stick to a diet and exercise programme, one should: • Focus on lifestyle change. It is more like a marathon than a sprint.  You should not aim to lose weight as a short term goal for a wedding or birthday. You should make eating healthy and exercising regularly a habit. • Secondly, it is a must to cheat as much as it is to follow the diet. The key is to cheat with a meal of your choice 2 times a week without feeling guilty to keep you motivated. Follow the 80/20 rule. Eat healthy 80 per cent of the time, rest indulge in the 20 per cent of your eating expeditions. • Further, it would help to shift focus on the benefits of health rather than focussing on weight loss goals. A dietary program or a dietary regimen can help increase blood circulation, help in increasing anti-ageing properties in your body, in controlling medical conditions, and reduce stress levels of the body. • Emotional eating can have adverse effects in the long run. Redirecting one’s stress to productive activities is a solution to this problem. Go run, put on some music and dance, go for a spa instead of reaching out for a pack of chips and a bottle of cola. Prepare healthy and fancy food at home like Lebanese salad from quinoa, cous cous with apricots, to satisfy your cravings. • Lapses in the diet are a part of the journey of weight loss. One does not need to pin down or demoralise oneself due to the lapses (inability to follow the diet consistently). The aim is to get back on track immediately once you make an unhealthy choice. It is a good idea to talk to your nutritionist to ask for alternate food which can satisfy your cravings and put you back on the fitness track. Go for herbal teas to take your mind off food. • Support from close friends and family need to be present. They need to exert polite and passive control over the individual on the diet plan rather than assertive control. It will help to motivate the individual for the consistent efforts. • It is important to create awareness for oneself when it comes to food choices but obsessing about it is not the right thing to do. Don’t feel you are being governed. Rather think as a way to enjoy life better. Only good food need not bring you happiness, there are other ways to stimulate your environment. • If you don’t like gym, sign up for Zumba or any other exercise classes of your choice. The idea is to move around, boosting your cardio health and in the process burn calories. • Always keep an eye on your portion size and drink at least 2-3 litres of water. To summarize, make the journey of weight loss as effective as possible even after you have reached your ideal weight and focus on maintenance with the same vigour. A little bit of indulgence is absolutely ok.  You should enjoy good health and good food without any guilt.   Mumbaigloss recently spoke to nutritionist Janvi Chitalia (jkchitalia@gmail.com) on the reasons why people leave their diet plans mid-way. Amy has 21 years of experience in the fashion industry. She draws inspiration from travel with her personal favourites being Bali, Greece, Las Vegas, Switzerland and Turkey. This unique House Of Design is the vision of Designer Amy Billimoria who wanted to create a space housing the best in Design complementing her Pret and Couture label. ABHD houses Nidhi Munim for Swimwear, Jyoti Mukerji for Kids Wear, Meera Mahadevia for Handbags, Aura Art for exclusive art and sculptures, Farzad Billimoria for Headgears and Fascinators, Honey Homes and hair and makeup by Bharat and Dorris. The space designed by architect Farzad Billimoria extends over three levels. Jyoti Mukherjee is wife of Raja Mukherjee (Rani Mukherjee’s brother). In fact, Rani was present for the store opening. She looked gorgeous as ever. Amy Billimoria adds “The success of this design house lies in an ability to unite the best in design and creativity under a single roof.This is my dream to house the crème de la crème in design and create a new luxury niche in the heart of the city.” Location – Amy Billimoria House of Design, Pooja House, Next to Starbucks cafe, Juhu – Mumbai, Time – 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM If you stay near Juhu, do visit the store for some inspiring fashion collection. I personally liked Babita and Bhagyashree’s style. Drape style dresses look so chic on 40 plus women. What do you think?  Leave a comment below.   Mumbaigloss was invited to the most unfake party by Smrinoff last week. It was a pure EDM pleasure and I loved every bit of it.  The stadium was jam-packed with music lovers who were shaking at the international beats. I am glad that Smirnoff started with such a music festival. The company promotes youngsters to enjoy parties intelligently and drink responsibly. This is such a great message for the younger generation. Few celebs like TV actress Barkha Bisht and Kollywood actor Indraneil were seen enjoying the show. Smirnoff Experience, India’s most unfake Electronic Dance Music (EDM) festival is based on the philosophy that Real fun begins with Real People. Smirnoff Experience was launched in 2013 and is set to redefine the festival-going experience for the growing community of dance music lovers in the subcontinent.  Mumbai played host to the second edition of Smirnoff Experience Music Festival- India’s most unfake music extravaganza. The festival, headlined by Australian duo Knife Party and the masked enigma, The Bloody Beetroots, brought together thousands of music lovers at the NSCI Dome in Worli. Those attended were seen dropping the act, shedding all pretenses and enjoying a night of real fun and great music. This mesmeric evening also had performances by renowned Indian artists like Dualist Inquiry, Sandunes, Sound avatar and Kris Correya who set the tone for the evening.  The Neon signboards that echoed the #unfake mantra and the quirky Talking Mirror just added to the theme. The brilliantly designed Eagle stage was a visual treat which further complimented the smashing music at the Smirnoff Experience Music festival.  All in all, this was a party which promised #unfakeit theme, best on music, a visual sensory experience and overall, a real party for the real dance music lovers. Considering the way everyone present shed their pretences and danced the evening away this was one party which lived up to its billing. Enjoyed it thoroughly. Looking forward to the next one already. This mesmeric evening also had performances by renowned Indian artists like Dualist Inquiry, Sandunes, Sound avatar and Kris Correya who set the tone for the evening.  The Neon signboards that echoed the #unfake mantra and the quirky Talking Mirror just added to the theme. The brilliantly designed Eagle stage was a visual treat which further complimented the smashing music at the Smirnoff Experience Music festival.  All in all, this was a party which promised #unfakeit theme, best on music, a visual sensory experience and overall, a real party for the real dance music lovers. Considering the way everyone present shed their pretences and danced the evening away this was one party which lived up to its billing. Enjoyed it thoroughly. Looking forward to the next one already. Mumbaigloss was invited to the most unfake party by Smrinoff last week. It was a pure EDM pleasure and I loved every bit of it.  The stadium was jam-packed with music lovers who were shaking at the international beats. I am glad that Smirnoff started with such a music festival. The company promotes youngsters to enjoy parties intelligently and drink responsibly. This is such a great message for the younger generation. Few celebs like TV actress Barkha Bisht and Kollywood actor Indraneil were seen enjoying the show. Smirnoff Experience, India’s most unfake Electronic Dance Music (EDM) festival is based on the philosophy that Real fun begins with Real People. Smirnoff Experience was launched in 2013 and is set to redefine the festival-going experience for the growing community of dance music lovers in the subcontinent.  Mumbai played host to the second edition of Smirnoff Experience Music Festival- India’s most unfake music extravaganza. The festival, headlined by Australian duo Knife Party and the masked enigma, The Bloody Beetroots, brought together thousands of music lovers at the NSCI Dome in Worli. Those attended were seen dropping the act, shedding all pretenses and enjoying a night of real fun and great music. This mesmeric evening also had performances by renowned Indian artists like Dualist Inquiry, Sandunes, Sound avatar and Kris Correya who set the tone for the evening.  The Neon signboards that echoed the #unfake mantra and the quirky Talking Mirror just added to the theme. The brilliantly designed Eagle stage was a visual treat which further complimented the smashing music at the Smirnoff Experience Music festival.  All in all, this was a party which promised #unfakeit theme, best on music, a visual sensory experience and overall, a real party for the real dance music lovers. Considering the way everyone present shed their pretences and danced the evening away this was one party which lived up to its billing. Enjoyed it thoroughly. Looking forward to the next one already. Ileana is Pond’s White Beauty brand ambassador. And she was caring enough to show some love for Mumbaigloss readers. I asked her a few questions and she was quick to reply. Here are the excerpts from the Q&A session.  MG: Hi Ileana. May I know what is your wardrobe staple? What does fashion mean to you? Ileana: A good pair of denims. They get more comfortable with time. Fashion for me is perfect blend of classy and sexy. LBD’s are an absolute must-have for every girl’s wardrobe. Wear clothes you feel comfortable in and flaunt your best asset. I prefer figure-hugging, sheath dresses as they flatter my body type. MG: That’s excellent. Even I refuse to give up on my favourite pair of denims. What is your good skin secret? Ileana: I realized that treating a problem as soon as it crops up is the best way to ensure your skin will always stay healthy and glowing. Pond’s White Beauty Daily Anti-spot Cream is a product I swear by, ever since I started using it and I’ve noticed a change in my skin! My skin looks radiant and has a natural spot-less glow.  MG: Seriously? You use Pond’s products for your skin? What else do you recommend for a good skin. Ileana: Drink lots of water and at every opportunity. Water is a miracle worker! So drink as much as you can every day, just as you moisturize your skin every day. Maintain a healthy lifestyle, drink lots of water, clean your skin and moisturize it using the right products. Wow, thank you Ileana for the quick tips. Readers of Mumbaigloss, what do you think about these tips? Do leave a comment below. Ileana is Pond’s White Beauty brand ambassador. Protibha from Mumbaigloss went to experience #BringHairAlive, hair spa treatment by Himalaya Herbals last weekend. With hair problems like breaking, splitting, dryness at the ends, dry scalp, etc. I wasn’t sure how this was going to help.  Usually, ayurvedic products are considered mild and without any side effects so I thought there was no harm in giving it a try.  Once I reached Asif Salon in Lokhandwala, I spoke to the concerned hair specialists about my problems. The hair specialist assessed my tresses and said that there was no dandruff and a bit of hair-fall was natural. Later, he suggested that to counter the dryness in the hair and scalp, I should regularly use, hair oil or hair cream to provide moisture to the hair shaft. He said that I should wash my hair with mild shampoo and moisturising conditioner. I took down the useful tips and eventually my hair treatment started.  Hair specialist first applied the Anti – Hair Fall oil to the roots of my hair and scalp with soaked cotton ensuring that my entire head received the oil treatment. The oil contains Bhringraaj and Amlaki which promote growth of hair.  In my childhood, my mother would ask me to wash my hair with Amla and Reetha for better hair. Now those age-old recipes have been sealed in a bottle by Himalaya Herbals. The oil is supposed to nourish the roots and help with scalp moisturisation. It is non-sticky so it can be applied daily. After applying the oil, he started with the head massage which was relaxing and invigorating. Head massage increases blood circulation to the roots as well as helps in product penetration in the hair shaft. Post head massage, I was taken for a hair wash. My hair was washed thoroughly with Anti-Hair Fall shampoo to remove every trace of the oil from the body of the hair. This was done to remove any dirt and impurities which was in my hair and scalp.  Once my hair was towel dried, it was divided into sections and Anti-Hair Fall Protein Cream was applied to the scalp and hair. The hair specialist slowly covered my entire hair with the cream section by section. Again, I received a little head massage which felt very relaxing. My hair was twisted and put up in a bun.  Steam was given to my treated hair so that the protein rich cream penetrated the hair shaft completely giving it a glossy and healthy look. After 15-20 minutes of the steam application, I was taken for another head wash where Anti-Hair Fall shampoo and Protein rich conditioner were used to wash my hair. Finally, my hair was blow-dried and styled. The first thing that I noticed about my hair was that it looked glossy and felt soft. It smelled great.  Stylist from Himalaya Herbals also said that the hair cream can be used both as a mask as well as a styling cream. And it costs only Rs. 100 for 100 ml. The best thing is that the products are affordable but give excellent results. Natural ingredients like China Rose, Chick Pea, Oats, Lotus, Amlaki, Bhringraaj, Licorice, and several other herbs have been used to create this hair-care range. It’s like I am getting products which my mother would have recommended me to use for nourished hair. I would recommend these products to those who want lustrous, shiny, black hair the natural way. Press Release: “The Vintage Affair” – a fashion and accessory brands exhibition powered by Angels Network, which  will showcase second hand and new stylish and branded apparel, bags and glasses amongst many other things at extremely affordable prices ! A new and an unheard concept of exhibiting second hand and few new fashion pieces, has been launched, not just with the intention of selling some unused stuff lying in our wardrobes, but the concept is driven by spirit and enthusiasm of over 50  motivated women , who feel that not only there is a market for second hand branded labels, but also by participating in this exhibition, the donors and the sellers would be doing some good to the society  as all the funds raised at this exhibition are going to be used for building a new home for the homeless and abandoned elderly at Earth Saviours Foundation, an internationally recognised NGO in Delhi. The proceeds of the chairty sale will be given to  Karma Yogi  Ravi Kalra. The earlier home in Vasant Kunj was burnt down in a fire last year. A Vintage Affaire to be held in #1, Under Defence Colony Flyover Market, formerly Nirulas on April 17th(12:00 pm to 7 pm) and April 18th 2015 ( 11:00 am to 7 pm), will showcase bags & clutches, shoes, scarfs, sun glasses, clothes including Indian and Western wear for women, men and children from luxury brands such as Bottega, Gucci, Christian Dior, Fendi, YSL and high street brands, Zara, Mango, Promod and the best part would be that all which would be on display would be original and filtered by the team from The Angel Network to ensure that all products on display are in extremely good and usable condition. The catch at the exhibition  would surely be the outfits by Rabani and Raaka, Nikhil and Shantanu, Raw Mango, Preetika Swarup, Elisha W, Renge Style among others who believe in the work being done by The Angels Network and thus have come forward and have donated some of their last season stock for this exhibition. Some of the other hottest picks to watch out for are: Fashion labels like Raw Mango, Rabani and Raaka, Nikhil and Shantanu, Preetika Swarup, Elisha W, Renee Style will rule the weekend at A Vintage Affaire. Drop by if you wish to own these coveted brands at up to one tenth the price. What do you think about second hand fashion? Do leave a comment below. On April 7th, Mumbaigloss witnessed a never before seen talent show at BlueFrog, Lower Parel, in Mumbai. BlueFrog stage saw the final leg of India’s first digital mentorship program, The Step Up by Johnnie Walker. After a thrilling journey of four weeks, the platform culminated into a stunning Johnnie Walker-inspired evening where nine talented participants showcased their talent in the presence of their mentors Nikhil Thampi, Nikhil Chibb and Midival Pundits duo Gaurav Raina and Tapan Raj. Only nine aspirants from across India made it through the elimination rounds and were guided to sharpen their skills and undertake an inspirational journey packed with rigorous training and tough challenges, by mentors Nikhil Chib, Nikhil Thampi and the MIDIval Punditz. From pop-up restaurants to celebrity styling to creation of original tracks with limited instruments, this unique platform brought alive the dreams of nine talented individuals to do their best. Anusha Dandekar hosted the show gracefully and looked lovely in her red gown and Jadau neckpiece. The event culminated with the announcement of three winners who took The Step Up and will now go on to realize their dreams in their chosen fields. The winners are Srikar Shetty (food), Viraj Mohan (Music) and Rishika Jain (fashion). They will now enjoy a six month apprenticeship with Nikhil Thampi and Nikhil Chib, respectively. The best performer in music will set off on an exclusive four-city tour with Midival Punditz. Now how many 20 somethings get such an opportunity? I am really happy for the trio. Speaking about the splendid grand finale, Mr. Bhavesh Somaya, Head of Luxury, United Spirits Limited – a Diageo Group Company said “The Step Up is a reflection of the Johnnie Walker philosophy that encourages individuals to take the next big step and move forward in life. This mentorship program has helped us create a strong platform for aspiring young adults in the fields of food, fashion and music to further enhance their skills and prepare them to STEP UP in the pursuit of their passions. Our aim is to nurture and promote these abled mentees and direct them on the path of progress and excellence.” The series were written and directed by famous theatre and TV actor Divya Palat for her production house Balancing Act Productions. I used to love her in Captain Vyom as Dr. Zen. For those who are not aware, Captain Vyom was India’s first sci-fi series in the 90’s. I saw Vivan Bhatena with wife Nikhila Bhatena (who is Divya’s sister) and several other celebs like Kunal Vijaykar, Sumona Chakravarti (Comedy Nights with Kapil fame), Miss Malini and her husband Naushad enjoying the show. This was a good platform for young and talented people. If you guys are interested, you should apply next time for this online talent hunt. You never know you might be the next winner of #TheStepUp. BlueFrog stage saw the final leg of India’s first digital mentorship program, The Step Up by Johnnie Walker. After a thrilling journey of four weeks, the platform culminated into a stunning Johnnie Walker-inspired evening where nine talented participants showcased their talent in the presence of their mentors Nikhil Thampi, Nikhil Chibb and Midival Pundits duo Gaurav Raina and Tapan Raj. Only nine aspirants from across India made it through the elimination rounds and were guided to sharpen their skills and undertake an inspirational journey packed with rigorous training and tough challenges, by mentors Nikhil Chib, Nikhil Thampi and the MIDIval Punditz. From pop-up restaurants to celebrity styling to creation of original tracks with limited instruments, this unique platform brought alive the dreams of nine talented individuals to do their best. Anusha Dandekar hosted the show gracefully and looked lovely in her red gown and Jadau neckpiece. What do you all think? Do leave a comment below. Mumbaigloss has always loved fitness related topics. More so when I personally feel the need to indulge in activities which will help me remain fit and are fun to do. So I recently downloaded this free app Dance With Madhuri (DWM) on my android phone. It is available on IOS as well. This app is an extension to her online dance academy with the same name.  The app was launched in 2013.  But when I downloaded the app it was showing only 50 downloads on Google store. Though, old news portals quoted that more than 10000 downloads were done for the app. I believe that the app was re-launched recently. User Interface is pretty attractive for the new version of the app. So I thought, let me download it and see what it has in store for me. Moreover, what could be better than learning Bollywood thumkas from the dancing diva herself? Dance with Madhuri app, asks you to login with either Facebook, Google or requests you to create a new login ID. The app doesn’t post on FB automatically so it is ok to login with Facebook. After login it takes you to a page where you can choose among two buttons Quick start (which takes you to the list of options) and Surprise Me (Where a random clip or dance lesson is chosen for you). For me most of the random selections were done for fitness dance classes reminding me that I need to get in shape. (Evil grin!) Once you select Quick start, it takes you to a list of dance options. For example you can learn to dance for a wedding, Navratri, Club Party, Audition, etc. Once you click on each of these tabs, it takes you to a list of relevant dance lesson clips. From Ghagra to Tamma Tamma to Batameez Dil, you can learn to dance on these popular numbers through this app. The dance lessons are divided into brief one and a half minute sections so that you can learn at your own pace and pay attention to details.  Not only that, you can learn various dance forms like Bollywood, Indian Classical like Kathak and Bharatnatyam, Folk, Latin & Ballroom including Tango and Salsa, Contemporary, Street Dancing, etc. with this free app. Each section has videos from dance experts who will take you through step-by-step process of learning that dance form. The app also lists jobs with DWM, institutes where you can enrol for dance classes near your home, events, contests, etc. You can also record your performance and upload on the app forum for voting from users across the world. I just saw a Russian lady dance impeccably on the song ‘Chane Ke Khet mein’. Absolutely mind blowing!  The lessons are very informative and easy. They come without any adverts which is the best part. So you can learn dancing from anywhere without having to invest in time or money. Professionals who are short of time can take part in Dancercise where you can burn almost 350 calories in a 25 minute session without going to a gym or a fitness class. Isn’t that great? (But it doesn’t mean I am allowed to eat aaloo paranthas after that. Just a thought!) It also, includes dance fitness moves to help you with body conditioning, core strengthening and stretching, to get you fit and healthy.  The app is not snag free though. At times manoeuvring to different sections by a novice might seem difficult. The app stops working if you make quick selections and the video becomes pixelated sometimes. It might be due to improper internet buffering. But all in all, it is a good app for the dance and fitness lovers. So, people who are looking for some fitness motivation should download this app. You will certainly enjoy learning with Madhuri Dixit and dance gurus like Terrence Lewis, Remo D’Souza, etc. The app has been endorsed by celebs like Priyanka Chopra, Salman Khan, Ranbir Kapoor, Saroj Khan, Pt. Birju Maharaj and the likes.  Download this app if you love dancing. Do let me know what do you think about it? Leave your comments below. Mumbaigloss has always loved fitness related topics. Mumbaigloss was trying to figure out the latest trends in shoes when it occurred to us that why not explore the comfort shoe section. I know many people love their Crocs and refuse to come out of them so are their any such brands which provide high quality comfort to the wearers. And then, we came to know about Scentra, a niche shoe brand which develops comfortable walking shoes for men, women as well as children.  Scentra, is India’s first scented shoe brand so next time you take off your shoes around friends and family, no one will excuse themselves away to escape the odor or smelly feet.  These are comfortable canvas shoes made from 100 per cent organic cotton a certified orthopedic sole and a strawberry scented insole (to keep you smelling as good as you look). These shoes are foldable and can fit into any nook of the luggage without any hassle. It is specifically designed to fulfil the gap in the footwear industry between the necessary formal and casual sports shoes and I am glad someone thought that way for people who want slip on comfortable shoes with their denims or casual wears instead of heeled or sports shoes. These are ideal for traveling or for those who love to walk.  The spring summer collection of the brand boasts of a vibrant diverse mix of prints and colors. From the fun floral and animal prints, to bright textures to eclectic embroidery.This season animal prints and subtle multi coloured flowers are going to make their debut on women’s canvas shoes. While the collection for men will go old school with camouflage fabrics. The outsoles get a facelift and have become thicker giving the men’s collection a robust and better look. In addition, Scentra is introducing two tone prints where it will have a luxurious blend of embroidery and bold colours. You can check out the collection here. It is also available at Jabong.com. The price starts from Rs. 2500 onwards. Don’t think that canvas shoes cannot be paired with trendy clothes. Here is a look-book for you to refer.  What do you think about these scented shoes? On one hand the event got over successfully bringing forth few talented designers and their designs to the industry and on the other hand it saddened a few as many fashion designers repackaged the old and didn’t innovate something new. Satya Paul by Gauri khan was a big let-down. The collection was based on tropical plants but was very run of the mill and average. I feel Gauri Khan should have taken time to dwell on this collection. But let me not mull over it now. I hope the next season has some great designs and fashion ideas which can be implemented at a large scale. Here are my picks of top 11 dresses that I would want to wear as my everyday fashion staple. These have been presented during this fashion week and this list will help you choose the trendiest ensembles for yourself, next time you go shopping. 1. Neha Agarwal is definitely my favourite designer this season. Her dresses are trendy and very much wearable off the ramp. The bright prints of Russian Babooshka dolls and florals just made these dresses look so interesting. The base colours remain pastels which is ideal for summers.  2. Another Neha Agarwal dress that I would love to wear is the one recently worn by actor Tapasee Pannu. This has bright prints and happy colours. The lemon yellow is oh-so-summery. The floor grazing asymmetric hemline makes it stand out from the crowd.  3. This tiled bird print dress by Mandira Bedi is another favourite of mine. It is light, airy and has beautiful interplay of pastel and bright colours. The net detail at the collarbone area adds to its appeal. Ideal for summer brunch. It looks sporty-chic and well-toned arms can be easily flaunted in this dress.  4. Suneet Varma’s flowy massive anarkali in a deep purple colour with golden gota work just blew mind away. The net arms with floral embroidery for the blouse makes it a good summer evening wear. This looks so chic in Indian wear segment.  5. Another Suneet Varma dress which I would like to wear is this little number that has floral print with beautiful mirror work on it. The western wear inspired by the gorgeous traditional motifs and crafts of Gujarat and Rajasthan makes it look special.  6. The Pankaj and Nidhi dress is a good option if you want to look polished for a summer afternoon. The light fabric jacket and skirt in traditional Iznik pottery of Turkey, looks fresh and can be easily adapted from a day to night look.  7. VERANDAH BY ANJALI showcased fusion of edgy and soft, shapes and florals on a light background. This jumpsuit from the collection is very good for summer evenings. Throw in a light denim jacket to this jumpsuit to add some drama.  8. Divya Sheth’s coat dresses can be added to the list of power dressing. Well-tailored coat dresses made with light fabrics in military shades can look neat for a summer evening. Hopefully, the muted earthy prints make them look different from parkas.  9. This dress made from mulmul, a light and soft fabric was presented during Harper Bazaar’s textile show and has all the elements to make it a glamorous choice for a summer wear. I loved its intricate cut work.  10. This abstract print dress by Quirkbox is one of my favourites. It is light, it is bright. The crop top and long skirt combo is ideal for summer months.  11. The Harper Bazaar’s textile show also presented this dress which isn’t unique but is definitely beautiful and spells summer comfort and elegance. I would definitely like to wear this.  Manish has used intricate thread work, mirroring the Parsi gara, on soft and flowing fabrics for his collection The Blue Fashion Runway presented by WEvolve. The Blue Fashion Runway represented fashion for a cause promoting a global social message of gender equality and prevention of gender based violence. This display of fashion for a cause left everyone awestruck!  The outfits are highlighted with jewellery by Anmol Jewellers. The colour palette this season is dominated by hues of blue from powder to midnight, with bold touches of variations of yellow reflecting the promise of a bright future.  The women’s line includes summer flowy gowns, jacket-saris, off shoulder and halter crop tops and skirts as an ode to the lehenga, with embroidery giving a 3D effect to light fabrics. And men’s line has bandh-galas in light fabrics and flowy silhouettes.  I just loved the generous use of tassels and off shoulders in his new collection. It has added the fun element to the entire collection. Many Bollywood celebs attended the show to support the cause like Kajol, Deepika Padukone, SriDevi, and Jacqueline Fernandez among others. But Kapoor sisters were missed at the event. For the first time in Manish’s association with LFW, the show was organised offsite in the old world ambiance of the Great Eastern Home – a sprawling home décor store featuring unique and worldly furniture. I have been to this store and it spells magic for the people who love vintage home décor. Manish personally chose this venue to present his collection. What do you think about his new collection? During Lakme Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2015, day 1 saw launch of Sculpt range of beauty products from Lakme as well as launch of India’s first ever real-time makeup app called Makeup Pro. The show curated by Lakmé expert Natasha Nischol and Lakmé’s face Shraddha Kapoor played the muse.  Natasha brought alive various art forms in makeup looks – inspired by Sculpt – including etching, bronze, mosaic, clay and paint. Later, Lakmé’s revolutionary Makeup Pro App was launched. The app claims to be a real-time virtual makeover app with complete palette of shades and looks across the Lakmé portfolio. From prepping the skin to applying makeup, this app lets you try how each product looks   on you digitally. Lakmé’s prostylist looks created by makeup experts, including the look that Shraddha sported on the runway today, is the highlight of the app.  You can simply try the look in a single click.  “In our 15th year at Lakme Fashion Week, we reinvent make-up – presenting it as avant garde looks, in line with fashion.  The new hi-definition matte lipstick is the star of the Lakme Absolute Sculpt line – our trend forecast at Lakme Fashion Week for this season. Taking it one step further, we empower every Indian woman to experience this beauty trend first hand with the first of its’ kind – Lakmé Makeup Pro app. A true revolution in the world of makeup, this real-timeMakeup Pro app promises to be the biggest blockbuster in beauty and we are absolutely thrilled to bring it to all makeup lovers all over the country”, said Purnima Lamba, Head of Innovation at Lakmé.  “Makeup Pro is an amazing app and I simply love experimenting with my favourite looks. Every time I have 5 min free during shoots, this is what I am using! It is extremely user friendly and helps me select colors and styles that compliment me, in an instant. I also love how I have access to all the Lakmé makeup right on my fingertips.” said Lakmé face Shraddha Kapoor. So, I decided to give it a try and therefore downloaded it on my phone today. This approx. 38 MB file took almost 15 minutes to download on my 3G connection. I don’t know if it will be faster with a wi-fi. Once the app was installed it wasn’t difficult to login as I logged in with Facebook credentials. The app doesn’t publish on Facebook automatically which is a good thing. Once you log in to the app, on the left hand corner is a drop down box which lists saved looks, tutorial, details about the app, privacy policy, etc. The app automatically opens in a mirror like screen where it asks to click a self-portrait in a good light condition to get real-time makeup suggestions. You can choose to ask your friend to click a good picture by reversing the camera settings with a click. You can also upload an old picture from your phone folders, facebook album, etc.   So I decided to use my old picture to get Lakme Makeup Pro suggestions. As soon as I uploaded my image, the scanner tried to map my face and a pop up appeared to highlight my eye, eyebrow and lip area. It asked if the smile was showing any teeth. With a swipe the dots were adjusted and I was ready for a digital makeover. The palette of options appeared for face, eyes, skin, lips and Pro Makeup makeovers. As and when I touched each of the options, further options appeared. For example lips opened a wheel of shades for lipstick as well as lip-gloss. The app also allows to control the intensity of the product applied which helps in getting realistic results. Low setting was always better. I had a lot of fun trying out various shades of eye liners, lip-glosses, eye-shadows, etc.  But when I decided to try the readymade Pro Makeup makeovers/looks. It was a disaster. The makeup looked so cakey and unreal. There is no way you can control the set colours in the readymade makeovers and most of the designed looks made me look like a ghost. I wanted to look like Kareena though. Doesn’t my face remind you of the ghost from the Grudge series? Jokes apart, I think these readymade settings are not convenient at all as one look cannot fit all.  Anyway, I decided to get back to the manual makeover session. Once the desired adjustments were made in my manual makeover journey, I was ready to lock and save that look. The app allows you to compare the before and after look. Once you are completely satisfied then you can save your look which stays in a folder in the app for as long as you want. If you are not happy with something, you can always delete it. The app suggests all the Lakme products used to create the look and gives you an option to put them in a cart and buy directly through the app. How cool is that.  I recently tried another beauty app called Perfect365 and found it better in terms of face mapping and makeover options. But as Lakme Makeup Pro App is trying to promote their own products so they cannot have a gamut of looks or colour palettes to try on their app. The app hangs sometimes and takes time to load a few pictures. It has been downloaded a little over 100 times and has a long way to go before it become the most sought after beauty app in the Indian market. Still, I feel it is a good attempt by the Lakme India team and certainly looks promising. So fashionistas, you can rejoice as apps like these will make your beauty life seamless, or rather perfect. Now no need to waste your money on wrong products. You can try them digitally before buying. What do you think about this app? Do leave a comment below.
