Last week was pretty busy for Mumbaigloss as it attended India International Jewellery Week (IIJW) 2014 between 14-17July at Grand Hyatt, Mumbai. This once a year show is the most awaited by the Indian gems and jewellery industry as top designers and companies showcase their craft to the masses. This year there were many celeb show stoppers such as Parineeti Chopra, Sridevi, Shraddha Kapoor, Sunny Leone, Raveena Tandon, Kalki Koechlin, Yami Gautam, Esha Gupta, Neha Dhupia, Amisha Patel, etc. adding the oomph factor to IIJW 2014. The closing ceremony was presented by Bipasha Basu and IIJW brand ambassador Sonam Kapoor. No one can beat Sonam Kapoor when it comes to making a style statement. But apart from her, the ones who created immense flutter for the shutterbugs are my top 5 showstoppers from the event.  1. Director/actor/model Divya Khosla of T-Series and Yaarian fame stopped the show with her electrifying entry wearing a grand three-strand pearl necklace and a diamond choker, lace cuffs and rings for PN Gadgil. She created a look like Katy Perry and was extremely playful on the ramp. She might not be regular on the runway but she certainly stirred a lot of interest.  2. Chitrangada Singh, Bollywood’s glamorous diva made a lovely showstopper for Moni Agarwal presented by Solitaire Gemological Laboratories. She looked beautiful in her desi avatar. Her nose ring garnered a lot of fan following; a new trend, which we might soon see on the high-street fashion radar. She walked the ramp wearing a dazzling Raani Haar, studded diamond collar, intricate cummerbund, nose ring, Haath Phool and bracelet from the collection.  3. Sridevi was the showstopper for Golecha Jewels and looked ethereal in her Indian attire. The evergreen actress walked the ramp wearing a regal diamond Raani Haar with a grand square gleaming pendant, matching earrings, bracelet and ring. Vijay and Rupali Golecha couldn’t have found a better showstopper for their collection which is a good balance between vintage and modern.  4. In the grand finale, Best–of–the–best, stunning Bipasha Basu closed the show for PC Jewellers. She wore a luxurious green embroidered net lehenga/ maroon blouse and modelled a gorgeous polki Raani Haar, shoulder dusters, bangles and an impressive cocktail ring. She looked like a “queen” in her own words.  5. Sunny Leone opened the show for Apala by Sumit Sawhney to showcase his collection ‘The Royal Tribe’ in an opulent Victorian neckpiece with elements of the Hasli with gold claws adding the tribal touch to it. Bringing extra drama was the rear piece with an amazing wreath effect in jade along with beautiful anklets and head piece.  Raveena Tandon and Kalki Koechlin were also impressive. Who do you think was the best showstopper at IIJW 2014? Leave a comment below. She walked the ramp wearing a dazzling Raani Haar, studded diamond collar, intricate cummerbund, nose ring, Haath Phool and bracelet from the collection.  3. Sridevi was the showstopper for Golecha Jewels and looked ethereal in her Indian attire. The evergreen actress walked the ramp wearing a regal diamond Raani Haar with a grand square gleaming pendant, matching earrings, bracelet and ring. Vijay and Rupali Golecha couldn’t have found a better showstopper for their collection which is a good balance between vintage and modern.  4. In the grand finale, Best–of–the–best, stunning Bipasha Basu closed the show for PC Jewellers. She wore a luxurious green embroidered net lehenga/ maroon blouse and modelled a gorgeous polki Raani Haar, shoulder dusters, bangles and an impressive cocktail ring. She looked like a “queen” in her own words.  5. Sunny Leone opened the show for Apala by Sumit Sawhney to showcase his collection ‘The Royal Tribe’ in an opulent Victorian neckpiece with elements of the Hasli with gold claws adding the tribal touch to it. Bringing extra drama was the rear piece with an amazing wreath effect in jade along with beautiful anklets and head piece.  Raveena Tandon and Kalki Koechlin were also impressive. Last week was pretty busy for Mumbaigloss as it attended India International Jewellery Week (IIJW) 2014 between 14-17July at Grand Hyatt, Mumbai. This once a year show is the most awaited by the Indian gems and jewellery industry as top designers and companies showcase their craft to the masses. This year there were many celeb show stoppers such as Parineeti Chopra, Sridevi, Shraddha Kapoor, Sunny Leone, Raveena Tandon, Kalki Koechlin, Yami Gautam, Esha Gupta, Neha Dhupia, Amisha Patel, etc. adding the oomph factor to IIJW 2014. The closing ceremony was presented by Bipasha Basu and IIJW brand ambassador Sonam Kapoor. No one can beat Sonam Kapoor when it comes to making a style statement. But apart from her, the ones who created immense flutter for the shutterbugs are my top 5 showstoppers from the event.  1. Director/actor/model Divya Khosla of T-Series and Yaarian fame stopped the show with her electrifying entry wearing a grand three-strand pearl necklace and a diamond choker, lace cuffs and rings for PN Gadgil. She created a look like Katy Perry and was extremely playful on the ramp. She might not be regular on the runway but she certainly stirred a lot of interest.  2. The bloggers meet called #DateWithDiamonds was arranged in association with Mumbaigloss.in. The event was a grand success. The bloggers found this visit very informative and entertaining as they also got to witness the process of how jewellery is made in the adjoining factory. They also got a chance to wear, touch and feel the new collection which was equally enthralling to them. The bloggers received exclusive silver pendants and crystal pens from Kama as a token of appreciation for their participation at the event. The new collection which I would like to call ‘Imara’ is for strong women. Imara means strong or resolute. The statement neckpieces, rings and earrings are for someone who loves attention and knows how to handle such attention. It is for the empowered women. The use of yellow and white diamonds in the bold geometrical designs is absolutely stunning. Yellow diamonds create the illusion as if the wearer has the brightness of the sun, beauty of the marigold and glow of the turmeric. Am I going overboard? Well, it’s just that I can’t contain my excitement after wearing those beauties. The collection has a modern day appeal and can be worn with both modern and traditional wear. The collection uses Asscher, Emerald and Cushion cut diamonds that are set in 18kt white and yellow gold to accentuate the sparkle of the white and yellow diamonds. My favourite from the collection is a necklace made with a string of cushion cut diamonds. That piece is simple yet absolutely stunning. It is a perfect accessory to a gown or monochrome maxi dress. It spells class and elegance. I also loved the bracelet which has big yellow cushion cut diamonds. It would certainly steal a few envying glances. I have worked with GIA in the past and I can pretty much say on the basis of my experience that the quality of stones used and the setting in the jewellery is of good quality. Imara, as I would like to call it, is a collection for everybody. It has smaller pendant and earring sets as well which is perfect for a working woman. Be it corporate trainings or client meetings, the smaller sets are graceful and attractive. Kama Jewellery also has finance facilities for its customers. So, if you are looking to invest in a timeless piece then this collection should give you ample of choices. For more information about the collection please visit http://www.kamaschachter.com/   Pearls are elegant, classic and versatile. Be it ball gowns or boyfriend jeans, they can be worn with anything and on any occasion. The earliest mention of pearl in ornaments has been found in scriptures dating back to the ancient Pandyan dynasty that was a (pre-Christian era) Tamil dynasty. Later on, pearls became a hit in the European market.  Not only queens, even actresses and elite class wore pearls regularly. I am sure everyone remembers Audrey Hepburn wearing strings of pearl with her LBD (Little Black Dress) in the famous movie Breakfast At Tiffany’s. Her look has gone into the pages of fashion history as the most iconic look of all times.  Mumbaigloss decided to talk to Mira Gulati, founder and designer of Mirari to know more about this beautiful gemstone and how to care for pearl jewellery. The hard lustrous object formed with the soft tissues of a living shelled mollusc like an Oyster, are called Pearls. Pearls are the latest throb in the jewellery circuit. Its elegant glow is evident to make a spoil for choices and they are the genre of new arriving trend in the jewellery market. The most valuable pearls occur in the wild, and are extremely rare. Whether wild or cultured, pearls occur in different sizes and across a splendid variety. On a broad scale there are majorly 5 types of Pearls that exist in the market, namely, Akoya, South Sea, Fresh Water, Tahitian and Basra Pearls. They are found in the following shapes: baroque, button, coin, tear drop, dome, blister, round, nugget, oval, potato, rice, etc. Akoya: Known for its lustre, these saltwater pearls, mostly used for designing necklaces are generally white or cream-colored. Persisting to a round shape, they are exclusively produced in Japan. South Sea: South Sea pearls have several distinct characteristics that are unique to this gem. South Sea pearls have a unique, satiny lustre that comes from the rapidly deposited nacre and warm waters of the South Seas. South Sea pearls also have a subtle array of colors; typically white, silver and golden, that is rare in other pearl types. Fresh Water: They are grown in pearl farms created by using freshwater mussels, and are known for its rich texture and high-end finish and these are majorly produced in China. Quality of cultured freshwater pearls is evaluated through a grading system of a series of values, based on lustre, shape, surface, colour, etc. Tahitian: The Tahitian (or black pearl) is an organic gem formed from the black lip oyster. Tahitian pearl comes in various shapes, sizes, and colours. Because of their darker hues, Tahitian pearls are commonly known as “black pearls”. However, Tahitian pearls have the ability to contain various undertones and overtones of green, pink, blue, silver and yellow. All (or any combination) of these colours may be seen in a cultured Tahitian pearl. Due to the variety of shapes and colours of the Tahitian pearl, it has been known to fit in any jewellery setting. The versatility and mixture of colour give it its value. Basra: The Basra pearls are a highly valued and treasured species. These pearls have a featured in recorded history as far back in time as 300BC. Most are characterised by irregular shape and a yellowish tint. Some have a distinctly pinkish tint too. Natural Basra pearls, especially undrilled one is silvery-white colour and round/spherical shape is rare and extremely precious. Care for your Pearls: Pearls are the most fragile set of jewel pieces invented for crafting adornments. Their surface gets scratched easily. Pearl Jewelleries being delicate in nature deserves a lot of maintenance. Keeping them away from the normal set of jewelleries while storing them is always a better option. A soft velvet bag or a separate section in one’s jewellery box is the perfect place to shelter the pearl items.  Always wear them after you apply any makeup to make pearl lustre last longer. Spray perfume before you put on any pearl jewellery. Gently wipe your pearls with a soft cloth after you remove them for the day. Immediately wipe your pearls clean with a soft cloth if they get exposed to any acid (sweat, perfume, fruit juice, vinegar etc.) Thank you Mira for giving us a low down on how to keep our pearls bright and beautiful! I am sure our readers can apply these tips to keep their pearl jewellery in good shape.  Pearls are elegant, classic and versatile. It came beautifully packed in a cloth bag and had a small note about the product. It claims that in three washes the split ends would disappear by up to 96 per cent. Why did I opt to review this product? Because the ends of my hair are dry due to years of abuse. (Read colouring, streaking, straightening, etc.) And I wanted to check how this shampoo and conditioner duo can make my tresses better. My hair is fine, wavy with medium volume. Shampoo price: Rs. 80 for 90ml, Rs. 215 for 170ml and Rs. 349 for 600ml Conditioner price: Rs. 80 for 90ml & Rs. 179 for 215ml After using it religiously for a week (I used it thrice) here are my observations: Pros: • Hair felt soft, shiny and less frizzy • Hair was manageable • Dry ends didn’t disappear but looked and felt softer • Scalp was less dry and itchy • From price point, shampoo and conditioner are affordable • Good fruity fragrance Cons: • Hair was weighed down due to silicon and looked volume less • Scalp felt oily within 48 hours after shampoo Verdict: It is good for women who have head full of frizzy hair. It is a tool to tame your manes if they refuse to obey the laws of gravitation. On a serious note, if you have wavy to curly hair with good volume then this product is ideal for you. For people like me who have fine, wavy, medium volume hair may find it flattening. Straight hair girls may try it if they have good volume. But does it do anything to your split ends? Umm well, not really other than making them appear softer. Life hack: Use a volumising spray after the shampoo like 24 Hour Body Foaming Mousse by Tresemme to get some volume. Though, it costs Rs. 1500/- approx. and might not be pocket friendly. Rating: 3.5/5 I received samples of Tressme Split Remedy Shampoo and Conditioner 2 months back (through Indiblogger). It came beautifully packed in a cloth bag and had a small note about the product. It claims that in three washes the split ends would disappear by up to 96 per cent. Why did I opt to review this product? Because the ends of my hair are dry due to years of abuse. (Read colouring, streaking, straightening, etc.) And I wanted to check how this shampoo and conditioner duo can make my tresses better. My hair is fine, wavy with medium volume. Though, it costs Rs. 1500/- approx. and might not be pocket friendly. Rating: 3.5/5 My OH has been complaining off late that I spend too much time on my smart phone. Can I help it? May be not! Apart from social networking, blogging, etc.; I also search for quick fashion fixes whenever I am going out. In fact, Whatsapp has become my go-to app. If I am confused between two shoes, I ping my sister with the images to get her opinion. The Whatsapp groups I have joined keep on buzzing with what’s in and out of trend. And that’s not all. Many a times I have a quick chat with my mum regarding what will look better on me. (If I should wear a pink or a deep red lipstick with gold brocades saree).  That’s when I thought, which are the fashion apps available in the Android market that can be helpful to a fashion enthusiast like me? After a few downloads and testing, I could list these: 1. Trendabl (Social Networking for fashionistas): It is like Instagram and Facebook for the fashion freaks who would love to network with other fashionistas around the world. Upload a photo, filter it and tag it to allow users to browse photos by categories such as skirts, swimwear, or shoes. With Trendabl you can tag what you’re wearing based on label, price and availability. You can also browse others’ outfits and get some style inspiration. 2. The Womens Store (shopping app organizer and memory saver): A fashionista always wants to get the best deals on the most trending clothes and accessories and for that she needs to visit various online stores. But downloading each and every app of these online stores is plain cumbersome and will consume your mobile data and storage space. That is when you can download The Womens Store. This app is your shopping app organizer. Rather than downloading each and every app of your favourite store and cluttering your mobile top, you can simply download this one and then visit various stores as and when required. American Swan, Fashion and You, Jabong, Myntra, Fashionara, Provogue, Yebhi, Zivame, Koovs and a lot more online stores have been linked through this app. Apart from shopping; it also lists sites for food, travel, jewellery, books, etc. You can also get some fashion inspiration from these sites. And in case, you thought that you will miss out on the deal alerts, then this app also lists promotional emails where you can keep a tab on the sales and promotions happening across these sites. 3. Styledotme (Network, create timed polls): Meghna Saraogi is the founder of this app, who like us was always confused while shopping. Sometimes, friend’s opinion becomes very important while purchasing an accessory worth thousands and that’s when this app comes handy. You can upload images of two products and create an instant poll. The poll can be further enhanced with a timer (Like I need advice in the next five minutes) and then your friends can quickly give their vote. You can also add image-enhancing filters to your photos and share your posts with your friends on Facebook and Twitter. You can follow your friends, favorite celebrities, brands and bloggers on this app. I checked this app which is relatively new. Not much feeds from other users available. The real fun will begin only once your set of friends create an account on this app and start using it regularly.  4. Flipboard/Magzter (Read fashion articles): Yes! With a bit of customization you can follow and get feeds from Vogue India, Harper’s Bazar, W Magazine, Glamour, etc. You can get street style, celebrity style and other popular feeds right into your smart phone. It’s for those who are hooked on to reading fashion magazines and are always on the lookout for what’s new and trending from the editor’s table. Unfortunately, not many Indian magazines feeds are available with this app. Yet, the interface is beautiful, user-friendly and easy to read. Magzter app gets you access to free copies of Noblesse India issues which is a glossy fashion and lifestyle magazine. (True at the time of publishing this article.) You can download the soft copy of the magazine on your android device and read it at leisure. 5. Miss India app (know your beauty queens and beauty pageants): Get latest updates gossips news features and photos of your favourite Miss India’s on the go. Also get access to information on prestigious international beauty pageants like Miss Universe, Miss Asia Pacific, etc. Even you can vote for your favourite contestants during Miss India competition. Browse through photos, watch videos, even you can apply for the next pageant through this app. It’s incredible that such information is accessible at your fingertips. All those dreaming to become the next ‘Miss India’ will find this app very handy. 6. Mydressing: (Create personal lookbook with existing wardrobe or new additions). So you never knew that your grey T-shirt from Zara would look great with your red cotton pencil skirt you bought from Linking Road. Yes, it’s a discovery after a year of having purchased those things. It happens to many of us. But what if we had the option of mixing and matching clothes virtually, creating looks and instant references for future? I know it will be a blessing not to struggle early morning while rushing to office if we know in advance, what we would like to wear to office. With this app you can cut out the clothes (jacket, tee, dresses, etc.) from an image and put them on a look board along with accessories, makeup, shoes, etc. for quick reference, next time you are going out.  I am waiting for an app like Snapette or Pose to be launched in India listing Indian brands and stores. It uses GPS info to help you discover what’s out there in the stores around you. Also, you can get a real-time view of what millions of other fashionistas are finding stylish in major cities. For style inspiration from major fashion bloggers across the country, I am waiting for Stylepile to create an Android app which will be a hit with Indian fashion enthusiasts.  Many designers like Rajesh Pratap Singh, Pia Pauro, Payal Pratap, Gauri & Nainika and Anupama Dayal have already launched their own apps in the Android market. The users are able to preview the collections at the comfort of their own smart phone.  After smart phones and useful apps, the face of fashion is certainly going to change in India. In this age of artificial beauty and heavily photoshopped images, freckles are seen as unpleasant marks on the skin; even treated like a skin disease. These are predominantly found on the face and can very well damage a person’s confidence. Numerous skin creams, laser treatments, etc. are being prescribed to treat them. Alas, everyone wants a porcelain clear skin. In reality, these are brown flat spots on the skin, genetic in nature and can happen to any fair skinned person from any race. The formation of freckles is triggered by exposure to sunlight. Exposure to UV-B radiation activates melanocytes to increase melanin production, which can cause freckles to become darker and more visible. Upon exposure to the sun, freckles will reappear if they have been altered with creams or lasers and not protected from the sun, but do fade with age in some cases. So, to conclude it is best if freckles are embraced like beauty spots and skin should be managed for overall health. Many Hollywood and Bollywood beauties and super models have freckles and they live with it in harmony. Julia Roberts, Megan Fox, Gisele Bundchen, Kate Moss, Lucy Liu, Bar Rafaeli, Julianne Moore, Sienna Miller, Lindsay Lohan, Jennifer Lawrence and many others from Hollywood have freckles and they are completely comfortable sporting it. Kareena Kapoor, Rani Mukherjee, Genelia D’Souza, Vidya Balan, Kangna Ranut and many other Bollywood actresses have accepted them as an extension of their personality. Few have more freckles than others but that doesn’t stop them from putting their best face forward. These are all A-listers and red-carpet regulars so we mortals should be ok with having a mark or two on our skin, isn’t it? I did want to try out Photo-facial to get rid of my freckles which is supposedly the best treatment for the brown spots. Many home-remedies suggest applying lime juice on the affected area to lighten the marks. These treatments do lighten the spots but freckles do not go away completely. And there is always a chance for them to reappear if the skin is exposed to direct sunlight. If you are still upset with your freckles, you can always hide them under good makeup. When tattoos can be concealed with good make-up, why not freckles. Try a heavy base foundation and a good concealer to camouflage them. Embrace your freckles if you can. It is ok to be speckled! In this age of artificial beauty and heavily photoshopped images, freckles are seen as unpleasant marks on the skin; even treated like a skin disease. These are predominantly found on the face and can very well damage a person’s confidence. Numerous skin creams, laser treatments, etc. are being prescribed to treat them. Alas, everyone wants a porcelain clear skin. In reality, these are brown flat spots on the skin, genetic in nature and can happen to any fair skinned person from any race. The formation of freckles is triggered by exposure to sunlight. Exposure to UV-B radiation activates melanocytes to increase melanin production, which can cause freckles to become darker and more visible. Upon exposure to the sun, freckles will reappear if they have been altered with creams or lasers and not protected from the sun, but do fade with age in some cases. So, to conclude it is best if freckles are embraced like beauty spots and skin should be managed for overall health. Many Hollywood and Bollywood beauties and super models have freckles and they live with it in harmony. Julia Roberts, Megan Fox, Gisele Bundchen, Kate Moss, Lucy Liu, Bar Rafaeli, Julianne Moore, Sienna Miller, Lindsay Lohan, Jennifer Lawrence and many others from Hollywood have freckles and they are completely comfortable sporting it. Kareena Kapoor, Rani Mukherjee, Genelia D’Souza, Vidya Balan, Kangna Ranut and many other Bollywood actresses have accepted them as an extension of their personality. Few have more freckles than others but that doesn’t stop them from putting their best face forward. These are all A-listers and red-carpet regulars so we mortals should be ok with having a mark or two on our skin, isn’t it? I did want to try out Photo-facial to get rid of my freckles which is supposedly the best treatment for the brown spots. Many home-remedies suggest applying lime juice on the affected area to lighten the marks. These treatments do lighten the spots but freckles do not go away completely. And there is always a chance for them to reappear if the skin is exposed to direct sunlight. If you are still upset with your freckles, you can always hide them under good makeup. Remember the last time you took your reluctant toddler to a parlor for a haircut and came out all bruised, deranged and completely exhausted with managing a wailing (shrieking, actually) child who refused to part with their locks. Phew! The aftermath of the exercise is either, an absurd haircut or a very high BP (the dread of scissors snipping the skin instead of hair on a protesting toddler kills you completely). Most of the times, the stylists refuse to touch hair of such young clients. Of course, it isn’t easy dealing with them. (Ask us parents!) And a few, whom they dare service cry after the haircut, stating it is not in style. And we adults look at them helplessly; completely clueless about what exactly is in style. So, to take care of the needs of these style conscious little munchkins, a dedicated kid’s salon has opened in Bandra West. It is called Starfish Kids Salon and is a brainchild of Marya Lanewala and Preeti Harkare. (God bless these angels!) Mumbaigloss decided to talk to these ladies to decode what exactly Starfish offers for your kids.  MG: How was Starfish conceptualised? How big is the team?  StarF: We were pretty unhappy when it came to getting salon service for our kids. Most of the salons across the city do not take young clients seriously. We spoke to several moms across Mumbai and other cities if they felt the same. We identified that there was certainly a need gap in the area of providing good quality salon services to children of all age groups. We can tell you that each one of the moms said that they would be keen to take their kids to a child friendly salon. Also, we did a good research to know exactly what was missing and from their Starfish was born. A lot of insights have also been gathered from within the family; my three year old daughter and our nephews and nieces were consulted about what they would like in a salon when we were planning the design and experience! We manage the salon and have 4 trained and experienced staff managing the services in our first salon.  MG: That’s impressive and a very new concept indeed. But is it difficult managing the prime clients, i.e. kids? Is it more time consuming than the regular clients?   StarF: It is not as difficult as one thinks. What works for us is that we have created an environment that is very child friendly i.e. bright and cheerful, with toys and other distractions. One of the very important factors has been that we identified our staff very carefully who could patiently deal with young children. It was important that they all like children as it automatically makes a warm and inviting place. We have trained them in interacting with children. Our head stylist, Dilshad, is well experienced and has been a hair stylist for children for over 10 years.   MG: Sounds good. What services are offered for kids in Starfish other than haircut/hairstyle?  StarF: We provide the entire range of salon services; in addition to haircuts. We do party styles for girls (curling, blow dry. crimping), oil massage and hair wash, hair braiding with/without accessories, mani and pedi for kids as well as nail art. We also have select services for mothers like blow dry, hair wash, mani, pedi and nail art, etc. Our belief is that kids should feel happy and engaged at Starfish Kids Salon rather than just coming for a service. We also have special offerings like ‘My haircut certificate’ for first haircuts and mundans or specially designed gift vouchers. Our basic services like trims start at Rs.350 for both boys and girls. The prices vary between Rs.450-500 for more advanced cuts and razor styles. Our other nail and styling services for kids and mothers are priced between Rs. 400 and upwards. We also have specialised services like Mundans, prices for which vary depending on whether it is done at salon or at home.  MG: Excellent! Mundans are not worrisome anymore. What are the latest trends in kid’s styles?   StarF: We get a lot of requests for Mohawks from boys. Now that the summer holidays have started, hairstyles are also getting more adventurous and fun, with requests for razor styles like spider webs, angry birds and other funky designs. Girls are also very adventurous and most of them are happy to go short for the summer. The graduating bob is the most loved currently. For party styles, we get a lot of requests for different braids and cute hair accessories.  MG: Do you organise salon parties for kids? What all is included?   StarF: Yes, we offer salon parties and playdates. Parents can chose from a variety of options. For girls there is hair styling to nail art or mani and pedi. For boys parents can opt for razor styles, gel styling, hand and feet clean up. The cost is between Rs. 600 to 900 per person depending on the services chosen (food not included). Thank you Marya and Preeti for giving us a peek into Starfish Kids Salon! I am sure many moms are relieved that now the haircutting for their kids is not going to be a hair-raising event for them. Starfish sounds like fun. If you are in and around Bandra, I would definitely suggest a visit to Starfish Kids Salon with your kids. All the kids are treated to special Starfish cookies and they can play in the waiting area with toys till their turn comes. My LO loved the pink Mini mouse chair and was happy to sit on it for a change. The staff is also very helpful. For more information, call 022 2642 3093. Mondays closed. We at Mumbaigloss have been harping about the latest trends for some time now. Lakme Fashion Week followed by Wills Lifestyle India Fashion week happened back to back at Mumbai and Delhi. And these two giants of the Indian fashion scene threw in some major style overhaul. Bigger and bolder was the norm. Even accessories were seen chunkier (not heavier). Let us list a few trending accessories style from WIFW so that next time you go shopping, you know what to pick. Tribal print clutch and handcuff  Not only tribal print dresses, even tribal print accessories made a mark at WIFW. Woven fabrics like jute were combined with bright tribal print lace to create an outstanding piece. Matching hand cuff also added to the creativity. This is a brilliant concept and can be easily adapted into everyday wear. Chunky metallic handcuff  I know a few would feel that such looks will only look good in mythological melodramas, but if worn aesthetically it will add the glam quotient to any evening wear. Especially, during summers, when tank tops and sleeveless becomes the ritual; this accessory will make a statement and will add the drama required to your simple cotton dress or ensemble. Chunky metallic neck collar  Neck collars have been much in fashion last year. But an ethnic chunky twist to the somber peter-pan collars or stone cut-outs is definitely eye-catching. This will add the edginess to a plain spaghetti strap top or ganjee when worn with a floor length skirt. Chunky jeweled head wear  Add florals and some pearls and some sequins and some….and the list is never ending. The underline is –chunkier the headwear, the better it is. It should be next to a princess’s tiara. The best way to carry off this look is to keep rest of the accessories understated. Chunky chaand balis  Deepika Padukone did make chaand balis fashionable again with her Raam Leela get-up last year. But little did we know that chaand balis can equally up the style quotient in western wear as well. Next time, try a chaand bali with your evening gown. Indo-western fusion is hot in this season. Metallic clutches  Looks like metallic clutches will never go out of fashion. Chunky ethnic metallic clutches which you kept aside after your wedding can be easily teamed with denim shirts and skinny jeans. Hope this list will help you next time you go accessories shopping. Reigning trend is Indo-Western fusion. Let us know which accessories did you like? We at Mumbaigloss have been harping about the latest trends for some time now. Lakme Fashion Week followed by Wills Lifestyle India Fashion week happened back to back at Mumbai and Delhi. And these two giants of the Indian fashion scene threw in some major style overhaul. Bigger and bolder was the norm. Even accessories were seen chunkier (not heavier). Let us list a few trending accessories style from WIFW so that next time you go shopping, you know what to pick. Tribal print clutch and handcuff  Not only tribal print dresses, even tribal print accessories made a mark at WIFW. Woven fabrics like jute were combined with bright tribal print lace to create an outstanding piece. Matching hand cuff also added to the creativity. This is a brilliant concept and can be easily adapted into everyday wear. Chunky metallic handcuff  I know a few would feel that such looks will only look good in mythological melodramas, but if worn aesthetically it will add the glam quotient to any evening wear. Especially, during summers, when tank tops and sleeveless becomes the ritual; this accessory will make a statement and will add the drama required to your simple cotton dress or ensemble. Chunky metallic neck collar  Neck collars have been much in fashion last year. But an ethnic chunky twist to the somber peter-pan collars or stone cut-outs is definitely eye-catching. This will add the edginess to a plain spaghetti strap top or ganjee when worn with a floor length skirt. Chunky jeweled head wear  Add florals and some pearls and some sequins and some….and the list is never ending. The underline is –chunkier the headwear, the better it is. It should be next to a princess’s tiara. The best way to carry off this look is to keep rest of the accessories understated. Chunky chaand balis  Deepika Padukone did make chaand balis fashionable again with her Raam Leela get-up last year. But little did we know that chaand balis can equally up the style quotient in western wear as well. Next time, try a chaand bali with your evening gown. Indo-western fusion is hot in this season. Reigning trend is Indo-Western fusion. Let us know which accessories did you like? Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week concluded on March 30. Delhi fashion circle got a chunk of the latest fashion trends in the form of various accessories, makeup, colors, silhouettes, prints, details, etc. during this event. We at Mumbaigloss, decided to put together five most trending makeup looks from this fashion week which you can use in your everyday makeup wear. Blue & Black lipstick  After Rihanna sported a dark blue lipstick a couple of months back, it has become a style statement for fashionistas world over. Similar trend was seen at WIFW where models used navy, deep maroon, black lipstick to create an impactful look. This look can be easily adapted to your regular style. You can wear navy or black lipstick with a pair of denims as well an evening dress. The only catch is that the over-all look should suggest hip and cool. Just ensure that your eyes stay as natural as possible so avoid using dark eye-shadows. Dark lipstick looks good with bold and pronounced eye brow. To create this look, just prep your skin with a foundation or BB cream of your choice. Fill the brows with brow gel or eye pencil to make it look bold and pronounced. Use mascara to open up your eyes. Use a dark lip liner to line the lips and fill them with the navy or black color lipstick. This look goes best with matte finish lipstick. If you see extra cream or gloss on your lips, just bloat it with a napkin. Brands like Ana Sui, Channel, NYX and many others have black lipstick in their collection. White eye-liner  Lakme recently launched the Eyeconic White eye-liner. And with that putting white eye-liner has become the latest trend. Though, white eyeliner has been used by the make-up artists since ages to make the eyes look bigger and create a Bambi wide-eyed look. WIFW saw the perfect use of white eye-liner on the ramp where the models were trying to keep their makeup subtle. White eye-liner looks great with a winged black liner on the top lashes. Just use it like a regular kajal on the tear-line to open up the eyes and make them look fresh and bigger. Brands like NYX, Maybelline and others have white-eyeliner in their product line. White eye-liner is also used under the brow to highlight the brow bone. You can use it towards the inner corner of the eyes to make your eyes look wide-set. Metallic eye-shadows  Metallics ruled the ramp. Not only with the fabrics but with the makeup as well. Silver, gold, bronze, and several metallic hues were seen during the event. But what caught our attention was the use of metallic eye shadow used in the inner corners of the eyes along with very subtle makeup. Lips were kept natural, flesh pink or nude. The eyebrows were made bold and the eyes were highlighted with muted colors like browns, greys, etc. along with metallic eye-shadows. This look can be easily used in day-to-night makeup. Just add pearl finish or metal finish eye shadow to your day-time brown smokey eye and you are ready to rock the party. Metallic eye shadows easily glam up your face. As the other factors are kept natural, so it doesn’t look over-the-top. It can be used both during day-time and night makeup. Brands like Lakme, Stila, NYX, Bobby Brown and many others have metallic eyeshadows in their product line. Chin Bindi/stick-on tattoo  Chin stick-on tattoo is the next fashion statement from the tribal influenced makeup after temple bindis. This look is for the bold and fierce. It will look best with edgy accessories like ear cuffs, feather jewellery or tribal print dresses. The mantra to keep the look elegant is by keeping other makeup subtle. Again, bold brows add to the look but other makeup like eyes, lips, cheeks, etc. need to be kept understated. To make this look even more dramatic, put double winged eyeliner and you will certainly garner a lot of attention. To create a chin bindi without stick-on-tattoo, you can use liquid black eye pen. The same pen can be used to create winged eye-liner. Lakme, Revlon and many other brands have liquid pen eyeliner in their product line. Grey smokey eyes  Grey is the new black in the smokey eye world. If you are tired of sporting raccoon like eyes in black smokey eyes then go for subtle colors like greys and browns to create a smokey eye. It looks good with summer colors and light fabrics. Pink glossy lips look best with grey smokey eyes. You can wear this look in both night and day. So, we see that the makeup trend for summer is understated, soft, muted colors where eyebrows and eyes have been given a prominent space. Which trend you going to try out this summer? Lakme Fashion Week Summer Resort 2014 is over a week ago but we just can’t stop raving about the terrific trends it showcased this season. We have chosen the five most doable and stylish trends which can be easily adapted to your everyday wear. 1) Crop top Crop top has been here for a while and is certainly not going anywhere for sure. If you have a toned mid-riff, this is the perfect opportunity to show off. It is a summer trend which can be easily worn with a long skirt, palazzo pants and even skater skirts.   2) Print on print Print on print adds a lot of character to your ensemble. It is difficult to match it perfectly but once you know the trick about what works for you, you will score a 10 on 10 with the style brigade. Try and get the prints from the same color family. Fine prints and bold prints can be contrasted against each other.  Look for the colors which compliment you.   3) Art Who said you cannot wear art. Designers like Aarti Vijay Gupta, GeNext by INIFD, Love from India presented tops which had art print and looked striking and impressive. One of the best ways to showcase your love for culture and art is by wearing one on yourself. The bright prints are bold and do make a statement. Wear a short dress with art print or team it up with printed leggings to up your style quotient.   4) Trousers with high-low hem capes/tops Darling Lisa Haydon made high-low hem cape with hot denim pants look super cool in ‘Queen’. But it wasn’t the first time high-low hem made heads turn. It has been here for a while and looks like it’s going to grow stronger in the world of Indian fashion with each passing day. Especially, when ace designers like Suman Nathwani and Manish Malhotra showcased formal trousers with high-low hem capes/tops in their collection. It looks super chic and can be easily adopted in everyday wear.   5) Maang Tikka with western wear After Deepika Padukone appeared in a maang tikka along with a red-carpet gown in one of the recent award ceremonies, this has become a style statement for many. Even, Lakme Fashion Week saw many designers promoting this style. If you plan to wear one, try and choose delicate designs for day wear. Team it with skirts, trousers and anything you like. Bouffant hair styles help to carry these headgears better.     Lakme Fashion Week Summer Resort 2014 is over a week ago but we just can’t stop raving about the terrific trends it showcased this season. Rock-chic is for the bold, the care-free, the powerful, and the risk-taker. Lakme Fashion Week had us asking for more as we saw a lineup of jewelled studded bustiers, leather bustiers, leather gowns, leather gloves, androgynous silhouettes, gold chains and bling, ox blood color lipstick, smokey eyes, sheer and brocade fabric and other elements which made a lot of statement during the event and can inspire our day-to-day fashion choices. Mumbaigloss selected a few of the style inspirations which can help you to dress-up for an evening out or simply make a mark during the day. Beware! You might turn a lot of heads in your direction.  The first of the style-to-do list is jeweled bustier. Sourabh Kant Srivastava’s studded jeweled bustier or similar can be worn with palazzo pants or floor length skirts. You can keep it all black or try to break the monochrome with bold jeweled tones like ruby red, turquoise blue, amethyst purple, etc. It is a showstopper and will add up to your glam quotient effortlessly. The unique blend of brocade black skirt with black tank and leather accessories showcases a perfect fusion of east meets west. Tarun Tahiliani dress is ideal when you are going out with friends in the evening. The flowing skirt and tank top is airy enough for a summer evening yet is edgy. It can be easily manipulated into an ethnic wear if the tank top is replaced with a spaghetti strap blouse and matching odhni. Nikhil Thampi’s brown leather gown took the rock-chic to a new level. It spells poise, yet is fierce. It is perfect for an evening which needs you to be at the centre of all attention. The centre slit along with the jeweled waist belt glams up the rugged leather perfectly. Jabong Street Style’s skater dress is figure accentuating. If you have boyish body shape then use it to create a waist. The contrasting colorful sling bag and boots along with Goth makeup also add to the edginess of this ensemble. Androgynous fits as seen in Valliyan by Nitya Arora are other ways to create a rock-chic look. Add a little bling to glam up the garb. I personally liked the silver trousers and black tank top covered with a dress made from black sheer fabric as seen in Ashdeen collection. The concept is sexy and can be easily adapted to everyday fashion. It can be worn during the day as well as the evening. The sheer garment covering the basic trousers and top gives a structure to the apparel. It is edgy but very feminine. I know you all are rock stars in your own right but if ever you need some style inspiration from the ramp then this list will certainly help you choose the look perfect for you. Go rock it ladies! What are summers without whites in the wardrobe? In fact, a well-fitting white shirt is a wardrobe staple for many. And at Lakme Fashion Week Summer/Resort 2014 we found that white and off-white were used across various silhouettes, fabrics, cuts and designs. Designers like Shehlaa Khan, Kommal Sood, Shantanu and Nikhil, Anita Dongre, Neeta Lulla and many others used pure whites, creams and apple whites in their ensembles. Payal Khandwala used white blouses as a base for her color blocked Indian wear. White is a complete color in itself, its soothing, yet striking. Be it sheer fabric or cotton drapes, white is always beautiful. So, we at Mumbaigloss thought, why not list a few ways in which you can wear whites to your trendiest best. Choose apple white, pure white or creams as per your skin tone. Cool skin tones look good in pure white, whereas warm skin tones look good in creams. Whenever you want to buy a white dress put it next to your skin in natural day light. If you look washed out or dark then that white is not “right” for you! White eye pencil can be used to make your eyes look bigger. Just color the tear line of your eyes with white eye pencil and use a black mascara to see the magic unfold. Make-up can be either nude or dark depending on the occasion. Pink, peach look good on white during day time and so does red and coral in the evening. Use layering and draping to create multiple dimensions to your ensemble. A simple pair of jeans can look trendy with a white top if worn with complimenting capes, jackets or accessories. White skinny jeans can be worn with white drape top and a waist belt for a trendy look as seen on Kim Kardashian here. Wear white lace peplum top and a floor length white skirt to create a similar look as seen in the latest Shantanu and Nikhil collection. Latest trend spotted at LFW’ 14 is to add leg shaft in the Churidaar as seen in Ritika Mirchandani collection. It will look brilliant in monochrome designs, especially in black and whites as it beautifully adds dimensions to one color ensemble. In fact crop tops teamed with floor length skirt or palazzo pants are ideal for summers. See Dia Mirza in a crop top and floor length skirt in Anita Dongre creation. This can be easily emulated in real life fashion. Anti-fit large white tops over printed tights are another excellent wearable idea in the summers. So what are you waiting for? Go and grab your whites. After all it is time to chill in the trendiest of white dresses as summers are here. What are summers without whites in the wardrobe? Go and grab your whites. After all it is time to chill in the trendiest of white dresses as summers are here. Last week was pretty hectic for Mumbaigloss. Of course, we were busy with Lakme Fashion Week Summer/Resort 2014 at Grand Hyatt in Mumbai. What an amazing time we had hobnobbing with the fashion fraternity. The week presented few of the best designers from across the country and showcased their exclusive designs at the ramp. Reputed names like Rajesh Pratap Singh, Manish Malhotra, Neeta Lulla, Shantanu & Nikhil and many others participated over 6 days of fashion and glamour. New names like Mandira Bedi, Dorothy Perkins and others were also seen foraying into the Indian fashion scene. And what did we observe? Lots of fashion trends which can be easily emulated from ramp to reality. Though, I myself am a little averse to light reflecting elements but many designers freely used metallic colors, mirrors, sequence and shiny fabric at Lakme Fashion Week Summer/Resort 2014.  Gold and silver ruled the ramp. This trend might not be apt in the hot and humid summers of Mumbai; but if used moderately it might add to the glam appeal which is perfect for a party or any celebration. The idea is to “shine out” from the remaining crowd. Tastefully designed silver gown from Dorothy Perkins made Kangna Ranaut look like a yester year Hollywood star. She looked like a goddess scorching the ramp in her silver gown. Not only Dorothy Perkins, even renowned designer Rajesh Pratap Singh freely used silver and other metallic hues in his Grand Finale Collection. Even men were not spared from silver and gold fabrics in his collection. Kareena Kapoor had everyone spell bound with her oomph and seductive aura in the black and silver gown. It had a futuristic appeal. Rajesh Pratap Singh also used mirrors in this collection, a recent trend which was sported by Hollywood beauty Jennifer Lawrence at the Oscars. Payal Khandwala used silver arm band/cuff to add the zing to her color blocked Indian wear with white blouse. Mawi’s Indian Odyssey used golden fabric abundantly with tribal accessories giving the collection an enchanting feel.  Raven + Rose, Kommal Sood, Anushka Khanna, Papa Don’t Preach Me, Ashmita Marwa, Rajat Tangri and many others used the metallic colors lavishly. Now you must be wondering, how not to go overboard with metallic for your everyday dressing. If it’s a day wear, keep the metallic hues minimal. If the fabric has metallic colors, strictly keep your makeup simple. You can pair white and yellow (one of the popular trends at LFW) with a slim golden/silver waist belt and metallic strappy sandals. You can wear a metallic waist coat over your cotton white shirt to sport this trend. You can also add the glam factor by wearing a metallic head band with your day wear. For evening wear you can experiment with any metallic color, sequence work, crystal work, etc. as long as the fabric is flowy and natural. Don’t go for very heavy fabrics which might make you look like an astronaut.  Try and keep your accessories to the minimum. Makeup can be goth or nude as per the shade you are wearing. (Light shades like silver, pearly whites can opt for goth and dark shades can opt for nude makeup). So what do you think about the metallic trend as seen at Lakme Fashion Week Summer/Resort 2014? Will you try this on? More trend features coming your way. Stay tuned.   Last week was pretty hectic for Mumbaigloss. If the fabric has metallic colors, strictly keep your makeup simple. You can pair white and yellow (one of the popular trends at LFW) with a slim golden/silver waist belt and metallic strappy sandals. You can wear a metallic waist coat over your cotton white shirt to sport this trend. You can also add the glam factor by wearing a metallic head band with your day wear. For evening wear you can experiment with any metallic color, sequence work, crystal work, etc. as long as the fabric is flowy and natural. Don’t go for very heavy fabrics which might make you look like an astronaut.  Try and keep your accessories to the minimum. Makeup can be goth or nude as per the shade you are wearing. (Light shades like silver, pearly whites can opt for goth and dark shades can opt for nude makeup). So what do you think about the metallic trend as seen at Lakme Fashion Week Summer/Resort 2014? Will you try this on? More trend features coming your way. Stay tuned.   Cocktail rings are large, lavish and dramatic. They are a style statement and are very much in vogue. Not only diamonds, rubies, emeralds and sapphires are used to produce beautiful designs, even semi-precious stones like amethyst, jade, pearls and a lot many other gems are being used to create colorful patterns. The designs can range from classic to edgy. The idea is to garner maximum attention to your hands. The cocktail rings originated in America during the prohibition era; when drinking in public were illegal. Those who wanted to show their rebellion wore a large ring to signify that they were breaking the rules. Initially, it was meant to be costume jewelry but later it was manufactured in the main stream expensive jewelry segment as well. These days it’s a fashion statement and is popular with A-listers, especially in parties and soirees. Super-rich are wearing engagement rings which can easily pass-off as cocktail rings. But how do you choose a perfect cocktail ring? Choose stones as per your skin tone. People with warm skin tone should opt for green to yellow gems. People with cool skin tone should go for red to blue gems. And people with neutral skin tone should go for pale greens, pale blues, pinks, etc. Go for exclusive and edgy designs with multiple colors and textures. Go for floral, Victorian designs, multiple gem clusters or opt for a center large stone/gem with intricate details at the borders. Stones more than 3 carats should be good.  If you are on a budget, use synthetic or simulated gemstones. Try and order from online stores for maximum cost benefit. Just remember if you wear an oversized ring, go minimal on the other jewelry. The rule is one statement jewelry at a time. Slender and shapely fingers should opt for delicate and smaller designs in rings. Do not wear too many rings at one go. One piece other than your engagement band is more than enough. Thick and short fingers can opt for longer designs. This helps to elongate your fingers. Cocktail rings should be worn only in cocktail parties or dinner. Don’t wear them during the day. So what are you waiting for? Go and put your best finger forward with a perfect cocktail ring adorning it. Image via Anmol Jewellers and Mahesh Notandas jewellery. And I am so proud to say that today Shriya is showcasing her talent at an international arena like Nolcha Fashion Week in New York. Her luxury fashion brand ‘Maison de Papillon’ is going to adorn the catwalk in the “Ones to Watch” Runway Show at 5:30 pm. Designer Danielle Salinas is her partner who along with Shriya is going to officially launch their ‘Sleepwalker’ collection. Nolcha Fashion Week is a leading award winning event, held during New York Fashion Week, for independent fashion designers to showcase their collections to a global audience of press, retailers, stylists and industry influencers.  Born and raised in Nainital, Shriya made her acting debut appearing on popular national television shows like ‘Karam Apna Apna’ and ‘Kasauti Zindagi Ki’.  Shriya considers herself a “self- taught” artist; her paintings and artistic creations draw a lot of inspiration from her travels around the world and her fascination for the arts in its many forms. Her creativity came out in fashion designing once she started her further studies at the Parsons New School for Design in New York alongside Texas native Danielle. And they decided to create a luxury collection that is comfortable to sleep, travel, and live in, while never losing its unique, elegant style. Prior to Maison de Papillon, this concept didn’t exist in the market. Now, you can walk out of the door in your sleepwear without getting un-approving glances.  In the designer’s words, “Sleepwalker is a luxury hybrid collection of sleepwear, loungewear, travel wear, and ready to wear all in one. Each garment in this collection is designed for the elegant woman on the go who wants to add luxury, comfort and practicality to her wardrobe. Using the best fabrics and giving attention to every detail, Maison de Papillon is committed to providing looks of unparalleled quality. This line is versatile, luxurious, and most importantly comfortable without losing its sophisticated style & elegance.” That’s innovative!     For information regarding Maison de Papillon please visit www.maisondepapillon.com or www.facebook.com/maisondepapillon.com. If you like this article, don’t forget to like us on https://www.facebook.com/mumbaigloss Winters have not yet left us completely. And wearing full sleeve blouses shouldn’t be a problem, more so that they are pretty much in vogue. I went to a wedding last evening and saw the bride, brides-to-be friends, bridesmaids and relatives in full sleeve cholis. Not only with a saari, but also with a lehenga. I think Mandira Bedi can forget about the spaghetti strap blouses that made her a household sensation overnight. The current trend is to ditch the no sleeves or mega sleeves look and go for anything longer than the normal sleeve length. It’s prudent to cover yourself up when there is nip in the air. The longer the sleeve, the better it is! Even sleeves with churi (ruches) and sleeves with ruffles are doing the rounds. Is vintage fashion coming back? May be yes, the long sleeve blouses were very much part of yester years saari clad beauties who were regulars at the Derby. It was their wardrobe staple. Even the royal women used to cover themselves in long sleeve blouses. Velvet sleeves, net sleeves, cutouts, embellishments, you name it and you will find it in long sleeve choli choices. In India, it is a peak season for marriage and definitely long sleeve choli is much in demand. Even fashion designers have dabbled with various versions on the ramp. There is an old world charm to it. So, if you are a fan of retro fashion then you will certainly like this trend.  Now the question arises, how to wear one without any faux pas. Select the fabric as per the weather. If it’s too cold then go for velvet, and if it’s just breezy then go for blended silk. If the weather is going to be warm then choose net or cotton. Choose the design as per the occasion. If its party or marriage ceremony then opt for backless and string design otherwise keep it simple. Embellishments, sequins work, brocade work should be as per the occasion as well. Wear jewelry to compliment the overall ensemble. Very heavy jewelry in the arms is not recommended till the time you are not opting for three-fourth or half sleeve choli.  Bollywood is not far behind. In the recent past, many celebrities like Aishwarya Rai, Sri Devi, Bipasha Basu, etc. have been seen in long sleeve cholis. What is your take on this? Are you good to wear a long sleeve choli? Images via pinterest Whatever sparkles is not a diamond and whichever blue gem you see is not a Sapphire. Yes, it’s true that the allure of blue gems in contrast to white diamonds has been an all-time A-lister’s favorite. Sapphire being the more popular one! Not only have the celebrities, even the royalties been mesmerized with the Sapphire and Diamond combination since time immemorial. (Let’s not forget the royal engagement ring sported by Kate Middleton which used to adorn Princess Diana’s finger at one point of time.) Even our own Nizams have been a great admirer of blue stones. (The Nizam of Hyderabad owned a blue diamond called Wittelbachs diamond.)  Blue gem holds a lot of attention and beauty. But what if a blue gem reflects purple, brown and blue haze at different point of time, with different lights and at different time of the day? Sounds mystical and impossible, isn’t it? Yes, that’s possible with Tanzanite, a rare purplish blue gemstone which looks very neat and trendy with diamonds set in white gold. Tanzanite and diamond make a statement together.  Tanzanite is one the most revered, rare and coveted gemstones which fascinates with its unusual, captivating aura. Its deep blue with the slightly purple hue is one of the most exotic colors your eyes can witness. It is owned by the powerful and the beautiful. It was discovered 30 years ago in Mererani, Arusha, Tanzania by a local tailor. The mineral was named by Tiffany & Co. after Tanzania, the country in which it was discovered. Tiffany & Co were the first to bring this dazzling new gemstone to the market. In 2002, the American Gem Trade Association chose Tanzanite as a December birthstone, the first change to their birthstone list since 1912.  Many believe that a good Tanzanite has the powers to augment the power of Saturn leading to good fortune and wealth. Now, how do you ascertain a good Tanzanite? If your stone has color, brilliance and luster, particularly inward luster; is transparent without any impurities or cracks then it will undoubtedly get you the celestial powers as believed to be provided by this gemstone. If you are not impressed by its astrological powers, you can be rest assured that it will definitely make you look like a prize. With its different hues, it will surround you in a mystical aura. The best part is you can rock it over an LBD (Little Black Dress) as well as over your Kanjivarams without batting an eyelid. Tanzanite is certainly a versatile and beautiful gemstone and with diamonds, its beauty is accentuated manifolds.  Image courtesy Anmol Jewellers from their ‘Allure of Tanzanite’ collection. Yes, that’s possible with Tanzanite, a rare purplish blue gemstone which looks very neat and trendy with diamonds set in white gold. Tanzanite and diamond make a statement together.  Tanzanite is one the most revered, rare and coveted gemstones which fascinates with its unusual, captivating aura. Its deep blue with the slightly purple hue is one of the most exotic colors your eyes can witness. It is owned by the powerful and the beautiful. It was discovered 30 years ago in Mererani, Arusha, Tanzania by a local tailor. The mineral was named by Tiffany & Co. after Tanzania, the country in which it was discovered. Tiffany & Co were the first to bring this dazzling new gemstone to the market. In 2002, the American Gem Trade Association chose Tanzanite as a December birthstone, the first change to their birthstone list since 1912.  Many believe that a good Tanzanite has the powers to augment the power of Saturn leading to good fortune and wealth. Now, how do you ascertain a good Tanzanite? If your stone has color, brilliance and luster, particularly inward luster; is transparent without any impurities or cracks then it will undoubtedly get you the celestial powers as believed to be provided by this gemstone. If you are not impressed by its astrological powers, you can be rest assured that it will definitely make you look like a prize. With its different hues, it will surround you in a mystical aura. The best part is you can rock it over an LBD (Little Black Dress) as well as over your Kanjivarams without batting an eyelid. Tanzanite is certainly a versatile and beautiful gemstone and with diamonds, its beauty is accentuated manifolds.  Image courtesy Anmol Jewellers from their ‘Allure of Tanzanite’ collection. Also, featuring ring by Pure Gold Jewellers. For more information, contact Anmol Jewellers.  Whatever sparkles is not a diamond and whichever blue gem you see is not a Sapphire. (Let’s not forget the royal engagement ring sported by Kate Middleton which used to adorn Princess Diana’s finger at one point of time.) Even our own Nizams have been a great admirer of blue stones. Also, featuring ring by Pure Gold Jewellers. For more information, contact Anmol Jewellers.   Gifting season has not yet left us. December month brings on the shopping and gifting spree, thanks to Christmas and New Year. And, these days everyone looks for gifts that can be customized to add that personal touch. While, searching for such options I came across Shoe-U. Owned by 21 year old Stefan Fernandes, Shoe-U transforms your plain canvas shoes or sports shoes into a piece of art. Hand painted Converse shoes are a rage abroad. Now, it is gathering the status of a style statement in our very own Mumbai campus. If you are crazy about Garfield, get a customized Garfield design hand painted on your shoes, if your niece loves Transformers; get an autobot like Bumblebee hand painted on her little sneakers. If you like celtic tattoos, get them on your shoes too. And the list goes on. Run your imagination wild and get that design you have always wanted, hand painted on your shoes. Or if you simply want to give your old shoes a makeover, join the workshops conducted by Stephan and learn to bring your design ideas to life with colourful fabric paints. Stephan has been creating hand painted shoes from the past 2 years. He is still a student and pursuing his further studies. He loves art. For him, painting shoes is a stress buster. Initially, his family was a bit doubtful about his business venture but with his success he has proven that art can be a good business opportunity too. So, how did Stephan start with this creative venture? Let’s find out from Stephan: MG:  How did you come up with the idea of creating customized hand painted shoes? Which shoes can you customize? SF: The idea for this venture was actually an inspiration I drew from my friend who was part of a shoe painting workshop during a college fest we visited in Goa. When I saw the shoes she had worked upon, I knew for sure that this is a way of showcasing my creativity as well as my love for art. I get orders for canvas shoes but I also work on converse, DC shoes, etc. MG: Till now how many shoes have been ordered? Who are your clients? What is the price? SF: I’ve sold 70+ orders so far and still working on a few right now. My clients vary from time to time but mainly these are college students or older. The prices of these shoes are quite reasonable i.e. Rs. 900 (for canvas shoes inclusive of courier delivery) and the prices of the shoes increase depending on the urgency or a type of shoe (other than canvas shoes). I discuss the order with the client, ask details about their shoe size, shoe type and quality and the design they have in mind and eventually start my designing work.  MG: What is your educational background? Are you happy being an entrepreneur? Do you enjoy your work? SF: I’m a BA graduate from St. Xavier’s College and studying MA at Mumbai University right now. Yes, I’m happy being an entrepreneur and I really enjoy my work because I love painting and this sometimes acts like a stress buster. MG:  Recently, you did a workshop at St Xavier’s college? How was the response? What did the students gain from this workshop? SF: I did a workshop at St. Xavier’s college recently, which was actually my first. It was a special moment for me because I was asked to conduct a workshop at a place where this venture began and took shape. The response was surprisingly good. Around 20 students were present for the workshop. They got a chance to experience what I do for a living and they really seemed to enjoy the workshop. I helped them whenever they were unsure about their designs and gave them tips to paint something that they will be comfortable wearing. I was surprised to see a variety of artwork made by them.  MG:  What are your growth plans? Can you do bulk orders? SF: Yes, I can surely work on bulk orders but the order should be placed at least a couple of weeks or more in advance. I do plan to expand this venture by taking orders from people living in other cities. Once that works out, I will try to expand it further. A website is going to be launched soon. I am trying to spread the word by sponsoring a few events or college festivals. My venture is still young and gradually making a mark. I feel it will be a while for it to take off on a national level. Hoping for the best! MG: Any message for the readers SF: The only message I can give is that ‘never be afraid to follow your dreams and do something you love’. Also, do visit my facebook page i.e Shoe-U and The Artisans (my other venture where you can order customized hand painted mugs, T shirts, home décor and other gift items).  If you are looking for customized gifts on a budget, contact Stefan. I am sure he will have an answer to your woes. Images via Stephan Fernandes and pininterest  Gifting season has not yet left us. Images via Stephan Fernandes and pininterest This week Mumbai is witnessing art in many forms with GoodHomes for Art week 2013. MumbaiGloss decided to celebrate art in its own way. It decided to showcase the affinity between fashion and art through the works of Sumer Verma, who is a fashion and a wildlife photographer. Sumer was a diving instructor on the exotic islets of Kadmat and Bangaram, in Lakshadweep before he decided to fiddle with the shutterbox. While teaching people to dive, he also started making underwater wildlife documentaries and taking photographs of the colourful world beneath the blue. Gradually, his work expanded to fashion and fine art. He began experimenting with the interesting effects of light moving from the medium of air into that of water, its still glass-like reflective qualities and its playful bubbles to bring out colours in fabrics, the sparkle in jewelry and the grace in the contours of a human body. He has shot editorials for Vogue and Condenast Traveller, advertisements for Channel V and wildlife videography for Dusty Foot Productions, amongst many other illustrious clients. His work is available as prints and stock images, and he also specializes in editorials, advertisements and film shoots. Let us see his illustrious work in this photofeature. I am sure those who love fashion will be enthralled to no-limits knowing the possibilities of capturing glamour and beauty under water.                    This week Mumbai is witnessing art in many forms with GoodHomes for Art week 2013. I am sure those who love fashion will be enthralled to no-limits knowing the possibilities of capturing glamour and beauty under water.                    Recently, I came across a free copy of Noblesse India, a luxury and lifestyle magazine and saw stunning photographs of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. I was fairly surprised and absolutely happy to see her return to her glam avatar. She is rumored to be making her comeback with director Karan Malhotra’s upcoming movie Shuddi, opposite Hrithik Roshan (Facebook/World Of Aish).  I know the entire media is writing about her Noblesse photo shoot where she is wearing designer gowns and was decked up by celebrity stylist Daniel Bauer. But I was looking beyond this glamour and appreciating her strong resolution to come back and conquer again.  Since her pregnancy in 2011, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan has received a lot of flak because of her de-glammed appearances, her weight gain and her fashion choices. Many wrote her off saying that her career is over with her pregnancy. (She opted out of the much publicized and ambitious project, Madhur Bhandarkar’s ‘Heroine’). The rumours of her leaving the industry did a few rounds but died down as she kept on making rave appearances in Cannes and other international film festivals, representing India and ensuring that Bollywood shined at the foreign shores.  What I want to talk about today is that how this beauty queen turned a girl-next-door when marrying her love as well as when she delivered a baby. She took her time to tend to the critical years of her daughter Aaradhya Bachchan, when as an infant a child needs the mother the most. She was a hands-down-mummy and would spend maximum time with her child even with her occasional star appearances both in India and abroad. These initial years of bonding prove to be a lifelong boost for a child’s emotional and psychological health. She would travel with the baby to all her international visits and commitments.  She is herself very much attached to her mother Vrinda Rai and wants to develop a similar relationship with her daughter. I am sure all the mums and daughters can relate to it. She drew a lot of criticism when she didn’t lose the post pregnancy weight for a long-long time (read 1-2 years). Of course, other celebrity mums were dropping pounds as soon as they were out of the labour room. I am happy to say that at least one celebrity mother decided to set realistic standards for her fans and followers. Her kaftan dresses, anarkalis and brocade sarees didn’t go well with the fashion police. Yet she decided to appear in dresses she was comfortable in and could carry off with elegance. Aishwarya took time to get back to shape and focus on other important aspects of her life which were on priority at that point of time. And now she is back with a bang. Look at the 40 year old sizzle on the sands of The Leela, Goa. She can still give the latest glam brigade a run for their money. In one of her interviews with a magazine she claims that she has a sweet tooth and starts her day with a cupcake. (If you would like to believe it, looking at her svelte figure now). And she doesn’t workout regularly. Now that makes her mortal, like you and me, who gives in to her sins and indulges in the good things of life. I am eager to see her performance in her next release.  I want to see how a mother bounces back to her natural self and gets on with the grind. It will be an inspiration to all the new mothers who beat themselves up on issues related to career and weight gain. Aishwarya has set an example on how to prioritise in life.  She might be a star to the world, she might be the career woman, the Bollywood diva, but her child and family command equal attention from her.  And that what makes her so awe inspiring.  Images: Pininterest, Noblesse India Recently, I came across a free copy of Noblesse India, a luxury and lifestyle magazine and saw stunning photographs of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. I was fairly surprised and absolutely happy to see her return to her glam avatar. She is rumored to be making her comeback with director Karan Malhotra’s upcoming movie Shuddi, opposite Hrithik Roshan (Facebook/World Of Aish).  I know the entire media is writing about her Noblesse photo shoot where she is wearing designer gowns and was decked up by celebrity stylist Daniel Bauer. But I was looking beyond this glamour and appreciating her strong resolution to come back and conquer again.  Since her pregnancy in 2011, Aishwarya Rai Bachchan has received a lot of flak because of her de-glammed appearances, her weight gain and her fashion choices. Many wrote her off saying that her career is over with her pregnancy. (She opted out of the much publicized and ambitious project, Madhur Bhandarkar’s ‘Heroine’). The rumours of her leaving the industry did a few rounds but died down as she kept on making rave appearances in Cannes and other international film festivals, representing India and ensuring that Bollywood shined at the foreign shores.  What I want to talk about today is that how this beauty queen turned a girl-next-door when marrying her love as well as when she delivered a baby. She took her time to tend to the critical years of her daughter Aaradhya Bachchan, when as an infant a child needs the mother the most. She was a hands-down-mummy and would spend maximum time with her child even with her occasional star appearances both in India and abroad. These initial years of bonding prove to be a lifelong boost for a child’s emotional and psychological health. She would travel with the baby to all her international visits and commitments.  She is herself very much attached to her mother Vrinda Rai and wants to develop a similar relationship with her daughter. I am sure all the mums and daughters can relate to it. She drew a lot of criticism when she didn’t lose the post pregnancy weight for a long-long time (read 1-2 years). Of course, other celebrity mums were dropping pounds as soon as they were out of the labour room. I am happy to say that at least one celebrity mother decided to set realistic standards for her fans and followers. Her kaftan dresses, anarkalis and brocade sarees didn’t go well with the fashion police. Yet she decided to appear in dresses she was comfortable in and could carry off with elegance. Aishwarya took time to get back to shape and focus on other important aspects of her life which were on priority at that point of time. And now she is back with a bang.
