Images: Pininterest, Noblesse India Indian jewellery is not restricted to only Indian shores anymore. It has gathered momentum in many parts of the world. Thanks to Hollywood celebrities like Heather Graham, Adele, Jennifer Lopez and many others, a Mughal set is not only donned over a saree or lehenga but also over western outfits and evening gowns. The latest craze in the circle being jadau jewellery with enamel work (Meenakari). We spoke to Manubhai Jewellers director Samir Sagar who gave us insight on this trend and what it takes to preserve such precious and beautiful jewellery for the coming generations. MG: How is Jadau and enamel confluence trending the market? MJ: Jadau Jewellery has become a rage among the brides-to–be these days.  Being an ancient technique of manufacturing jewellery, jadau gives a heritage look once worn, especially on the wedding day. The design in each jewellery piece is inspired by the regality of the Mughal dynasty, teamed with gemstones such as rubies, emeralds and kundan stones. So when a bride wears such a piece on her wedding outfit, it makes her feel like a princess. The art of Jadau uses much colour through the entire jewellery piece. To add grandeur and colour to the set, the back of the jewellery pieces are enamelled. The art of enamelling requires a keen eye for detailing and a high degree of skill on part of the artisan. Ruby and emerald pota’s are the most common gemstones used to add the red and green colour in jadau jewellery. Precious stones such as uncut diamonds (polki / vilandi), blue and pink sapphires along with pearls are also another special feature in jadau jewellery. Especially in long kantha’s (string work), the entire neckpiece is made up of pearls with gold beads. Several brides today are opting for the traditional jadau jewellery with an antique finish, because it adds glamour to the occasion. Each jewellery piece feels like a heritage piece handed down from generations, selected from the treasure of a Queen.  Heavy Chokers have become very popular among brides. Chokers with an antique polish and engraving on the gold piece combined with south sea pearl drop have become a huge favourite.  Most brides like to team this up with a long kantha in pearls and beads designed in the Rajwada style.   Paisley motifs complete with red and white kundan stones is in trend currently.  The innovation in design with various motif’s and craftsmanship renders a distinct contemporary feel to each piece.  Today a bride can not only adorn a jadau jewellery piece on a lehenga, but also carry it off well on a gown at an evening party. MG: Thank you for letting us know about the trends. As you mentioned that these designs can also be worn over a gown at an evening party, can you please elaborate which designs can be worn with western wear? Are these popular in the west?  MJ: Contemporary jewellery designs are inspired by the ancient art, but does not emulate it entirely. The jewellery piece today has more intricate craftsmanship with delicate engraving. The main or centre pendant would have a traditional look but the remaining portion of the piece would have a more modern and artistic look. Filigree is another addition within the design giving a contemporary look to the piece and it looks understated yet elegant with a gown. Using geometric designs in sets is another way to create a modern twist. Designers work towards balancing the design; crafting a contemporary piece while maintaining the aesthetics of traditions. The west in fact has always been smitten by Indian jewellery and is more openly adorning them now.  MG: Of course. Recently, we have seen a string of Hollywood celebrities appearing in traditional Indian jewellery on western outfits. But as these look very expernsive, can you throw some light on its price? MJ: Jewellery pieces range from as low as 80 gms to 100 gms in light weight pieces and sometimes even go upto 900 gms in an elaborate neckpiece. So price of the jewellery too ranges from 1 Lac to 20 Lacs. However, the price fluctuations are based mainly on the karigari or labour charge. Each piece is handmade with every karigar laboriously working on each element of the entire jewellery piece and design. MG: Yes! I agree that a piece of jewellery is a work of art. And the efforts put into creating one are the decisive factors related to its cost, not to mention quality of stones used, gold quality, etc. How can we preserve jadau and enamel jewellery? What are tips to keep jadau enamel jewellry safe from damage so that it can be passed on to generations? MJ: Jewellery usually gathers a film from lotions, powders, soaps and natural skin oils which erode the sheen of the metal. Sometimes even the chemicals present in our atmosphere or while we travel can oxidize the metal, depending on the purity of gold. Cleaning Jewellery: Using harsh chemicals to clean gold will reduce its luster; making it look worn out. Instead use a mild detergent at home, (dishwashing powder) with warm water in a bowl. Dip the jewellery for a minute and gently brush the same with a soft bristled tooth brush in the direction of the setting. For Kundan jewellery, avoid contact with any form of water, damp cloth, any other liquid or soapy solution. In case the kundan jewellery turns dull or acquires any blemishes, use a basic eraser (used for erasing pencil marks).  If the darkened portion isn’t getting cleaned, take it to your nearest jeweller for a safe remedy. Maintaining Jewellery: MG: Thank you for you valueable inputs on the upkeep of jadau and enamel jewellery. Can you talk a bit about the latest collection from Manubhai Jewellers? MJ: Manubhai Jewellers has launched its bridal collection, Utsavi which includes a variety of range from elaborate chokers and multiple lined kanthas to medium sized necklaces and large pendant sets. It has also put on view heavy kundan and jadau jewellery. It is a blend of contemporary and traditional designs. The collection influenced from the royal courts of the Mughal Era. To know more about this collection, please visit www.manubhai.in. You can also follow us on Facebook for regular updates. So, what are you waiting for brides-to-be. Manubhai jewellers have two branches (Borivali & Ghatkopar) where you can check out their latest collection. Chokers with an antique polish and engraving on the gold piece combined with south sea pearl drop have become a huge favourite.  Most brides like to team this up with a long kantha in pearls and beads designed in the Rajwada style.   Paisley motifs complete with red and white kundan stones is in trend currently.  The innovation in design with various motif’s and craftsmanship renders a distinct contemporary feel to each piece.  Today a bride can not only adorn a jadau jewellery piece on a lehenga, but also carry it off well on a gown at an evening party. MG: Thank you for letting us know about the trends. As you mentioned that these designs can also be worn over a gown at an evening party, can you please elaborate which designs can be worn with western wear? Are these popular in the west?  MJ: Contemporary jewellery designs are inspired by the ancient art, but does not emulate it entirely. The jewellery piece today has more intricate craftsmanship with delicate engraving. The main or centre pendant would have a traditional look but the remaining portion of the piece would have a more modern and artistic look. Filigree is another addition within the design giving a contemporary look to the piece and it looks understated yet elegant with a gown. Using geometric designs in sets is another way to create a modern twist. Designers work towards balancing the design; crafting a contemporary piece while maintaining the aesthetics of traditions. The west in fact has always been smitten by Indian jewellery and is more openly adorning them now.  MG: Of course. Recently, we have seen a string of Hollywood celebrities appearing in traditional Indian jewellery on western outfits. But as these look very expernsive, can you throw some light on its price? MJ: Jewellery pieces range from as low as 80 gms to 100 gms in light weight pieces and sometimes even go upto 900 gms in an elaborate neckpiece. So price of the jewellery too ranges from 1 Lac to 20 Lacs. However, the price fluctuations are based mainly on the karigari or labour charge. Each piece is handmade with every karigar laboriously working on each element of the entire jewellery piece and design. MG: Yes! I agree that a piece of jewellery is a work of art. And the efforts put into creating one are the decisive factors related to its cost, not to mention quality of stones used, gold quality, etc. How can we preserve jadau and enamel jewellery? What are tips to keep jadau enamel jewellry safe from damage so that it can be passed on to generations? MJ: Jewellery usually gathers a film from lotions, powders, soaps and natural skin oils which erode the sheen of the metal. Sometimes even the chemicals present in our atmosphere or while we travel can oxidize the metal, depending on the purity of gold. Cleaning Jewellery: Using harsh chemicals to clean gold will reduce its luster; making it look worn out. Instead use a mild detergent at home, (dishwashing powder) with warm water in a bowl. Dip the jewellery for a minute and gently brush the same with a soft bristled tooth brush in the direction of the setting. For Kundan jewellery, avoid contact with any form of water, damp cloth, any other liquid or soapy solution. In case the kundan jewellery turns dull or acquires any blemishes, use a basic eraser (used for erasing pencil marks).  If the darkened portion isn’t getting cleaned, take it to your nearest jeweller for a safe remedy. Maintaining Jewellery: MG: Thank you for you valueable inputs on the upkeep of jadau and enamel jewellery. Can you talk a bit about the latest collection from Manubhai Jewellers? MJ: Manubhai Jewellers has launched its bridal collection, Utsavi which includes a variety of range from elaborate chokers and multiple lined kanthas to medium sized necklaces and large pendant sets. It has also put on view heavy kundan and jadau jewellery. It is a blend of contemporary and traditional designs. The collection influenced from the royal courts of the Mughal Era. To know more about this collection, please visit www.manubhai.in. You can also follow us on Facebook for regular updates. So, what are you waiting for brides-to-be. Manubhai jewellers have two branches (Borivali & Ghatkopar) where you can check out their latest collection. Use these tips to keep your jewellery shining and intact for many many years.   The much anticipated debut show of “Let’s Design” winners Josh Goraya and Vedangi Agarwal took place at Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week, on October 13. Cotton Council International (CCI) is a non-profit trade organization devoted to the promotion of cotton in India. The design competition “Let’s Design” by Cotton Council International (CCI) has become India’s premier design competition and brought cotton to the forefront of fashion.  Absolute devotion to tailoring, cut, detail and the fabric were the hallmarks of Josh Goraya’s collection, Alter Nature. The collection uses the full spectrum of cotton fabrics, batiste, organdy, poplin, cambric, voile, sateen, muslin, flannel, chambray, denim, twill, jersey, and canvas. The palette is understated but by no means dull. He combines tones of navy, off-white and grey to create vibrant mosaics with unexpected pops of red.  “Encouragement when you’re emerging onto the fashion scene is vital for new designers. Working with CCI and FDCI has provided us with a fantastic platform to showcase our collections at India Fashion Week and to incorporate high quality cottons into our collections,” said Josh.  The soft hues of the rising sun give a warm glow to the collection Aurora by Vedangi Agarwal. Vedangi elevates cotton to glamorous heights using cotton sateen, matty, twill and cambric to create stunning drapes, with delicate gold embroidery to add elegance and sophistication. Each garment challenges the notion that cotton is ordinary.  “Naturally I’ve always been aware of cotton but working with CCI has opened my eyes to the breadth of possibilities in cotton which has allowed me to grow as a designer,” added Vedangi.  Renowned designer and “Let’s Design” judge Rina Dhaka congratulated the pair on their debut collections. “They should both be very proud,” Rina said. “Both collections showed immense talent and maturity, and a deep understanding of the possibilities of cotton.”  Sunil Sethi, President of FDCI(Fashion Design Council of India) said, “It was a proud moment for FDCI to see the young designers’ passion for cotton translate to design. Josh and Vedangi showed us how the humble cotton can be made fashionable.”   The much anticipated debut show of “Let’s Design” winners Josh Goraya and Vedangi Agarwal took place at Wills Lifestyle India Fashion Week, on October 13. Celebrating 15 years, Bridal Asia 2013 is once again ready to set the tone of bridal trends with new innovations and styles.   Divya Gurwara, CEO – Bridal Asia and restaurateur Aashita Relan hosted  a champagne party at The Royal China for a select gathering to  present the bridal collection by Siddartha Tytler  and jewellery by Purnima Jhunjhunwala. Sidhartha Tytler: Trained in fashion from the National Institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi and the prestigious Fashion Institute of Technology in New York City, Siddartha  launched his label in  2002. Novel silhouettes, innovative structural elements, new fangled patterns, wearability and originality are the essential elements in every creation at Siddartha Tytler studio.  For Bridal Asia 2013 collection, the designer has played around and used various innovative techniques of surface texturing using the traditional dori embroidery. Evolving the trademark appliqué work into embroidery, the Sicilian lace collection bejeweled with lace and sequins is the highlight of the collection. The prints are inspired by the 16th century Italian motifs and the colour palette moves around rich jeweled colours – teals, fuschias, orange, turquoise, olives… and the silhouettes vary from anarkali, lehengas, pre-pleated saree gowns, gowns, skirts and jackets for women and sherwani, kurtas and waistcoats for men. Purnima Jhunjhunwala: Purnima Jhunjhunwala’s collection includes handcrafted polki, jadau, and diamond jewelry – handcrafted and beautifully designed. Each piece of her jadau and polki collection is designed to perfection and reflects a classic yet contemporary look. The high quality diamond jewelry is a blend of elegance and modernity. She enhances a bride with her exquisite bridal collection as well as makes a women feel special on any occasion with her wide range of jewellery and range earrings.  Purnima Jhunjhunwala has a loyal discerning clientele and has received an overwhelming response in adorning the beautiful women of today who are looking for something just perfect for them. Designer Anjalee and Arjun Kapoor showcased their latest collection ‘Jamawar Aria’ at Eros Hilton, New Delhi on 2nd September. Anjalee & Arjun has dressed up celebrities like Katrina Kaif, Deepika Padukone, Bipasha Basu, Anushka Sharma, Chitrangda Singh, Kangana Ranaut, Hema Malini and many more. The showstopper for ‘Jamawar Aria’ was Bipasha Basu, who looked stunning in a dress created with Swarovski elements.    The collection is reminiscent of the Mughal era and has a strong Jamawar influence in the collection with an essence of the Renaissance era. It has two distinct lines; opulent Victorian construction gowns and extravagant Jamawar inspired bridal couture. The dresses have a lot of texture and ruffles. Mermaid fits along with the use of peplum to construct the gowns give a fairytale like appeal. The dresses have fitted torsos which flair out at the bottom into voluminous layers. Embellished with Swarovski elements the embroidery interspersed with delicate roses and over the top use of feathers lends a very glamorous look to the ensemble.  For Bridal couture ethnicity has been fused with modern design to lure a modern bride. Deep colours like burgundy, tomato red and hot pink dominate this line. Generous use of fine fabrics such as the rich velvet and Benarasi as the base for lehengas and anarkali suits has been made.  Intense threadwork embroidery has been meticulously worked upon. Tulle and cancan is extravagantly used as an accent, to create a lacy, floating look. Enchanting cocktail sarees using shimmer chiffon captures attention. Bejewelled borders with Renaissance motifs all over as the jaal of the saree has been used. Extremely detailed bejewelled bustiers have been coordinated with the sarees and lehengas. For the new generation groom, floor length sherwanis which reek of flamboyance have been specially crafted. The silhouette is traditionally Mughal. Indo-western jackets with interesting cuts find a place in the men’s collection which can be worn stylishly over a kurta payjama and donned over pants as well.  Very interesting laser cut metallic belts have been introduced in the Jamawar Aria collection. These belts make a statement and are instant eye catchers. These can be worn on sarees or with Kaftans and western garments.Anjalee & Arjun Kapoor has studios in New Delhi, Mumbai, Hong Kong and Dubai. O Box – 3969   As the festival season is approaching, it is quite obvious that we are trying to find ways to add bling to our lives. A little bling does no harm and what better way to do that than rock a pair of beautiful diamond earrings. But this becomes tricky if you have short hair. Not all earrings look good on women who sport a short haircut. Let us discuss a few options available in earrings for women with short hair. Short haircuts like pixie, bob, crop, etc. is sported by many working ladies. Even home makers prefer a chic short cut over long dos. So, when you are trying to choose an investment like a pair of diamond earring, on a short haircut which will highlight what you wear on your ears; keep in mind the following factors: 1. Face shape – A small face doesn’t look good in large OTT designs so go for delicate pair of earrings. If you have a round face, try to get ring shape or long chandelier shaped earrings rather than studs. If your face is on the fuller side, very delicate designs will be lost so go for designs like enamel and jadau or un cut diamonds, which will give a dimension to your face. If you have a very long face then go for mid length earrings rather than long chandelier shaped earrings. Make sure that the design is proportionate. 2. Skin tone – If you have a cool skin tone (pinkish to red) try to avoid rubies and garnets. Any red colour stone will make you look more flushed. Blue sapphires, purple amethyst will suit you better. Even emeralds will look good on you. Try to get white metal like white gold, platinum, silver, etc.  If you have a warm skin tone, then try to balance it with pearls and emeralds. Rubies will look excellent on you. Go for yellow metal. 3. Age – Very girly designs like florals, birds, stars and moons, etc. should be left for the younger women. Older women should go for either traditional or futuristic designs. 4. Type of occasion – If going to wedding or party go for heavy designs. If wearing as a day time or office wear accessory, keep it minimal. It’s a no brainer that with traditional wear, try to choose traditional designs and with western wear try to choose modern designs. All designs courtesy Zevadhi Jewels. Zevadhi looks to create a place of its own in the market for exquisite diamond and jadau pieces. Zevadhi continues the Moghul & Victorian tradition, adding the essence of modern design to a timeless art. Price range starts from 3 lac onward. The collection boasts of stunning interwoven metals for a structured and regal look. A modern-day twist to traditional Indian wear is the idea behind this new bridal line. It uses mesmerizing patterns and intricate artistry to create a style statement.  This season, Jade is also reimagining old favourites. Versatile gota patti has been recreated, with a strong focus on its texture to highlight ensembles. Married to lace, the result is dreamy and romantic – everything a bride aspires for! You can also see the creation of structured embossed motifs against strong colour backgrounds. You will also find designs in pop colour. Figure enhancing silhouettes coupled by traditional Indian hand-woven embroidery make this collection versatile in every way. The designs are chic and elegant, and lend sophistication with a hint of romance.  The Jade store succeeds at creating a realm of style and elegance, owing to the chic interiors of the store that is further enhanced with the Collections on display. Tel: + 91.22.23533635, Cell: +91.9833002000, email: jade@jadecouture.com   Jewellery designer Alpana Gujral will showcase her latest collection ‘The Golden 20’s’ at her Lajpat Nagar, Delhi, showroom on 16th and 17th September. To see Alpana Gujral jewellery collection, you can visit her showroom.  She has used intricate vintage designs on oxidized gold along with deft use of pearls, emeralds, rubies, enamel and diamonds. She has taken inspiration from the majestic grandeur of the Mughal Era, yet keeping in mind the modern day styles. Her collection includes both light weight and heavy jewellery. The designs have been crafted for both Indian and western ensembles; for day wear and evening wear.  Daughter of famous artist Satish Gujral, Alpana has creativity in her blood. And when you see her designs, it becomes so evident. Alpana’s discerning aesthetic values in patterns, forms and lines are because of her artistic upbringing. “The embodiment of affluence lies in quality not in flash”, says Alpana. Her designs spell class. They are simple yet elegant. They are intricate, subdued, yet beautiful.  Alpana started as an interior designer with special focus on furniture design, but today with sheer hardwork and uniqueness she has made her mark as a jewellery designer. But how did she transition from one art to another. She says, “Creativity knows no bounds. It is fluid. It is seamless. It has the intensity to flow from one realm to another with innate ease. I have always been interested in creating new stuff and looking beyond the predictable. In fact, for years I had been designing and making jewellery for the family and for close friends. So if you take that into account, my foray into jewellery designing isn’t new; it’s just that now I have been focusing more on it. Now there’s market for it. Most jewellery outlets provide traditional sort of jewellery and people have had enough of it.”  Alpana’s unconventional style is evident in her jewellery design as well.  The theme of the 20’s collection is yin and yang; to get the opposites together. The opposite components have been meticulously composed to come together in harmony.  Be it rings, chandelier earrings, bracelets; you will see a harmony of elements. You can visit her exhibition on 16th and 17th September at: 16 Feroze Gandhi Road, Lajpat Nagar – 3, New Delhi For more information, contact – 09810043776 Jewellery designer Alpana Gujral will showcase her latest collection ‘The Golden 20’s’ at her Lajpat Nagar, Delhi, showroom on 16th and 17th September. There were many other celebrities who walked the ramp like Chitrangada Singh, Madhur Bhandarkar, Juhi Chawla, etc. Bridal glamour was the flavor of the season where polki, kundan and gold jewellery encrusted with diamonds, rubies, emeralds and pearls were put on the show. Here is a glimpse of IIJW 2013.    Sonam Kapoor looked like a diva and Chitrangada Singh left viewers asking for more. Sonam Kapoor wore traditional jewellery encrusted with uncut diamonds and pearls, while Chitrangada donned another versatile piece of jadau jewellery which was going well with her western ensemble. Juhi Chawla represented the tradional house of mangalsutras. The show also witnessed many new and upcoming talents. These jewellery designers were sponsored by well-known companies. This was the fourth edition of IIJW in Mumbai and it has already established itself as one of the most sought after events of the year for the gems and jewellery fraternity.   The glittery saga of IIJW 2013, Mumbai edition, came to an end on August 10. Most celebrated brands of the jewellery industry participated at IIJW, displaying their best of creations which bedazzled every one. The venue was Hotel Grand Hyatt Ballroom. Sonam Kapoor, brand ambassador of India International Jewellery Week was present on the ramp to add the glamour quotient. The models walked the ramp on the beats of Bollywood numbers sung by Shalmali Kholgade. JJ Valya, the celebrated designer was present at the event to coordinate the fashion show. There were many other celebrities who walked the ramp like Chitrangada Singh, Madhur Bhandarkar, Juhi Chawla, etc. Bridal glamour was the flavor of the season where polki, kundan and gold jewellery encrusted with diamonds, rubies, emeralds and pearls were put on the show. The location is brilliant and the facilities are no less than a five star. I felt that it was pleasant in every way. Especially, I loved their Seven Colours Spa, which was a relaxing and an invigorating experience. It is located next to the hotel. It can be visited by the main road as well as through an inside passage joining the two properties. The spa in veranda grand baie hotel & spa is open from morning 9 am to evening 8 pm. Services are available only through prior reservation. It is open for anybody above 16 years of age. They have a special kids spa programme as well. (Kids need spas…????) Its a non-smoking area. All in all, the entrance is beautifully decorated and the reception area is kept perfumed with exotic oils. Seven Colours spa at veranda grand baie hotel & spa treatments are inspired by the wisdom of ancient natural healing techniques. Benefits of botanical, aromatherapy and energetic pressure application are applied to create harmony for an individual’s mind and body. The services provided by the spa includes, facials, mini facials, hena application, body treatments and wraps, manicure, pedicure, nail art, etc. I went to the spa as per my appointment and was greeted by the hostess. She explained me the procedure and asked me to change into the spa dress. She gave me a refreshing drink and asked me to relax for 20-30 minutes at the spa Jacuzzi. I decided to get an Aqua massage. After 30 minutes, the attendant guided me to the treatment room which was kept ready for the service. The technician explained me the entire process and how it will help me to feel relaxed. It was for half an hour but the spray like jets of water massaged my skin thoroughly giving it an instant glow and hydration. The treatment room was warm and inviting, incensed and dimly lit, perfect for rejuvenation of mind and body. I came out all refreshed. It was priced at Rs 900 Mauritian rupee. After the treatment, I requested them to give me a tour of the spa, which they readily obliged. I saw couple treatment rooms and other treatment rooms which were located upstairs near to the changing room. All I could think was OH just missed out on this relaxing rendezvous. I also wanted to try their signature hot stone massage for 90 minutes which was priced at Rs 2700. Unfortunately, didn’t have enough time at hand. If you ask my verdict, I would say take out time for it. How often do you get pampered at an exotic locale? And was she a head turner with her impeccable mannerisms, charm and presence? Indeed, she was a stunner. Her ensemble, jewellery, make-up, everything complimented her gorgeous persona. At 37, she can put many a new actresses to shame with her beauty and grace. She drew a lot of flak in the past for her sudden weight gain and the link-ups which were never established. People started speculating that motherhood (2 adopted daughters Renee and Alisah) must have taken its toll on this tall and dusky beauty. People started speculating about her marriage. But she put all these rumors behind as she announced her comeback to the tinsel town yesterday. She said that she took a sabbatical to take care of her baby Alisah and has been preparing for a comeback. Though, she didn’t take any names and asked to wait for the producers to announce about her project. She has always been a non-conformist. Any other actress would have jumped to declare about her comeback project but she decided otherwise. As I discuss her non-conformist trait, how can I not talk about the adoptions she made at the young age of 24. She made adoptions at a time when being a single mum was an alien idea in India. She adopted Renee, a girl child, at 24 when other women are just dreaming about their knight in the shining armour. She adopted Alisah three years back. She dotes on her daughters Renee (11) and Alisah (3). She is a hands down mum when at home with her children and tells them that they may not be born from her womb but are born from her heart.  She started her career at the age of 18 when girls are still discussing college admissions. She believes in all the religions. She is as firm in her hindu belief of Ma Durga, as she is comfortable taking her children to a church or celebrating Eid with her family. Her favourite phrase happens to be ‘Insha allah’, which many staunch hindu believers frown upon. (She is a Bengali hindu by birth). She dated men who have been younger to her or older to her but who could stay put with her intelligence and grace. Recently, a friend commented that Aishwarya Rai became a star, a wife and a mother, why couldn’t Sushmita do it? Again, a comparison which they both cannot escape, being contemporaries! To which, I said, may be the men get intimidated with her towering personality. Indian men never like their wife to be at the helm of affairs. And Sushmita is never politically correct; she says what she believes in. She does what seems right, maybe which is outright eccentric. She chose movies in her initial days which appealed to her senses and not to her bank balance. As her father has served Indian Air Force at a much senior position and her mother happens to be a jewellery designer, she had enough to fall back upon. Moreover, Indians prefer a fair-skin light-eyed actress over a dark, tall and unconventional beauty, a bias which is deep-rooted in their minds and our society in general. Has she looked any less beautiful? No, she has looked ethereal in ‘Main Hoon Na’ in a sexy-saari clad – school teacher avatar, or as gypsy queen dancing to the tunes of ‘Mehboob Mere’ in Fiza or as a negative lead in Biwi no 1. I cannot forget her portrayal of a dedicated IPS officer in Samay where I saw her play tough on the goons as well as soft for her child. She has a good comic timing which was evident in ‘Kyunki Main Jhooth Nahin Bolta’, ‘Maine Pyar Kyon Kiya’, ‘Do not Disturb’ and the latest ‘No Problem’. Now, she grooms contestants for ‘Miss Universe’ title through ‘I Am She’ a company she visualized and formed in the recent past. Being India’s first Miss Universe has given her the required edge and appeal to choose the right candidates who can represent India in the international arena. I wish her all the best for her venture and the coming release in the future. She might not be the reigning queen of Bollywood but she definitely rules many a hearts. How often do you wish that someone would guide you if you should choose the shades of red or brown hair colour for your precious mane? You do not wish to commit a mistake of colouring your hair in the wrong shade and then repent. If you do commit a mistake of colouring hair in the wrong shade then you might have to colour your hair in quick succession with another colour to correct the look. This might also damage the hair texture. So let our experts guide you in your choice of hair colour in either red or brown. The belief: Shades of brown are better for Indian skin tone. The facts: A few years back only shades of brown and natural black were available in the market when it came to hair dyes and colours. People opted for henna to dye their grey hair. But with gradual exposure to products available in the international market and the introduction of various international brands in the Indian market, now we have a lot more options available for colouring hair. With the recent trends in fashion, a rainbow of colours have been introduced by different brands. Few opt for streaks and many for global colouring. People are ready to experiment with their hair colour by applying shades of blonde and platinum colours as well. But the favourite remains browns and reds. Let us find out which is better for Indian skin tone. Berzin Irani, renowned independent make up artist suggests: Shades of brown are better for Indian skin. Most of the Indians have a wheatish to dusky skin tone. Brown colour goes with any skin tone. Shades of red usually look good with lighter or pale skin tone. ………………………………………………………………………………………… Shirin Merchant, owner of Kut and Make salon, Mumbai suggests: Red and Brown both look good on Indian skin. But dusky skin can carry off red very well. Mahagony, Auburn, Deep red, there are many shades available in the market which look good on both wheatish and duskier skin. The verdict: Our experts have different opinions regarding the hair colour in red and brown. Indian skin tone can carry off both red and brown shades with elan. Just choose the shades wisely. Make sure that if you are too dusky do not go for very light brown and if you are too pale or fair, do not go for the darkest brown. Hair colour should be chosen keeping in mind your original hair. The hair colour should be only three shades lighter or darker than the original hair colour.
